recipes.description: Designed with kids in mind, this recipe puts a new spin on snack time. Try different vegetables or dried fruit for a different looking "butterfly."
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean celery with vegetable brush under cool running water.
Cut celery in half cross wise.
Fill center of each celery stick with one tablespoon of peanut butter.
This is the body of the butterfly Add two pretzels to form the butterfly’s wings.
Use extra pretzel pieces for antenna and raisins for decoration.
recipes.name: Butterfly Bite
recipes.recipe_by: The Texas A&M University System — Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These scones taste better than those from your local bakery -- and you do not even have to change out of your pajamas! You can make many variations of this recipe by adding different fruits, sprinkling cinnamon prior to baking, or trying whole wheat flour. Get creative and have fun.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Combine the flours, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a medium bowl.
Mix well.
Add raisins and mix lightly.
In a small bowl, combine melted butter and buttermilk.
Add liquid ingredients to flour mixture; mix gently.
Spoon dough into 9 equal mounds on a greased baking sheet.
Bake until well browned, 18 to 20 minutes.
Serve hot or at room temperature.
Best eaten the same day you bake them.
recipes.name: Buttermilk Scones
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Butternut Squash & Apple Soup
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a stockpot, add the onion, celery, carrot, and oil.
Sauté for about 5 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Add water, squash, apple, and bouillon to the pot.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, then cover, and simmer.
Continue cooking for 30 minutes or until the squash and carrots are soft.
Carefully transfer soup to a food processor or blender and puree.
NOTE: If an immersion blender is available, the soup does not need to be transferred.
Add seasonings.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Butternut Squash & Apple Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Virginia Cooperative Extension - www.eatsmartmovemoreva.org

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tired of tomatoes? Try topping pasta with creamy low-fat ricotta and sweet roasted butternut squash for a weeknight dinner that’s anything but ordinary.

ingredients.name: dried whole wheat shell pasta
ingredients.raw: 4 ounces dried whole wheat shell pasta

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F.
Cut butternut squash in half and scoop out the seeds.
Place the cut sides down in a large baking dish and fill with 1/4 inch water.
Bake butternut squash until tender (about 45 minutes).
Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
While the squash bakes, bring a pot of water to a boil.
Add pasta and cook until just tender.
Drain and set aside.
Reduce oven to 375 °F.
From the butternut squash, measure out 2 cups of the squash.
Place in a food processor along the shallot, sage, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pulse until squash is smooth.
Add in low-sodium vegetable broth and pulse until well-combined.
In a small baking dish, place a third of the squash purée in the bottom.
Add half the noodles, followed by the low-fat ricotta.
Top the ricotta with the next third of the sauce, then the remaining noodles.
Finish with remaining sauce and low-fat shredded mozzarella.
Bake pasta for 25 minutes at 375 °F.
Cheese should be browned.
Remove and serve warm.
recipes.name: Butternut Squash Pasta Bake
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the Grain Foods Foundation, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Butternut squash and black beans make a hearty side dish that is delicious and full of fiber and protein.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the squash in the microwave on high heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
This will soften the skin.
Carefully peel the squash with a vegetable peeler or small knife.
Cut the squash into 1/2 inch cubes.
Peel and chop the onion.
In a large pan, heat the oil.
Add the onion, garlic powder, and squash.
Cook for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add vinegar and water.
Cook on low heat until the squash is tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the beans and oregano.
Cook until the beans are heated through.
recipes.name: Butternut Squash with Black Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Minute rice and canned tomatoes combined with cabbage make this a quick, easy, and healthy recipe.

ingredients.name: cabbage head
ingredients.note: small to medium, chopped in bite-sized pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a skillet with onion and garlic.
Drain off any fat.
Place meat in a large pot and add water, tomatoes, tomato sauce (or juice), and cabbage.
Cook until cabbage is almost tender.
Add minute rice and cook five minutes longer.
Serve.
recipes.name: Cabbage Roll Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Dill, mustard, and lemon juice give this crunchy salad a zesty flavor. Make the dressing ahead to save time later.

ingredients.name: dried dill
ingredients.note: may also use dried basil or parsley

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and prepare vegetables for chopping.
Use a cheese grater or slice all vegetables thinly with a sharp knife.
Put in a large bowl.
Add dill and/or other herbs to taste.
Mix mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, and sugar in a small bowl.
Blend well.
Add to vegetables.
Mix well.
Keep in refrigerator until ready to eat.
recipes.name: Cabbage Salad
recipes.recipe_by: From the Farm to the Table — University of Connecticut Cooperative Extension — Hispanic Health Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This one-skillet vegetable stir-fry has cabbage, green peppers, onion, and garlic; is quick to make; and is full of flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash green peppers and cabbage before chopping.
Heat oil in a large skillet.
Add onions, peppers, cabbage, and garlic to skillet and cook over medium heat until vegetables are tender.
Add soy sauce and stir until sauce boils.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Cabbage Stir-Fry
recipes.notes: Two cloves garlic and 2 tablespoons reduced-sodium soy sauce used in nutrition analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up this hot drink by adding cinnamon.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat reconstituted non-fat dried milk in saucepan until warm; do not boil.
Add coffee and hot chocolate mix.
Stir well and heat to desired temperature.
Divide coffee mixture between two mugs.
Top with non-fat whipped topping and cinnamon, if desired.
recipes.name: Cafe Mocha
recipes.notes: You can substitute 1 cup skim milk for the reconstituted nonfat dried milk.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA’S Collection of Nonfat Dry Milk (NDM) Recipes — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Catfish is breaded with cornmeal and baked in the oven for a healthier way to add flavor and crunch!

ingredients.name: lemon pepper seasoning
ingredients.raw: 3/4 teaspoon lemon pepper seasoning, no salt added

ingredients.name: catfish fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound catfish fillets, frozen, thawed, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Combine cornmeal and spices in a shallow dish.
Dip each fillet in the cornmeal mixture.
Coat evenly.
Place fillets on a baking sheet.
Bake 20–25 minutes flipping catfish halfway through.
Catfish should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145 F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
recipes.name: Cajun Catfish
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Chickasaw Nation Nutrition Services, Get Fresh Initiative

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh avocado doubles for dressing and filling complementing blueberries, carrots, arugula, and chicken in this appetizing summer wrap.

ingredients.name: ripe avocado
ingredients.note: seeded, peeled, and cut into chunks

instructions: Mash half the avocado chunks with yogurt and lime juice in a medium bowl.
Add remaining filling ingredients, including the rest of the avocado chunks; mix gently.
Top each tortilla with 1/4 of filling mixture.
Roll tuck in ends.
Slice in half diagonally, securing with toothpicks, if needed.
recipes.name: California Avocado Super Summer Wrap
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this side dish for a Thanksgiving treat or anytime yams are in season.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cut yams in half and boil until tender, but firm (about 20 minutes).
When cool enough to handle, peel and slice into 1/4 inch thickness.
Combine sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and grated orange peel.
Place half of sliced yams in medium-sized casserole dish.
Sprinkle with spiced sugar mixture.
Dot with half the amount of margarine.
Add second layer of yams, using the rest of the ingredients in the order above.
Add orange juice.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Candied Yams
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cool down in the heat with this fruit cooler. Refreshing orange juice mixed with sweet cantaloupe creates the perfect, easy-to-make drink! You can even get creative and use any fruit you please!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut melon in half.
Scoop out seeds, remove rind, and discard.
Cut melon into 1-inch cubes.
In blender or food processor, blend melon cubes with 1/2 cup orange juice until smooth.
Pour purée into pitcher and stir in the remaining orange juice and the sugar.
Stir until sugar is dissolved.
Pour into glasses filled with crushed ice.
recipes.name: Cantaloupe Cooler
recipes.notes: For a new twist, try other melons or strawberries in place of the cantaloupe.
recipes.recipe_by: Celebrate Health with a Lowfat Fiesta — California Department of Health Services — ​​​​​California Project LEAN

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this sauce over fruit or frozen yogurt for a dessert or special snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Reconstitute non-fat dried milk with water.
Combine reconstituted milk and cornstarch in a small saucepan and mix until cornstarch is thoroughly dissolved.
Add the butter and brown sugar and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wire whisk until mixture thickens and comes to a boil.
Continue to boil 1 minute.
Remove pan from heat and stir in vanilla.
Serve warm over baked French toast, ice cream, or fruit.
recipes.name: Caramel Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: USDA’S Collection of Nonfat Dry Milk (NDM) Recipes — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A refreshing and delicious salad that includes tomatoes, oranges, beans, onions, and lettuce.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in large salad bowl.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to one hour.
recipes.name: Caribbean Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.
recipes.serving_size: 1 cup prepared bean salad, 1/4 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick one skillet casserole dish of beans, bell peppers, tomatoes, and oregano uses instant brown rice to reduce cooking time.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) black beans, low sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onion and green pepper in canola oil, in a large pan, until tender.
Do not brown.
Add tomatoes, beans (include liquid from both), oregano, and garlic powder.
Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice and cover.
Reduce heat to simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand for 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Caribbean Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Plantains, tomatoes, and onions come together to give this side dish a Caribbean flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse and pick through the beans.
Put the beans in a large pot and add 10 cups of water.
Place the pot in the refrigerator and allow the beans to soak overnight.
Cook the beans until they are soft.
Add more water as needed while the beans are cooking.
Add the plantains, tomato, pepper, onion, garlic, and salt.
Continue cooking at low heat until the plantains are soft. *Option: Serve with rice.
recipes.name: Caribbean Pink Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Carrots give this traditional oatmeal and raisin cookie a colorful and tasty twist.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large bowl, cream together margarine and honey.
Stir in carrots and egg whites.
Stir together flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, oatmeal and raisins.
Gradually stir flour-oatmeal mixture into creamed mixture, just until all flour is mixed.
Do not over mix.
Drop from teaspoon on greased baking sheet.
Flatten slightly and bake at 350 °F for 10 minutes, or until lightly browned.
recipes.name: Carrot Cookies
recipes.notes: Honey should not be fed to children under 1 year of age. Instead of honey, you can use 1 1/4 cups sugar mixed with 1/4 cup water.
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Futures — Virginia Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This easy and healthy side salad has a sweet and tangy flavor. Make it ahead of time and serve it chilled.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, thoroughly mix carrots, raisins, sugar, and lemon juice.
Serve chilled.
recipes.name: Carrot Raisin Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Cent$ible Nutrition Cook Book — University of Wyoming Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Each serving of this delicious and quick pasta dish provides 1 1/2 cups of veggies.

ingredients.name: olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a saucepan, cook the onion in the oil until soft but not brown.
Add the tomatoes, tomato juice, carrots, salt, pepper, and sugar.
Cover and cook over low heat for 5 minutes.
Remove the cover and cook over low heat, stirring often, for another 5 minutes, or until the carrots are tender and the tomatoes are cooked down to a sauce.
Stir in the parsley.
Mix the butter with the cooked macaroni.
Add the macaroni to the carrot mixture and stir together.
recipes.name: Carrots with Tomatoes and Macaroni
recipes.recipe_by: University of Rhode Island Cooperative Extension — Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chili and spice seasoning give this seafood stew a punch of flavor. Serve it with brown rice for added whole grains.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut potatoes into quarters.
In large pot, combine potatoes, tomatoes and their juice, onion, water, and garlic.
Bring to boil and reduce heat.
Cook covered over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Add cabbage and return to boil.
Reduce heat.
Cook covered for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cut fillets into 2-inch lengths.
Coat with Chili and Spice Seasoning .
Add fish to vegetables.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 5 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork.
Serve in soup dishes.
Garnish with sliced green onion, if desired.
Serve with scoop of hot cooked brown rice.
recipes.name: Catfish Stew and Rice
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Creamy cauliflower and low-fat cheese make a delicious sauce for this pasta dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Fill 1 pot with 6 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Once the water is boiling, add pasta and cook for 8 minutes.
Drain pasta and fill the same pot with 2 cups of water, bring to a boil.
Place the chopped cauliflower in the boiling water and cook until the florets are soft (about 4 minutes).
Drain cauliflower.
Placed the cooked cauliflower, 1/2 cup milk, and garlic salt in a blender and blend until smooth.
In a separate pot, heat oil.
Add the flour and whisk until the mixture is smooth.
Add 1 cup of milk and cook the mixture until it bubbles and thickens.
Add the cheese and cauliflower mixture and stir..
Remove from heat.
Add the pasta back into the sauce and serve.
recipes.name: Cauliflower Shells with Cheese
recipes.recipe_by: With Veggies, More Matters! — Michigan State University Extension - Midland County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Crunchy, sweet celery is a versatile snack food, just right for this flavorful spread. Filled with dried fruit and nuts, this enticing and quick low-fat spread can be made ahead or on the spot. You could also serve it on whole grain crackers as an appetizer.
instructions: Chop dried fruit and pecans.
Mix blue cheese, cream cheese, and yogurt with a fork or hand mixer until smooth.
Stir in chopped, dried fruit and pecans.
Refrigerate spread until ready for use.
Slice celery stalks into 3-4 inch sticks.
Fill celery pieces with spread.
recipes.name: Celery with Apricot Blue Cheese Spread
recipes.notes: Tips on how to select, store, and serve celery:
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Just four ingredients is all you need to make delicious flatbread at home! Serve with dip at your next gathering or as a side to dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the flour in a large mixing bowl.
Add water, oil, and salt.
Mix with fork and then with hands.
Keep mixing until you can make a ball.
Knead the dough for about 10 minutes.
Let rest for 30 minutes in the bowl, covered with a damp cloth.
Roll the ball into a 12-inch log and cut into 6 chunks.
Roll each chunk into a very thin pancake, about 7 inches in diameter.
Don't worry about making the dough into a perfect circle-just try to get it as thin as you can.
Heat a cast iron skillet (lightly greased) on medium-high heat.
Place one chapati in the skillet and cook for 30 seconds.
Use a spatula to lift bread.
When chapati gets brown spots and bubbles, flip it over and cook for another 30 seconds.
Wrap the cooked chapati in a cloth napkin while cooking the rest.
Eat them right away with a little butter or margarine, or use as scoops for eating other dishes.
recipes.name: Chapatis Flatbread
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book: Taste of the World — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a hearty vegetarian soup for a filling and healthy meal on a chilly night. If you have leftovers that have been properly handled, you can add ham, chicken, or other meat for more protein.

ingredients.name: cheddar or American cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup cheddar or American cheese, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine potatoes, carrots, celery, onion and seasonings in pan.
Add 1 cup water.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add corn and pepper.
Cook 5 more minutes or until vegetables are cooked.
Add milk and cheese.
Stir until cheese melts and chowder is heated through.
Do not boil.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Cheese and Corn Chowder
recipes.notes: To make a Ham, Cheese, and Corn Chowder: Add 1/2 cup cubed, cooked ham.
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These potatoes are light and fluffy on the inside and baked twice to give a crunchy crust.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Scrub the potatoes.
Put the potatoes in the oven.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes until tender.
Slice each potato in half lengthwise.
Use a spoon to scoop out the inside of each potato.
Leave about 1/2 inch of potato next to the skin.
Save the inside part of each potato in a small bowl.
Peel the onion.
Chop it to make 2 tablespoons chopped onion.
Put the cheese, milk, and onion in another small bowl.
Add the insides of the potatoes.
Mix with a fork until light and fluffy.
Divide this mix into 8 parts.
Put part of the mix inside each potato.
Sprinkle paprika over the potatoes.
Return to the oven for 5 minutes to reheat.
recipes.name: Cheese Stuffed Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bright layers of spaghetti sauce, cheese, and macaroni cook together for one hour in the oven to make a hot meal.

ingredients.name: jar (24 ounces) spaghetti sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 jar (24 ounces) spaghetti sauce, meatless, low-sodium

ingredients.name: mozzarella cheese
ingredients.raw: 4 ounces mozzarella cheese, part skim, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl combine sauce and water.
In another bowl combine cottage cheese, egg and oregano.
Grease 1 quart casserole.
Spoon in 1/3 sauce.
Layer with 1/2 cup macaroni, 1/2 cottage cheese mixture, 1/2 mozzarella cheese and 1/3 of the spaghetti sauce.
Repeat layers one more time.
Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in a 350 °F oven for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Cheese-A-Roni Bake
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A great recipe to use leftover chicken that has been properly handled. Combine with broccoli, cheese, onions, garlic, and brown rice to create a quick dinner!

ingredients.name: (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, reduced-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In large saucepan, bring water to boil.
Add rice, onion, and garlic.
Cook for about 30 minutes or until rice is soft.
While rice is cooking combine milk, soup, salt, and pepper, mix well.
When rice is done combine with milk mixture, chicken, and broccoli.
Mix well.
Grease 9x13 pan and pour mixture into pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 18 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for another 6 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Cheesy Chicken, Broccoli, and Rice Bake
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Smells of vanilla, cinnamon, and fruit will fill your home after baking these cherry puff pancakes. If you don’t like cherries, try using peaches, pears, or blueberries.

ingredients.name: halved
ingredients.note: pitted sweet cherries, fresh or frozen, thawed and drained
ingredients.raw: 2 cups halved, pitted sweet cherries, fresh or frozen, thawed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
In a medium bowl or blender, beat the eggs, milk, and vanilla together until well blended.
Mix the flour, sugar, and cinnamon together.
Add to the liquid ingredients and mix until there are no lumps.
Put margarine or butter in a 10- or 11-inch oven proof skillet or a 2 1/2- to 3-quart baking dish.
Place the skillet or dish in the hot oven until the margarine or butter is melted and bubbly.
Remove from the oven.
Quickly spread the cherries across the bottom of the hot skillet or dish.
Pour the batter over the cherries and sprinkle with almond slices, if using.
Return to the oven and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the edges are browned and the puffs in the middle are golden.
Cool slightly before cutting into 4 pieces.
The center puffs will flatten during cooling.
recipes.name: Cherry Puff Pancake
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A delicious fruit salad with an added twist of cherries and coconut flakes. You will feel like you are in a tropical paradise eating this salad.

ingredients.name: sweet cherries
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup sweet cherries, pitted and cut in half

ingredients.name: seedless green grapes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup seedless green grapes, cut in half

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix together the cut fruit.
Pour orange juice over fruit and stir in coconut, if desired.
recipes.name: Cherry, Melon, & Grape Salad
recipes.notes: Try using different types of melon or grapes.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero, Adapted from Cherry Salad — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple one-pot dinner mixes kidney beans and chicken in a savory tomato sauce.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse beans.
Crush garlic.
Dice onion.
Dice chicken thighs.
In large, pot, cook chicken until half done.
Add tomato sauce, vinegar, onion, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for about 30 to 40 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Add kidney beans and simmer for 5-10 more minutes.
recipes.name: Chicken and Beans
recipes.notes: Cider, white, and Japanese wine vinegars differ in flavor. Try other vegetables. Dry beans may be used. See package for cooking directions.
recipes.recipe_by: Lifeskills in Food Education, Food Skills Cookbook — University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use fresh-cooked chicken or leftovers that have been properly handled to save time in this baked casserole.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Melt margarine in large sauce pan.
Add flour to melted margarine and stir.
This will be lumpy.
Slowly add chicken broth to margarine/flour mixture.
Stir to remove lumps and thicken.
Add cheese and stir.
Add rice, broccoli, and chicken.
Stir.
Put in a casserole pan and bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
recipes.name: Chicken and Broccoli Bake
recipes.recipe_by: Supermarket Smarts: The 5 A Day Way — Produce for Better Health and Connecticut Departments of Public Health and Social Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A simple and delicious salad topped with almonds and dried cranberries for bursts of flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss chicken, cranberries, and almonds with dressing.
Serve on a mound of chopped lettuce.
recipes.name: Chicken and Cranberry Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Recipes for Less Familiar USDA Commodities Used by Household Programs — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this spin on an all-time favorite chicken and dumplings. This easy, one-pot meal can be made for a family or ready to serve a crowd.

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.raw: 1 cup celery, chopped, including some leaves

ingredients.name: chicken broth
ingredients.raw: 8 cups chicken broth, fat free, low sodium

ingredients.name: fresh spinach leaves
ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh spinach leaves, coarsely chopped

instructions: Heat oil in Dutch oven or soup kettle over medium-high heat.
Sauté carrot, onion and celery for 5 minutes; stir in broth, chicken, peppercorns, thyme, and bay leaves.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, partially covered for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, in small bowl, mix dumpling ingredients until well blended.
Drop small spoonsful of dumpling dough into simmering soup.
Cover soup and allow dumplings to cook for about 20 minutes (they will rise to the top of the soup as they cook).
Stir in spinach.
Remove bay leaves before serving soup.
recipes.name: Chicken and Dumpling Soup
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These easy dumplings only need 4 ingredients. Drop them into the hot chicken broth mixture and cook them for 15 minutes. What a simple and quick meal for a busy night.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix 2 tablespoons flour and water in a pan until smooth.
Slowly stir in broth.
Cook over medium heat until thickened.
Add chicken, salt (optional) and pepper.
Make Dumplings: Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl.
Stir in milk until dough forms.
Drop dumpling dough from a tablespoon onto gently boiling chicken mixture, making 4 dumplings.
Cover pan tightly and cook slowly for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
recipes.name: Chicken and Dumplings
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book, Adapted from recipe Easy Chicken and Dumplings — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This one skillet meal makes a quick, tasty, and healthy weeknight dinner.

ingredients.name: whole chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 whole chicken, cut up, skin removed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet heat oil over medium-high heat and brown chicken on both sides.
Add green pepper, onion, and garlic and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add tomato, chicken broth, bay leaf.
Add salt & pepper to taste.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add rice, stir well, cover and simmer for 20-30 minutes longer, or until all liquid has been absorbed and chicken is tender.
Add peas, cook until hot.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
recipes.name: Chicken and Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book: Taste of the World — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add your favorite veggies and brown rice to this yummy chicken soup for a warm meal on a cold night.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use leftover cooked chicken or cook enough chicken to make 1 cup of chicken pieces.
Place the cooked chicken in a large saucepan.
Add the broth and uncooked rice.
Cover the pan.
Bring the broth and rice to a boil.
Cover the pan and turn the heat to low.
Stir and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chopped onions, chopped vegetables, and seasonings.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
recipes.name: Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Chicken Soup Recipe: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This skillet dinner calls for cooked chicken. Use leftover chicken that has been properly handled or canned chicken to stretch your food dollars.

ingredients.name: (8 ounces) tomato sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce, low sodium

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cups cooked chicken breast, diced, skin and bone removed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet, sauté onions and green peppers in oil for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add tomato sauce and spices.
Heat through.
Add cooked rice and chicken.
Heat through.
recipes.name: Chicken and Spanish Rice
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Celery and apple give a delightful crunch to this easy to make sandwich filling.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except for bread together in a bowl.
Create 4 sandwiches on whole wheat bread.
recipes.name: Chicken Apple Salad Sandwich
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Broccoli brings brightness to this recipe, while the Basic Soup and Sauce Mix gives this recipe a rich and creamy flavor.

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.raw: 1 cup broccoli, fresh or frozen, chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook fettuccine according to package directions.
Add broccoli for the last 4 minutes of cooking time.
Drain.
Heat butter in skillet.
Add chicken and cook until browned, stirring often.
Combine sauce mix and water in saucepan.
Bring to a boil and cook until thick.
Add milk, cheese, pepper (if using), and fettuccine mixture and heat through.
Serve with additional Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Chicken Broccoli Alfredo
recipes.notes: Recipe for Basic Soup and Sauce Mix . 1 serving = 1/3 cup.
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This easy recipe features chicken cooked in a tomato base. It’s a classic favorite that is easy to make and full of flavor!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Put the chopped onion in a saucepan.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, garlic powder, oregano, and pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 3 minutes.
If needed, remove the chicken skin.
Add the chicken to the sauce pan and cover.
Cook over low heat for about 1 hour until the chicken is tender.
recipes.name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This chicken casserole is a simple, satisfying main dish for lunch or dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cook rotini or macaroni according to package directions.
Drain well.
In a large oven-safe dish, mix the chicken, tomato sauce, peas, and macaroni.
Add the 3 slices of cheese on top of the casserole.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Chicken Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This colorful chicken and pasta salad is served over lettuce or spinach to make a tasty lunch or dinner. Pick your favorite veggies to add to this salad.

ingredients.name: Romaine lettuce
ingredients.raw: 6 cups Romaine lettuce, washed and torn

ingredients.name: green peppers
ingredients.note: or a combination of bell peppers, celery, cauliflower florets, cucumber, carrots*

ingredients.name: Lite Italian Dressing
ingredients.note: about 1/2 of what the recipe makes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and cool.
Place 1 1/2 cups of the Romaine lettuce in each of 4 large bowls or plates.
Combine chopped vegetables, chicken, and pasta.
Add dressing; toss lightly to coat.
Divide evenly among the 4 bowls.
Top each serving with a few egg slices, if desired, and 1 tablespoon of the shredded cheese.
recipes.name: Chicken Club Salad
recipes.notes: *2 cups of green bell peppers were used for cost analysis and nutrition calculations.
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Better. Buy Better: Iowa State University Extension 2009 Calendar — Iowa State University Extension and Montana State University

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chili powder, cocoa, garlic powder, and peanut butter make a traditional Mexican chicken dish. Serve it with brown rice for a mid-week dinner.

ingredients.name: fryer chicken
ingredients.note: cut into pieces, skin and fat removed
ingredients.raw: 1 fryer chicken, cut into pieces, skin and fat removed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chicken in a large pot with the 1/4 cup of water.
Cover and simmer until tender, about 45 minutes.
In a medium bowl, mix chili powder, oregano, cocoa, flour (1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons), pepper, and garlic powder along with 1 cup of water.
Add mixture from step 2 to chicken in pot; mix well.
Add peanut butter and 5 cups of water to chicken in pot; mix well.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium.
Cook for 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Chicken Mole
recipes.recipe_by: Pictorial Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service — Oregon Family Nutrition Program — Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chicken, vegetables, and egg noodles combine for a hearty soup.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw frozen chicken in refrigerator (about 24 hours), or thaw in microwave just before cooking soup.
Place chicken pieces in large kettle.
Cover completely with water.
Cover, bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer 2 to 3 hours.
With soap and water, carefully wash your hands and any counter surfaces and equipment that came in contact with raw chicken.
Remove cooked chicken pieces from broth with tongs or slotted spoon.
Cool 10 to 15 minutes before separating bones from meat.
Break meat into bite-sized pieces.
Remove any bones from broth.
Remove fat from broth by skimming with spoon, adding and removing ice cubes, or blotting top of broth with paper towels.
Put chicken meat, seasonings and vegetables into stock.
Bring broth to a boil, cover, reduce heat and cook about 15 to 20 minutes on medium heat until sliced carrots are crispy-tender.
Add noodles and boil uncovered for about 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally to break up any noodles that might stick together.
Ladle into soup bowls.
Refrigerate or freeze leftovers within 2 hours of cooking.
If refrigerated, use within 2 days.
When reheating, bring to a boil.
recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Simply Good Eating Recipe Cards, Vol. 1, 2000 — University of Minnesota Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Colorful veggies, black beans, and pasta make this salad healthy, flavorful, and filling. Make it several hours ahead and let it chill in the refrigerator for a quick summer dinner.

ingredients.name: canned corn kernels
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup canned corn kernels, low-sodium, drained

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) black beans, low-sodium, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions, drain; rinse.
Combine first eight ingredients (pasta through black beans) in a large bowl.
Toss gently with salad dressing.
Chill for several hours to blend flavors.
recipes.name: Chicken Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Color Me Healthy — North Carolina Department of Public Health and North Carolina Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Leftover chicken and frozen veggies help this chicken pot pie come together quickly.

ingredients.name: (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup, reduced-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pre-heat oven to 400 °F.
Mix vegetables, chicken, and soup in ungreased, 9-inch pie plate Stir baking mix, milk, and egg in a mixing bowl with fork until blended.
Pour over vegetables and chicken in pie plate.
Bake 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool for 5 minutes and serve.
recipes.name: Chicken Pot Pie
recipes.recipe_by: The Texas A&M University System, Adapted from Easy Chicken Pot Pie — Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This traditional Mexican soup has a deep flavor using a whole chicken. Hominy can be found in the canned food aisle of the grocery store.

ingredients.name: whole chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 whole chicken, skinned and cut into pieces

ingredients.name: canned hominy
ingredients.raw: 5 cups canned hominy, white or yellow, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put chicken pieces in a large pot and cover with the 8 cups of water.
Simmer over medium heat for 1 hour.
Add the chopped onion, pepper, chili powder, tomato sauce, and oregano to simmering chicken.
After the chicken is thoroughly cooked take the pieces out of the pot and remove most of the bones from the chicken and the pot.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add the rinsed hominy to the pot of chicken and simmer for another 45 minutes.
Serve with lettuce and a wedge of lime.
recipes.name: Chicken Pozole Soup
recipes.notes: To make even healthier, use tomato sauce with no added salt. Chicken breasts or thighs can be substituted for the whole chicken.
recipes.recipe_by: Pictorial Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service — Oregon Family Nutrition Program — Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chicken is added to this traditional vegetable dish of tomatoes, zucchini, and eggplant for a hearty and satisfying meal.

ingredients.name: small eggplant
ingredients.raw: 1 small eggplant, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: red or green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 red or green bell pepper, cut into pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove skin and fat from chicken and cut into 1-inch pieces Heat oil in large non-stick skillet.
Add chicken and sauté about 3 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Add zucchini, eggplant, onion, green pepper, and mushrooms.
Cook about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes, garlic, basil, parsley, and pepper; stir and continue cooking about 5 minutes, or until chicken is tender.
recipes.name: Chicken Ratatouille
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add fresh vegetables and seasonings to leftover chicken that has been properly handled and rice for a quick and delicious salad.

ingredients.name: Italian herb mix and black pepper to taste
ingredients.raw: Italian herb mix and black pepper to taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in a large salad bowl.
Use personal taste preferences to determine the amounts of seasonings.
Serve immediately.
This salad looks great when served on a large plate with a few of the seasonings sprinkled on top.
recipes.name: Chicken Rice Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Onion and pickle relish spice up a traditional chicken salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Use within 1-2 days.
Chicken salad does not freeze well.
How to use: Make chicken salad sandwiches.
Make a pasta salad by mixing with 2 cups cooked pasta.
Kids will love this salad served in a tomato or a cucumber boat.
recipes.name: Chicken Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from: Any Day's a Picnic Chicken Salad , University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — A Family Living Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Crunch into this chicken salad sandwich with crisp celery, apples, and red onion, rounded out by sweet peaches and soft, whole grain bread. Perfect for a picnic or packed lunch!
instructions: Mix together the chicken, apples, peaches, celery, onion, walnuts, and mayonnaise in a small bowl.
Spoon mixture onto 2 slices of the bread.
recipes.name: Chicken Salad and Peach Sandwich
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use up a large head of cabbage from the farmers' market or grocery store with this recipe. The bell pepper and green onions bring a variety of flavors while the chicken and peanuts add protein.

ingredients.name: red or green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 cup red or green bell pepper

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 2 cooked chicken breast, chilled and cut into cubes

ingredients.name: vinegar
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup vinegar, rice or white wine

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Break up noodles.
Set aside.
In a large bowl, add peppers, scallions, unsalted peanuts, and other vegetables if you like.
Add cooked chicken and cabbage.
In a small bowl make dressing with sugar, vinegar, olive oil, and flavor packet.
Stir well.
Pour the dressing over the salad and combine.
Sprinkle noodles on top.
Serve cold.
recipes.name: Chicken Salad with Ramen Noodles
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Green peas and carrots brighten up this traditional chicken soup!

ingredients.name: cooked chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked chicken, cubed, or canned (drained)

ingredients.name: uncooked rice
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup uncooked rice, macaroni, or small noodles

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine celery, carrots, onions, peas, and chicken broth in a pot.
Bring to a boil.
Add chicken and reduce heat.
Add rice, macaroni, or noodles.
Simmer on low until rice, macaroni, or noodles are tender and flavors are mixed.
Chicken should reach a final internal cook temperature of 165°F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
recipes.name: Chicken Soup for the Soul
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from First Nations Development Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Flavorful and filling, this soup is packed with protein making it a full meal. Add extra chiles or a dash of red pepper flakes if you like a spicier soup.

ingredients.name: mild chiles
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup mild chiles, canned and diced

ingredients.name: pinto or garbanzo beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cups pinto or garbanzo beans, canned or cooked and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chicken pieces in a large saucepan and add enough water to cover.
Cook over medium high heat until tender and chicken is cooked, about 25 minutes.
Remove chicken pieces from the broth.
Add tomatoes, garlic, onion, and chiles.
Remove chicken meat from the bones and return meat to broth.
Add beans and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Chicken Soup with Chiles
recipes.recipe_by: Pumpkin Post and Banana Beat Newsletters — University of Massachusetts Extension — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This colorful crowd-pleaser that incorporates vegetables, whole grains, protein, and dairy in one dish. Serve with some fresh, frozen, canned, or dried fruit for a meal that contains all of the food groups.

ingredients.name: medium red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: medium green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium green bell pepper, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: cooked chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 2 cups cooked chicken breast, skinless and diced

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) tomatoes, low-sodium, diced undrained

ingredients.name: (10.75 ounces) cream of chicken soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can (10.75 ounces) cream of chicken soup, low-sodium

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, shredded or grated

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking dish with vegetable oil spray.
Prepare the spaghetti using the package directions, omitting the salt and oil.
Drain well in a colander.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom.
Cook the bell peppers and onion for 4 to 5 minutes, or until tender, stirring occasionally.
Pour into a large bowl.
Stir in the remaining ingredients, including the spaghetti.
Pour into a baking dish.
Bake, covered, for 20 minutes.
Bake, uncovered for 10 minutes, or until the mixture is warmed through and light golden brown on top.
recipes.name: Chicken Spaghetti
recipes.recipe_by: Power to End Stroke: 46 Healthy Soul Food Recipes Cookbook — American Heart Association

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This flavorful rice uses canned tomatoes and chicken with fresh onion, green pepper, and celery. Chili powder and black pepper make it a perky main dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook onion, green pepper, celery, and rice in vegetable oil at medium heat in a large saucepan until soft, about 5 minutes.
Drain tomatoes and save the liquid.
Chop tomatoes into small pieces.
Add tomatoes, liquid, chicken, water, chili powder, and pepper to rice mixture.
Bring to a boil and stir.
Cover and cook on low heat.
Cook until rice is tender (about 25 minutes).
recipes.name: Chicken Spanish Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Eating in Indian Country: Exercise — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This classic stew can be made on the stove top and cooked in less than an hour. The vegetables and chicken make it a filling meal by itself.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove the skin from the chicken and any extra fat.
In a large skillet combine chicken, water, garlic, onion, salt, pepper, tomatoes, and parsley.
Tightly cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Add celery, potatoes, carrots, and bay leaves and continue to cook for 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaves before serving.
recipes.name: Chicken Stew
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This stir-fry is delicious for lunch or dinner. It is very quick to fix. It may also be served over spaghetti, rotini, and other macaroni products.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: or 1/2 can low-sodium carrots, about 8 ounces, drained

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.note: cooked, skin removed, sliced into strips
ingredients.raw: 1 pound chicken, cooked, skin removed, sliced into strips

instructions: Heat a large pan with vegetable oil over high heat.
Add vegetables and garlic to the hot pan.
Stir until garlic is slightly brown.
If using ginger, add that too.
Add the chicken and sugar to the pan, then add soy sauce.
Stir the food for about 1 minute in the pan.
Serve with cooked rice.
recipes.name: Chicken Stir-Fry
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured by a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Kale and carrots add lots of vitamin A to this hearty soup. It is a great recipe for using the beautiful kale from the farmers market.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 cup chicken, cooked, skinned and cubed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium sauce pan.
Add onion and carrots.
Sauté until vegetables are tender, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Add thyme and garlic.
Sauté for one more minute.
Add water or broth, tomatoes, chicken, cooked rice, and kale.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Chicken Vegetable Soup with Kale
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University — The Washington Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program — Puyallup Research and Extension Center

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe is a perfect way to use leftover chicken. With just 15 minutes of prep time, this recipe will be ready in a snap. No leftovers? Use the quick tip below for poaching boneless, skinless chicken breasts. You can also use store-bought rotisserie chicken. If you do, keep in mind that it’s already salty and omit the salt in the dressing.

ingredients.name: red or green grapes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup red or green grapes, halved

instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice and salt in a large bowl.
Add chicken, apple, grapes, celery, and half of the walnuts.
Stir to coat well.
Serve topped with the remaining walnuts.
recipes.name: Chicken Waldorf Salad
recipes.recipe_by: EatingWell Magazine

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Leftover rice? Use it in this fruit and chicken salad for a new spin on chicken salad. Serve the dish on lettuce leaves.

ingredients.name: apple or cantaloupe
ingredients.raw: 1 cup apple or cantaloupe, cut into chunks

ingredients.name: grape halves
ingredients.note: red or purple, cut into chunks
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup grape halves, red or purple, cut into chunks

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 1/4 cups chicken, cooked, cut into bite-size pieces

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
If not using leftover or "planned over" rice, cook rice according to package directions without adding salt.
Chill.
In a serving bowl, mix parsley, black pepper, garlic, dressing, and mayonnaise together.
Add cooled rice, apple, grapes, celery, and chicken.
Stir gently.
Serve cold on a bed of clean lettuce leaves, if desired.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Chicken, Rice, and Fruit Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series — Kansas State University Research and Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make your own delicious chickpea dip! Yogurt and paprika add a new dimension to this hummus recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients into a food processor and blend until smooth.
Serve at room temperature with pita chips, crackers, carrots, or other dipping vegetables.
recipes.name: Chickpea Dip
recipes.recipe_by: More Matters Recipes — US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sautéed veggies simmered with a can of tomatoes, chickpeas and wilted spinach make up this colorful dish. This recipes calls for chickpeas and spinach but any combination of "beans and greens" will work.

ingredients.name: (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, no salt added

ingredients.name: (16 oz) low-sodium chickpeas
ingredients.note: drained and rinsed with cold water

ingredients.name: (10 oz) frozen spinach
ingredients.note: kale can be used instead of spinach

instructions: Put a skillet on the stove on medium high heat.
When the skillet is hot, add oil.
Add onion, garlic, celery and carrot and cook about 15 minutes until the mixture is soft and the onions are lightly browned.
Raise the heat to high and add the tomatoes, beans (white beans instead of chickpeas) and water and cook for 5 minutes.
Lower the heat to low and top the mixture with the spinach (don’t worry about stirring).
Cover and cook until the spinach has thawed and heated throughout, about 10 minutes.
Stir well.
Add the lemon juice and red pepper flakes and stir thoroughly.
Serve with cooked quinoa or brown rice.
recipes.name: Chickpeas and Spinach Sauté
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A combination of zesty herbs and spices add flavor without adding salt. Make this seasoning mix ahead of time and keep it in your pantry to use in soups, stews, sauces, casseroles, and more! 1 serving = 1 Tablespoon
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together all ingredients.
Store in airtight container.
recipes.name: Chili and Spice Seasoning
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dip goes great with baked tortilla chips or raw vegetables at a party. You can experiment with the spices to get new flavors.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash beans in a bowl.
Add onion and chili powder and shredded cheese.
Serve warm or cold with raw vegetables or tortilla chips.
recipes.name: Chili Bean Dip
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Snacks — University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: If you’ve never tried hominy before, you are in for a treat! This dish makes a great comfort food with a creamy texture and a spicy and flavorful flare.

ingredients.name: instant white or yellow hominy
ingredients.raw: 4 cups instant white or yellow hominy, cooked

ingredients.name: (4 ounces each) chopped green chiles
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (4 ounces each) chopped green chiles, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat (350 °F in an electric skillet).
Add onion and cook until tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in hominy, green chiles, sour cream, chili powder and pepper.
Add half of the cheese and mix well.
Reduce heat to medium (300 °F in an electric skillet).
Cover and cook until heated through, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Cover and cook until cheese melts, about 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Chili Cheese Hominy
recipes.notes: Try with different types of grated or crumbled cheese.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make your own savory popcorn featuring chili and garlic flavors. Popcorn is one way to add whole grains and fiber into your diet.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix popcorn and margarine in a bowl.
Mix seasonings thoroughly and sprinkle over popcorn.
Mix well.
Serve immediately and enjoy with family and friends.
recipes.name: Chili Popcorn
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart. Play Hard.™ — USDA Food and Nutrition Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: You don’t have to use salt in this macaroni, tomato, and beef dish seasoned with the Eating Smart Seasoning Mix .

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) diced tomatoes, low-sodium, undrained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a large skillet, drain the fat.
Add water, macaroni, tomatoes, chili powder, and seasoning mix.
Stir.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and simmer covered on low heat for 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Taste, and add a small amount of salt if desired.
Top with shredded cheddar cheese.
Put the lid back on for 1 minute until the cheese is melted.
recipes.name: Chili Tomato Macaroni
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This refreshing and beautiful quick, summer soup features a blend of blueberries, apple juice, and low-fat yogurt, and is garnished with fresh mint leaves.
instructions: Rinse blueberries and set aside a few for garnishing.
Blend all ingredients in food processor or blender.
Serve immediately.
Garnish with mint leaves and blueberries, if desired.
recipes.name: Chilled Blueberry Soup
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with grilled salmon fish fillet (about 3 to 4 ounces), asparagus, and water with lemon slice.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This cool, refreshing melon and citrus soup is perfect for a day when it is too hot to cook. Have it with a hearty, protein-filled sandwich on whole grain bread for a filling meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place cantaloupe and 1/2 cup orange juice in a container of a blender or food processor.
Cover with lid and blend until smooth.
Transfer to large bowl.
Stir in lime juice, cinnamon, and remaining orange juice.
Cover, and refrigerate for at least one hour.
Serve chilled.
recipes.name: Chilled Cantaloupe Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Champions for Change Recipes — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add some South American flair to your meal with this flavorful sauce, which can be used on meat, fish, or vegetables as a marinade or poured over your finished product.

ingredients.name: flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.note: lightly packed and chopped without the stalks
ingredients.raw: 1 cup flat-leaf parsley, lightly packed and chopped without the stalks

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all the ingredients in a blender or food processor and pulse until well chopped, but not pureed.
Spoon the sauce over grilled meats, poultry, seafood, or vegetables.
This sauce can also be used as a marinade.
recipes.name: Chimichurri Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Argentinian Chimichurri Sauce Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add extra calcium to your cookies with yogurt. These cookies also use whole wheat flour which adds fiber and other nutrients.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 375 °F.
In a large bowl combine sugar, brown sugar and margarine; beat until light and fluffy.
Add yogurt and vanilla; blend well.
Stir in flour and baking soda; mix well.
Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto un-greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 375 °F for 8 to 12 minutes or until light and golden brown.
Cool 1 minute, remove from cookie sheets.
recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Yogurt Cookies
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Keep these treats in your freezer for a special day. Peanut butter and chocolate pudding make a delicious coating for graham crackers.

ingredients.name: (1.4 ounces each) low calorie chocolate pudding
ingredients.raw: 2 packages (1.4 ounces each) low calorie chocolate pudding, instant

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix pudding according to package directions, except use 3 1/2 cups milk.
Beat in peanut butter.
Line a 9x13 inch pan with half the graham crackers.
Spread pudding mixture over graham crackers.
Top with remaining crackers.
Freeze for four hours.
Cut into squares and remove from pan.
Store in a plastic bag in the freezer.
recipes.name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Frozen Bars
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Healthy with Diabetes — University of Florida IFAS Extension —

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Incorporating squash into a chocolate cake adds flavor plus fiber, vitamin K, phosphorus, and folate.

ingredients.name: squash
ingredients.raw: 1 cup squash, shredded or finely chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube or bundt pan.
In a large bowl, combine cake mix and cinnamon.
Add eggs, water, and oil.
Blend until combined, then beat with an electric mixer for 2 minutes on medium speed.
Fold in squash.
Add nuts if you like.
Pour into prepared pan.
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour, until cake springs back when lightly touched.
recipes.name: Chocolate Squash Cake
recipes.notes: Other Ideas:
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from: Aunt Barbara's Chocolate Squash Cake, Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon pepper and chopped onion make this a zesty dip that you can use with vegetables or other foods.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse the beans and mash in a small bowl with a fork or potato masher until most of the beans have been crushed.
If you have a food processor, you can use it for this step.
Stir in oil and onion along with lemon pepper and salt to taste.
The mixture will be chunky, not smooth.
recipes.name: Chunky Garbanzo Bean Dip
recipes.notes: Suggest serving with vegetables like carrots, pea pods, and celery.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Throw cinnamon, raisins, and almonds together into a food processor and you have an easy and yummy breakfast on the go.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the raisins and almonds with water.
Toss them in the food processor with the cinnamon.
When sufficiently mixed, form into balls or bar shapes.
recipes.name: Cinnamon Raisin Almond Balls
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These muffins are made with whole grain bran cereal, pumpkin, pecans and spices. They are the perfect treat for a fall day or any time of year!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Spray 12 muffin cups with cooking spray.
Combine 2 tablespoons sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a small bowl; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine cereal and milk and set aside for 5 minutes.
Combine remaining sugar and cinnamon, flour, baking powder, and baking soda in a bowl.
Whisk pumpkin, egg, and vanilla into cereal.
Fold in dry mixture; being careful not to over mix.
Spoon into prepared pan and sprinkle with pecans and sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.
recipes.name: Cinnamon Sugared Pumpkin Pecan Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Cooperative Extension — Ross County Extension Office

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: If you've never made homemade granola, you might be surprised at how a few simple ingredients like oatmeal and honey turn into a tasty, satisfying, whole-grain snack!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 275 °F.
Mix honey, water, vegetable oil, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in oats; mix well.
Spread mixture on a cookie sheet, making a thin layer.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven, stir mixture well and return to oven.
Bake 20 minutes more and stir as before.
Bake 5 to 20 minutes more, until granola is golden brown.
Break into small pieces with spatula.
Cool and then store in a covered container.
recipes.name: Cinnamon Vanilla Granola
recipes.notes: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this quick and easy breakfast mix, made in the microwave. Scoop portions into small bags and serve with yogurt and a banana for a nutritious, on-the-go breakfast!
instructions: In small bowl, mix sugar and cinnamon; set aside.
In large microwavable bowl, microwave butter uncovered on HIGH about 40 seconds, or until melted.
Stir in cereals until evenly coated.
Microwave uncovered 2 minutes, stirring after 1 minute.
Sprinkle half of the sugar mixture evenly over cereals; stir.
Sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture; stir.
Microwave uncovered 1 minute.
Stir in raisins or dried cranberries.
Spread on paper towels to cool.
recipes.name: Cinnamon-Raisin Breakfast Mix
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain (members include American Bakers Association, Wheat Food Council, Grains Food Foundation, National Pasta Association, USA Rice Federation, General Mills, and Kellogg's)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chicken thighs are coated in oregano, cumin, and lime juice and oven baked until tender and golden brown.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425 °F.
To trim the chicken, lay the chicken thighs on the cutting board, skin side up.
Press down on the chicken to push out the excess fat.
Use a sharp knife to cut excess fat.
Put the chicken, oregano, cumin, lime juice, salt, and pepper in the bowl and mix well.
Proceed to the next step or cover and refrigerate up to overnight.
Put the contents of the bowl in the baking pan and transfer to the oven.
Bake about 1 hour until cooked throughout and well browned.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Citrus Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe to can help make half your plate fruits and vegetables. Grapefruit sections are a great addition to fruit or green salads.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut fruit into bite size pieces.
Toss with lettuce and onion.
Mix remaining ingredients for dressing.
Drizzle over salad and toss just before serving.
recipes.name: Citrus Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Quick and Healthy, Vol.II — ScaleDown Publishing, Inc. — Brenda Ponichtera, RD

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this sweet and savory salmon dish with nutty wild rice and a green salad!

ingredients.name: orange or lemon
ingredients.raw: 1 orange or lemon, cut into wedges (optional)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
In an oven safe skillet, heat oil on medium high heat.
Add onion, carrots (or sweet potato), parsley, and ½ cup of orange juice.
Cook 5-8 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix ½ cup orange juice and honey.
In center of skillet, add salmon fillets and season with salt and pepper.
Pour orange juice and honey mixture over top.
Bake entire skillet in oven 16-18 minutes or until fish is flaky.
Garnish with orange or lemon wedges, if using.
recipes.name: Citrus Salmon Fillets
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from First Nations Development Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This warm toasted sandwich is easy to make. Our recipe uses one slice of bread per serving. An open-faced sandwich has less sodium and fewer calories.

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: or 2 tablespoons, about 2 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained

ingredients.name: fresh parsley or cilantro
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped

ingredients.name: cayenne or jalapeño chilies
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon cayenne or jalapeño chilies, diced

ingredients.name: pasteurized process American cheese
ingredients.raw: 3 slices pasteurized process American cheese, cut into halves

instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine tuna, lime juice, onion, tomatoes, apple, celery, and pepper.
Mix well.
Toast the bread.
Place 6 slices of toasted bread on a cookie sheet.
Put an even amount of tuna mixture on top of each slice.
If using parsley and chilies, add these too.
Put 1/2 slice cheese on top of the tuna and bake for about 3 minutes.
Add an extra slice of tomato and lettuce on top if you like.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Citrus Tuna Melt
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Put a new twist on classic mixed vegetables with a splash of lime juice, some olive oil, and fresh oregano.

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables
ingredients.note: such as zucchini, corn, and tomatoes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice vegetables and steam in a small amount of water.
Drain, and place in a bowl to cool.
Mix lime juice with oil.
Add oregano and combine.
Pour lime juice mixture over cool vegetables and mix well.
Serve.
recipes.name: Citrus Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — National Cancer Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Flan is a delicious custard dessert enjoyed throughout the world. End a special meal with this treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Place saucepan with water on stove over medium-high heat and allow to come to a boil.
Spray four ovenproof custard cups with vegetable oil spray.
Combine the whole egg, egg substitute, milk, 5 tablespoons of honey, grated lemon zest, and vanilla.
Beat until mixed but not foamy.
In a separate bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of honey and cinnamon, and mix to blend.
Place the custard cups in a baking dish large enough to accommodate them, plus the water bath.
Spoon 1/2 tablespoon of honey and cinnamon into each custard cup.
Divide the egg mixture equally into each custard cup.
Place the baking dish on the rack in the middle of the oven and pour the boiling water into the baking dish to a depth of 1 inch, taking care not to let the water splash the flan.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the knife blade comes out clean when inserted.
Serve warm or cold.
Before serving, loosen the edges with a knife or spatula and invert onto individual dessert plates.
recipes.name: Classic Honey Flan
recipes.notes: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart Healthy Latino Recipes — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The ultimate comfort food! This healthier version of a family favorite uses non-fat evaporated milk and low-fat cheese to create its creamy sauce.

ingredients.name: finely shredded low-fat sharp cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 1 1/4 cups finely shredded low-fat sharp cheddar cheese

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook macaroni according to directions. (Do not add salt to the cooking water.) Drain and set aside.
Spray a casserole dish with nonstick cooking oil spray.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Lightly spray saucepan with nonstick cooking oil spray.
Add onions to saucepan and sauté for about 3 minutes.
In another bowl, combine macaroni, onions, and the remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Transfer mixture into casserole dish.
Bake for 25 minutes or until bubbly.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Classic Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet and savory, this Cobb Salad is sure to delight with the addition of canned pears, carrots, and Parmesan cheese.
instructions: For the dressing, mix pear juice, vinegar, honey, mustard, and salt and pepper and olive oil in a blender.
Put mixed greens in large mixing bowl, drizzle dressing over greens and mix together.
Add remaining chopped pear, walnuts, and grated carrots and toss lightly.
Portion out 1 cup of salad and top with 1/2 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Cobb Salad with Pears
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This refreshing iced coffee smoothie is a delicious grown-up morning treat.

ingredients.name: of coffee
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup of coffee, cooled to room temperature

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, combine all ingredients; purée until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass and sprinkle with cinnamon, cocoa, or nutmeg if you like.
recipes.name: Coffee Cooler
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking For You or Two — University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tender collard greens flavored with ham hock, onion, green pepper, celery, and red pepper make up this thick and flavorful gumbo. Serve over brown rice for an all-time favorite meal any night of the week.
instructions: Put a skillet on the stove and turn the heat to medium.
When it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, thyme, red pepper flakes, salt, and oregano, and cook until golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the flour in small amounts, sprinkling a little bit at a time and stirring well, until it turns slightly brown, about 10 minutes.
Slowly add the water, stirring constantly.
Add the ham hock.
Raise the heat to high and when it comes to a boil reduce heat to low.
Add the collard greens and cook until tender, about 45 minutes.
Divide the brown rice between 4 shallow bowls and top each with about 1 cup of gumbo.
recipes.name: Collard Green Gumbo with Ham Hock
recipes.notes: One medium sized chicken sausage link can be substituted for a ham hock.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use fresh or frozen spinach and red peppers, or try adding your own colorful vegetables in this dish.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach leaves
ingredients.note: or 9 ounces frozen, thawed, and squeezed dry

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix the cream cheese and garlic powder.
