Spread about 2 tablespoons of the cheese mixture on each tortilla.
Sprinkle about 2 tablespoons bell pepper and 2 tablespoons cheese on one half of each tortilla.
Add spinach: 1/4 cup if using fresh leaves OR 2 tablespoons if using frozen.
Fold tortillas in half.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat until hot.
Put 2 folded tortillas in skillet and heat for 1 to 2 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Remove quesadillas from skillet, place on platter and cover with foil to keep warm while cooking the remainder.
Cut each quesadilla into 4 wedges.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Colorful Quesadillas
recipes.recipe_by: Iowa State University Extension and Outreach

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This three-ingredient salsa is colorful and delicious. Serve it with whole grain chips or crackers for dipping.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) black or red beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) black or red beans, low-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse the beans.
Drain the corn.
Combine beans, corn, and salsa in a medium-sized bowl.
Mix.
recipes.name: Confetti Bean Salsa
recipes.notes: Like it hot? Add a few drops of hot sauce or chopped green chilis. Try chopped cilantro, parsley or green pepper, too.
recipes.recipe_by: The Power of Choice — USDA Food and Nutrition Service and US Department of Health and Human Services Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this recipe with a variety of vegetables until you find what you and your family like best.

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups mixed vegetables, cut into small pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash rice and put into a 2-quart pot with water.
Bring to boil, then lower heat to simmer, and cook uncovered until all the water is absorbed (approximately 45 minutes) Pour into medium sized bowl and allow to cool.
Pour lemon juice over rice and stir.
When rice is cooled to lukewarm, add vegetables, salt, pepper, and oil.
Stir and chill at least 1 hour.
This dish also can be served warm.
recipes.name: Confetti Grain Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Cent$ible Nutrition Cookbook — University of Wyoming Cooperative Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lighten up traditional cole slaw with yogurt and a splash of juice. Raisins and nuts add some sweetness and crunch.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice and cut cabbage into thin strips.
Place pieces in large mixing bowl.
Peel and grate carrots.
Add to mixing bowl.
Add raisins and peanuts to mixing bowl.
Mix all ingredients together.
Combine yogurt and orange juice in small bowl.
Add yogurt mixture to cabbage mixture, stirring to combine ingredients thoroughly.
recipes.name: Confetti Slaw
recipes.notes: Create-a-Flavor Changes
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun -- A Pyramid of Snacks — Cornell Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A good, basic instructional recipe for cooking dry beans. Cooked beans are a great way to get more iron and fiber and can be eaten alone or added to salads and side dishes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sort : Before soaking beans, pick them over and remove any damaged beans, small stones or dirt.
Soak : Most beans will rehydrate to triple their dry size, so be sure to start with a large enough pot.
Choose one of the methods to soak your beans.
Cook : Drain soaking water and rinse beans.
Cover beans with fresh water.
Simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours until tender.
Soaking Methods: Hot Soak: Hot soaking helps reduce intestinal gas.
For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups hot water; heat to boiling and let boil 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover and set aside for up to 4 hours.
Quick Soak: For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups hot water; heat to boiling and let boil 2 to 3 minutes.
Remove from heat, cover and set aside for at least one hour.
Overnight Soak: For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups cold water and let soak overnight, or at least 8 hours.
recipes.name: Cooked Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make these appetizers for your next get-together. If you don't have a cookie cutter, just cut the tortilla into triangles. Add your favorite veggies to the filling.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cut out multiple shapes from 1 whole wheat tortilla using cookie cutters.
Spray a cookie sheet with non-stick cooking spray.
Place cut out tortilla shapes onto cookie sheet.
Bake in oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
While tortillas are baking, mix low-fat cream cheese with garlic powder.
Set aside.
Wash and chop mixed vegetables.
Once tortilla cut outs are finished baking, let cool.
Spread the cream cheese mixture onto each cut out shape and decorate with mixed vegetables.
recipes.name: Cookie Cutter Appetizers
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Family Nutrition Program
recipes.serving_size: 1/2 tortilla with cream cheese and vegetables

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chili powder and pepper flakes give a spicy twist to this classic bean and corn side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the canned corn, but reserve the liquid from the can.
Heat 3 tablespoons of liquid from canned corn in saucepan.
Cook onion in liquid until soft, about 2 minutes.
Add corn, kidney beans, chili powder, and hot red pepper flakes to onion mixture.
Cook over low heat for about 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Corn and Bean Medley
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spices and red wine vinegar dress up the vegetables in this recipe. Enjoy as a side dish with your favorite entree.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine ingredients and mix well.
Serve cold.
recipes.name: Corn and Cucumber Salad
recipes.recipe_by: ScaleDown Publishing, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cilantro, lime juice, and green onions add a delightful taste to this corn side dish. Try using fresh corn when it is in season.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Mix well.
recipes.name: Corn and Green Chili Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use brown rice in this classic stuffed pepper dish to add more whole grains to your meal.

ingredients.name: (10 ounces) diced tomatoes with chiles
ingredients.raw: 1 can (10 ounces) diced tomatoes with chiles, undrained

ingredients.name: (15.2 ounces) low-sodium canned corn
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.2 ounces) low-sodium canned corn, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Remove seeds from peppers.
Cook in boiling water 2 to 3 minutes.
Drain.
Set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in oil in medium skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Combine rice, tomatoes, corn, and onion mixture.
Mix well.
Spoon rice mixture into pepper halves.
Places on baking sheets coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350 °F for 10 minutes or until hot.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 5 more minutes until cheese melts.
recipes.name: Corn and Pepper Cups
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this corn bread recipe the classic way or jazz it up by adding chili powder, whole corn, or even blueberries to give a yummy twist to a basic recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 425 °F.
Grease 8x9 inch pan.
Measure cornmeal, flour, sugar, and baking powder into a large mixing bowl.
Stir to combine ingredients.
Crack egg into a small bowl and beat with a fork to combine white and yolk.
Add egg, oil, and milk to flour mixture.
Mix until ingredients are well blended.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until firm to touch or wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Create-a-Flavor Changes: Buttermilk Corn Bread: Use only 2 teaspoons baking powder and add 1/4 teaspoon baking soda.
Substitute 1 cup buttermilk for skim milk.
Whole Wheat Corn Bread: Use 1/2 cup all purpose flour and 1/2 cup whole wheat flour.
Corny Corn Bread: Add 1 cup kernels (fresh, frozen, or canned, well drained) with the milk.
Cheesy Corn Bread: Add 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese with the milk.
Chili Cheese Corn Bread: Add 1/2 teaspoon chili powder to the flour mixture.
Drain one 4-ounce can chopped green chilies.
Add chilies and 1/4 cup shredded Monterey jack cheese with the milk.
Blueberry Corn Bread: Fold 1 cup blueberries (fresh, frozen, or canned, well drained) into the batter.
Corn Bread Muffins: Pour batter into prepared muffin cups.
Bake 20 minutes at 400 °F.
recipes.name: Corn Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun - Muffins & More — Cornell University Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This family favorite casserole is good for breakfast or lunch. Add flavor by topping it with Fresh Tomato Salsa .
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a saucepan, cook onions over medium heat in vegetable oil until tender (about 4 to 5 minutes).
Open canned corn and drain liquid into a measuring cup.
If needed, add water to make 1 cup of liquid.
Add liquid and cornmeal to the cooked onions in the saucepan.
Stir until the mixture boils.
Remove saucepan from heat.
Mix in milk, corn, and dried egg mix.
In a mixing bowl, mix flour and baking powder.
Add cornmeal mixture.
Mix well.
Spray a 9-inch baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Pour mixture into baking pan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cut into 6 servings.
recipes.name: Corn Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple casserole can be served for breakfast, lunch, or a side dish. For a main dish, add 1 cup of cooked chicken or ground beef.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Beat eggs in a bowl.
Add corn, minced onion, sugar, black pepper, and half the bread crumbs.
Stir and put into a greased 8x8 inch baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining bread crumbs on top of the casserole.
Baked at 350 °F for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Corn Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This corn salad is a great side dish that's easy to make in advance and serve when needed.

ingredients.name: whole kernel corn
ingredients.raw: 2 cups whole kernel corn, fresh or frozen

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In bowl, combine vegetables.
Stir in dressing.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Corn Salad with Fat-free Ranch Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Kentucky Families on the Move: Food and Nutrition Calendar, 2005 — University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a great way to use fresh corn when it's in season. Make it the night before your next BBQ or family gathering.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook corn in boiling water or in the microwave.
Cut corn from the cob.
Add onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice and sugar.
Add oil and combine.
Stir the oil/lemon mixture and basil.
And salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Corn Salad with Fresh Basil and Lemon
recipes.notes: 3 cups frozen corn can be substituted for fresh.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This popular soup is sure to please any hungry stomach.

ingredients.name: reduced-sodium whole kernel corn (about 15 ounces)
ingredients.raw: 1 can reduced-sodium whole kernel corn (about 15 ounces)

ingredients.name: no salt added cream style corn
ingredients.raw: 2 cans no salt added cream style corn

instructions: In a large pot, brown ground beef over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain off fat.
Add water, corn kernels, cream style corn, onion, garlic, chili powder, salt, and pepper to pot.
Mix well.
Cook over low heat for about 15 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Corn Soup
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using corn meal that states "whole corn" or "whole grain corn" on the ingredient list means that you'll get the goodness of whole grains when enjoying this recipe.

ingredients.name: dry egg mix
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup dry egg mix, mixed with 1/4 cup water

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda.
In another bowl, combine buttermilk, egg mix, and vegetable oil.
Beat until well blended.
Add buttermilk mixture all at once to dry ingredients.
Stir until well mixed.
Turn mixture onto a lightly floured board and knead only 10 times.
Roll out to a thickness of 1/4 inch and cut with a 3/4-inch-round cutter.
Cook on a warm ungreased griddle or frying pan for about 10 minutes on each side.
recipes.name: Corn Toasties
recipes.notes: Don't have buttermilk on hand? Try using 2 teaspoons vinegar + 3/4 cup milk (made from non-fat dry milk powder).
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Eating In Indian Country: Diabetes — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Once you've enjoyed a warm, homemade corn tortilla, you might never go back to buying them in a bag! Look for masa harina in the baking aisle of your grocery store.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Measure the masa harina and salt into a large bowl.
Cut the butter into tablespoon-sized pieces and work it into the dry ingredients using the back of a wooden spoon.
Add the water and mix with a wooden spoon or with your hands until a soft dough forms.
Cover the dough with a clean cloth and let rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
To keep the dough from sticking to the tortilla press, put a piece of plastic wrap (or a plastic bag) on the bottom surface of the press.
Put a ball of dough in the center of the plastic.
Then place another piece of plastic wrap on the top of the dough.
Press the dough flat in the press.
Pick up the tortilla with the plastic on both sides.
Peel off one piece of plastic (which can be reused).
Flip the tortilla off of the plastic onto a hot griddle.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottom of the tortilla becomes golden.
Flip the tortilla and press lightly with a spatula, which will make the tortilla puff slightly.
Cook for one to two minutes more, until the tortilla appears to be done.
recipes.name: Corn Tortillas
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking with Kids — New Mexico State University Cooperative Extension Service — Lynn Walters and Jane Stacey — and USDA Food and Nutrition Service Food Stamp Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This savory dish features wild rice and blueberries, a fun way to add flavor and color to any salad!

ingredients.name: ears sweet corn
ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn or canned corn, drained
ingredients.raw: 6 ears sweet corn, husked (or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn or canned corn, drained)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, bring salted water to a boil.
Add corn.
Cook covered for 5 minutes, or until tender.
If using corn on the cob, remove corn from the cob after cooking.
In a serving bowl, combine corn, blueberries, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, wild rice, and jalapeno.
For dressing: In a screw-top jar, combine lime juice, oil, honey, cumin, and salt.
Cover and shake well to combine.
If you do not have a screw-top jar you can whisk ingredients in a small bowl.
Add dressing to salad and toss.
Salad is best enjoyed if covered and refrigerated overnight or up to 24 hours.
recipes.name: Corn, Blueberry, and Wild Rice Salad
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from First Nations Development Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Some families call this "dressing" while others call it "stuffing." Whatever your family prefers, there's no denying that cornbread, broth, and savory herbs come together beautifully in this traditional dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking pan with vegetable oil spray.
In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom.
Cook the green onions and celery for 4 to 5 minutes, or until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the broth, sage, and pepper.
Put the cornbread in a large bowl.
Stir in the vegetable mixture, egg substitute, and pecans (the mixture will be moist).
Transfer to the baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until cooked through and golden brown on top.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
recipes.name: Cornbread Dressing
recipes.notes: For quick and easy cornbread for this recipe, select a cornbread mix with the lowest amounts of saturated fat, trans fat, and sodium available. Prepare using the package directions, substituting fat-free milk for whole milk and egg substitute for the egg. Omit any butter, margarine, oil, sugar, or salt called for. Bake according to the package directions. Let cool. Crumble 4 cups for the cornbread with your fingers and use as directed in the recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: Power to End Stroke: 46 Healthy Soul Food Recipes Cookbook — American Heart Association

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mix up your breakfast routine with this recipe that uses cornmeal for a hearty and satisfying way to make pancakes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cornmeal, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Add butter (or margarine) to cornmeal mixture.
Bring water to a boil and add to cornmeal mixture.
Beat until well mixed.
Mix evaporated milk and vinegar in a small bowl.
Stir milk and vinegar mixture into cornmeal mixture.
Beat to mix well.
Beat in egg.
Heat griddle or frying pan over medium heat. (If electric frying pan is used, preheat it to 380 °F.) Pan is "hot" when a drop of water "dances." Grease pan lightly.
Pour batter onto griddle or fry pan.
Use about 3 tablespoons batter for each pancake.
A 1/4 cup measure is handy to use for pouring.
Stir the batter up from the bottom now and then to keep it well mixed.
Cook until top is covered with bubbles and the bottom is brown.
Loosen edges of each pancake all around.
Turn pancakes over and brown other side.
recipes.name: Cornmeal Pancakes
recipes.recipe_by: Smart Shopper Recipes — USDA Consumer and Marketing Service — Food Trades Staff

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This potato salad uses peas, onions, and celery for a bright crunch and a base that includes plain yogurt for a light, zesty flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash potatoes, leave skin on and cut in bite-sized chunks.
Place in pan and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, lower to simmer and cook uncovered until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain in colander and sprinkle lightly with cold water.
In the mean time, put the rest of the ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
Drain potatoes well and add to the bowl.
Mix well and refrigerate until ready to use.
Garnish with fresh lettuce and sliced tomatoes.
recipes.name: Country Style Potato Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Couscous is cooked with sage, peas, and onions for a savory side dish. Look for couscous or whole grain couscous in the aisle near the rice.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine oil and onions in heavy skillet.
Sauté for 5 to 10 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the peas, sage, water, couscous, and salt if desired.
Cover and cook on medium heat for about 5 minutes or until peas are tender but still bright green and all of the water is absorbed.
Fluff with fork.
recipes.name: Couscous with Peas and Onions
recipes.notes: Serve with lemon wedges or balsamic vinegar.
recipes.recipe_by: CHOICES: Steps Toward Health — UMass Extension Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This salsa is a party favorite. Using pantry items liked canned beans, corn, and tomatoes, this recipe comes together quickly and can serve a crowd.

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix kidney beans, black beans, corn, tomatoes, chilies, and onion in a large bowl.
Add oil and lime juice (if using), toss gently to combine.
Taste.
Add small amount of salt and pepper if desired.
Serve by itself, with raw vegetables and/or corn chips.
recipes.name: Cowboy Caviar (Bean Salsa)
recipes.notes: Be creative! Add any kind of beans you have. Make it spicier by adding hot sauce.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This red and golden whole grain dessert is a perfect balance of sweet apples and tart cranberries.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Wash apples, remove cores and slice thinly, keeping peel on.
In a bowl, combine the cranberries and apples.
Pour into an 8x8 inch pan.
Combine melted margarine with oatmeal, brown sugar, and cinnamon until well blended.
Sprinkle over apple/cranberry mixture.
Cover and bake for 15 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 more minutes until the topping is crisp and brown.
Serve warm or cold.
recipes.name: Cran-Apple Crisp
recipes.recipe_by: Pumpkin Post and Banana Beat Newsletters — University of Massachusetts Extension — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cranberry juice, raisins, allspice, and brown sugar give this dish a sweet and tangy sauce. Serve with your favorite veggies for an easy dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine brown sugar, cornstarch, and allspice in a saucepan.
Gradually add the next three ingredients and stir.
Cook over medium heat until sauce thickens and boils.
Place one slice of ham in greased baking dish.
Pour one half of the sauce over the ham slice.
Top with second slice.
Add remaining sauce.
Bake, covered in 350 °F oven for 45 minutes.
recipes.name: Cranberry Ham Slice
recipes.recipe_by: University of the Virgin Islands Cooperative Extension Service — 4-H/Family & Consumer Sciences Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this bread for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Use fresh cranberries when in season for a burst of flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and baking soda in a large bowl.
Grate orange peeling, then squeeze juice from orange.
Add additional orange juice to make 3/4 cup.
In a separate bowl, blend orange juice, butter, egg, and grated orange peel; add to flour mixture, stirring until just blended.
Mix in cranberries and walnuts.
Pour batter into a 9x5 inch loaf pan, greased on bottom only.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes; remove and cool completely on wire rack.
Optional: to make glaze, mix powdered sugar and water; add water as needed to make thin glaze.
Drizzle over cooled loaf.
recipes.name: Cranberry Nut Bread
recipes.notes: *You can substitute 1/2 to 1 cup of the flour with whole wheat flour. All-purpose flour used for nutrition analysis and costing purposes.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these delicious muffins for breakfast anytime of the year using canned pumpkin and frozen cranberries.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Sift together dry ingredients (flour through allspice) and set aside.
Beat oil, eggs, and pumpkin together until well blended.
Add the wet ingredients (pumpkin mixture) to the dry ingredients all at once.
Stir until moistened.
Fold in chopped cranberries.
Spoon into paper lined muffin cups.
Bake at 400 °F for 15 to 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Cranberry Pumpkin Muffins
recipes.notes: Serve with a glass of low-fat milk for a healthy snack.
recipes.recipe_by: Pumpkin Post and Banana Beat Newsletters — University of Massachusetts Extension — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet strawberry gelatin and tart cranberry sauce make a yummy dish. Make ahead and keep in the refrigerator until ready to eat.

ingredients.name: strawberry gelatin
ingredients.note: 3 oz. packages, can also use raspberry

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Make gelatin and refrigerate until partially set.
Beat cranberry sauce.
Grate orange peel into sugar and add to cranberry sauce with rest of ingredients.
Fold mixture into partially set gelatin.
Refrigerate until set.
Serve.
recipes.name: Cranberry Salad
recipes.notes: Suggested to serve with a mixture of instant lemon pudding mix and low-fat whipped topping.
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This creamy soup makes a perfect lunch or dinner. Keep it healthy using fat-free milk and fresh or frozen broccoli.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a saucepan combine chicken broth, chopped onion, broccoli, thyme, bay leaf and garlic powder.
Bring mixture to boiling.
Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf.
Place half of the mixture in a blender or food processor, cover and blend 30 to 60 seconds or until smooth.
Pour into a bowl; repeat with remaining vegetable mixture, set all aside.
In the same saucepan warm the oil.
Stir in flour, salt, and pepper.
Add the milk all at once, stirring rapidly with a wire whisk.
Cook and stir until mixture is thickened and bubbly.
Stir in the blended broccoli mixture.
Cook and stir until soup is heated through.
Season to taste with additional salt and pepper.
recipes.name: Cream of Broccoli Soup
recipes.notes: Fresh or frozen broccoli can be used.
recipes.recipe_by: Calcium -- It’s Not Just Milk — University of Nevada Cooperative Extension — Nevada Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish combines flavorful vegetables with chicken and seasonings to make a tasty lunch or dinner main dish.

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup red bell pepper, finely chopped

ingredients.name: skinless cooked chicken breast
ingredients.raw: 2 cups skinless cooked chicken breast, diced

ingredients.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Shred the potato and set aside. (It will darken in color, but this will not affect hash.) Heat 1 tablespoons butter or oil in a medium/large non-stick skillet.
Add onion, bell peppers, celery and garlic.
Sauté until lightly browned, 5 minutes.
Push vegetables to one side of pan.
Add remaining butter or oil.
Add potatoes and mix with oil to coat them.
Mix and combine well with the vegetables.
Cook 3 minutes.
If potatoes stick, scrape pan vigorously and move contents around pan to spray the bottom with cooking spray.
Mix in chicken, milk, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Spread and flatten out the mixture into a thick cake.
Use the edge of a pancake turner to cut it into 4 sections. (Or, hash can be broken into rough pieces while cooking.) Cover the pan.

Cook until potatoes are tender and hash is lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes, turning so bottom sides can also brown. (Spray pan with oil spray if necessary while turning hash.) When hash is done, divide equally among four plates.
Serve with barbecue sauce drizzled on top or around each portion. (If desired, sauce can first be thinned, by mixing 4 tablespoons sauce with 4 tablespoons milk.)
recipes.name: Creamy Chicken Hash
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe Corner — American Institute for Cancer Research

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: There is no cooking required for this dish, and kids can pick their favorite veggies to go along with the creamy dip.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the sour cream, yogurt, and dill in a medium bowl.
Stir together.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the fridge until you serve it.
recipes.name: Creamy Dill Dip
recipes.notes: Serve with cucumber slices. If you want a creamy salad dressing, add a few tablespoons of water to the dip.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this creamy dressing over salads or use as a dip for your favorite veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine all the above ingredients.
Refrigerate in a covered container for at least an hour.
Serve chilled.
recipes.name: Creamy Italian Herb Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: With just three simple ingredients, this peanut dip is an easy way to make ordinary fruit or veggie sticks extraordinary!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix the peanut butter and orange juice until smooth.
Stir in the vanilla yogurt.
Cover and put in the fridge until chilled.
recipes.name: Creamy Peanut Dip
recipes.notes: Serve with fresh apples, pears, carrot sticks or celery sticks.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Combining yogurt or cottage cheese with savory herbs and spices makes this veggie dip cool and delicious.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine yogurt (or cottage cheese), pepper, garlic powder, dried onion, dried parsley, salt, and dill (if used).
Beat until smooth.
Chill dip in refrigerator until ready to serve.
Serve with raw vegetables.
recipes.name: Creamy Vegetable Dip
recipes.notes: Serve with approximately 6 cups of vegetables, such as cauliflower florets, carrot sticks, celery sticks, jicama, sliced bell pepper, or sliced cucumber.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this recipe with red beans or other varieties and serve this main dish with cooked brown rice and a green salad for a complete meal. To learn how to cook dried beans, check out our recipe Cooked Beans .
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook celery, green pepper, and onion in vegetable oil in a large saucepan until soft, about 5 minutes.
Break up large pieces of tomatoes.
Add tomatoes and seasonings to vegetable mixture.
Bring to a boil.
Add beans and return to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat until flavors are blended and liquid is cooked away, about 30 minutes.
Stir once and a while to prevent sticking.
recipes.name: Creole Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Eating In Indian Country: Do You Weigh Too Much? — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use your favorite spices to season these oven baked French fries. Endless possibilities with your favorite seasoning blends.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Lightly oil a 9x13 inch pan.
Wash and cut potatoes.
Pat dry on towels.
Spread strips of potatoes in one layer in pan.
Distribute remaining oil evenly over potatoes.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until potatoes are golden brown and tender.
Turn frequently.
Season to taste.
recipes.name: Crispy Oven Baked Fries
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Keep the flavor but cut down on the fat and sodium with this oven-fried chicken recipe. A welcome addition to your next family meal or potluck.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Add 1/2 teaspoon of poultry seasoning to milk.
Combine remaining 1/2 teaspoon of poultry seasoning and all other spices (except paprika) with cornflake crumbs and place in a plastic bag.
Dip chicken into milk, shake to remove excess, then quickly shake in bag with seasoning and crumbs.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Remove from refrigerator and sprinkle lightly with paprika for color.
Evenly space chicken on greased baking pan.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil and continue baking for an additional 30 to 40 minutes or until the meat can be easily pulled away form the bone with a fork.
The drumsticks may require less baking time than the breasts.
Crumbs will form a crispy "skin." (Do not turn chicken during baking.)
recipes.name: Crispy Oven-Fried Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
recipes.serving_size: 1/2 breast or 2 small drumsticks, 1/6 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh pico de gallo, cooked chicken, veggies, and cheese combine to make these tasty taquitos that are baked, not fried, for a healthy meal or snack.

ingredients.name: canned corn
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup canned corn, no salt added

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.note: or Monterey jack or queso fresco

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 425 °F.
In a medium bowl, combine 1 cup Pico de Gallo, chicken, corn, green onion, bell pepper, and cheese.
Soften tortillas on the stovetop or in the microwave oven, and spoon a heaping tablespoon of filling onto the center of each tortilla.
Roll up tightly and secure each with a toothpick.
Place rolled tortillas seam side down on a baking sheet and brush each lightly with oil.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes or until crisp and lightly browned.
Place 3 taquitos on each plate and serve with remaining Pico de Gallo.
recipes.name: Crispy Taquitos
recipes.recipe_by: California Champions for Change Lunch Recipes — California Department of Public Health — Network for a Healthy California

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Baked instead of fried, these walleye patties are full of flavor with less fat!

ingredients.name: walleye fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound walleye fillets, minced (fresh or frozen)

ingredients.name: egg (or 2 tablespoons dried egg mix + 1/4 cup water)
ingredients.note: or 2 tablespoons dried egg mix + 1/4 cup water
ingredients.raw: 1 egg (or 2 tablespoons dried egg mix + 1/4 cup water)

ingredients.name: Note: "Minced" means cut up into tiny pieces.
ingredients.raw: Note: "Minced" means cut up into tiny pieces.

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Place minced fish in a colander and press firmly to remove as much moisture as possible.
In a medium bowl, mix fish, onion, celery, mayonnaise, crackers, egg, garlic powder, dill, paprika, and salt.
Let rest for 10 minutes.
Shape mixture into 8 patties.
Spray baking sheet with cooking spray and place patties at least 1 inch apart on the pan.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, flip, and bake for another 10 minutes.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Crispy Walleye Patties
recipes.notes: Optional: Serve with a lemon wedge or tartar sauce.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Marti Hunt, Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This lentil stew is full of wholesome vegetables, protein, and fiber. Although it can cook for several hours in the crockpot, the "hands on" preparation time is low.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onion and garlic with olive oil.
Combine sauté mix with the rest of the ingredients in a crock pot.
Cook on low for 8 hours or high for 4 hours.
Spoon stew into bowls to serve and top with a dollop of fat-free or low-fat plain yogurt (optional).
recipes.name: Crock Pot Vegetable Lentil Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Del Norte (California) Department of Health and Human Services — and University of Kentucky Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: So quick, so easy, and so delicious! This parfait is a favorite among kids and adults alike. Use soy yogurt instead of regular yogurt for those who can't have dairy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spoon yogurt into glass.
Top with fruit and granola.
recipes.name: Crunchy Berry Parfait
recipes.recipe_by: Saint Joseph College SNAP-Ed Nutrition Education Team

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This main dish is a combination of chicken, vegetables, and fruit. Enjoy it as a cold salad or as the filling of a hearty sandwich or wrap.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use leftover cooked chicken, or cook enough chicken to make 2 cups of chicken pieces.
Chop the celery and green pepper into small pieces.
Peel and chop 1/4 of an onion.
Peel and chop half of a cucumber.
Chop the apple into pieces.
It’s okay to leave the peel on the apple.
Cut the grapes in half.
Put all the ingredients in a large bowl.
Stir together.
recipes.name: Crunchy Chicken Salad
recipes.notes: Serve on lettuce, crackers, or bread.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of fresh and colorful veggies, these wraps are a great way to help meet your MyPlate goal of making half of your plate fruits and vegetables.

ingredients.name: zucchini
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup zucchini, cut into small strips

ingredients.name: yellow (summer) squash
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup yellow (summer) squash, cut into small strips

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/8 cup green bell pepper, seeded and diced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, stir ranch dressing into cream cheese; chill.
Wash and chop vegetables.
Steam broccoli in microwave for 1 minute with 1 tablespoon of water.
Spread cream cheese onto flour tortilla, staying one inch from edge.
Sprinkle vegetables over cream cheese.
Roll tortilla tightly.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours before serving (the wrap will hold its shape better).
With a sharp knife slice into circles and serve.
recipes.name: Crunchy Vegetable Wraps
recipes.recipe_by: Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using Master Mix Oregon saves time and money in this pumpkin pie recipe.

ingredients.name: all-purpose baking mix for biscuits
ingredients.note: or use Master Mix - see notes for link to recipe
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup all-purpose baking mix for biscuits

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F and lightly grease a 9 or 10 inch pie plate.
Combine all ingredients in a medium mixing bowl or a blender.
Beat 2 minutes with a mixer until smooth, or blend in the blender on high for one minute.
Pour into the pie plate.
Bake until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean, about 50 to 55 minutes.
Cool slightly and keep refrigerated.
Serve with whipped topping or ice cream.
recipes.name: Crustless Pumpkin Pie
recipes.notes: *Recipe for Master Mix
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This blend of tofu and cooked rice combines corn, peas, carrots, and seasonings pressed into a skillet and cooked into "crispy" goodness.

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.note: sliced including white and green parts

instructions: To make the rice, cook rice according to the directions on the package.
Set aside to cool and dry out.
Put the tofu, corn, scallions, carrot, basil, and salt in the bowl and mix well.
When the rice has fully cooled, add it to the bowl with the tofu and mix well.
Put the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the rice and tofu mixture; reduce heat to low and press down the rice mixture with a spatula.
Cover and cook 10 minutes.
Press down again to help form a crust.
Flip portions of the rice so that you get chunks of crispy rice.
Cook until crispy, up to 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Crusty Rice with Tofu and Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vinegar, oregano, garlic, and onions kick up the flavor in this classic rice and bean recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet.
Sauté the garlic, onion, and green bell pepper until golden, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the beans, broth, vinegar, and seasoning; bring to a boil then lower to a simmer.
Cook covered for 5 minutes.
Spoon over cooked rice and serve.
recipes.name: Cuban Beans and Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.
recipes.serving_size: 1 1/2 cups prepared beans and rice, 1/4 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This classic salad blend of lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and radishes are brought to life with the refreshing dressing made with oil, lime juice, and seasonings.

ingredients.name: head Romaine lettuce
ingredients.note: washed, patted dry with paper towels, and torn into bite-sized pieces

instructions: To make the dressing: Put the oil, lime juice, garlic, salt, and pepper in the small bowl and mix well.
Lemon juice can be used instead of lime juice.
To make the salad: Put the lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and radishes in the mixing bowl and toss to combine.
White onion can be used instead of red onion.
Pour the dressing over the lettuce mixture and toss.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Cuban Salad
recipes.notes: For protein, add low-sodium canned tuna or salmon on top of the salad.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick, simple and refreshing salad featuring fresh blueberries and crisp cucumber chunks with feta cheese, arugula, and a lime vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: lime juice
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon lime juice, freshly squeezed or bottled

ingredients.name: medium greenhouse-grown cucumber
ingredients.raw: 1 medium greenhouse-grown cucumber, cut into small chunks

instructions: In a small bowl whisk together vinaigrette ingredients.
In a large bowl mix together all salad ingredients, except bread.
When ready to serve, add vinaigrette to salad and toss.
Toast bread, then cut into four pieces.
recipes.name: Cucumber Blueberry Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This cucumber salad has a light and creamy dressing. Make it ahead of time and chill it in the refrigerator until you are ready to serve it.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and thinly slice cucumber.
Mix all other ingredients in the mixing bowl.
Add cucumber slices and stir until coated.
Chill until serving.
recipes.name: Cucumber Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Right Is Basic — Michigan State University Cooperative Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh tomatoes and cucumbers make this couscous salad a summer time treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss together the cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, couscous (or rice), dill, and salad dressing.
Chill for 1 hour.
Serve.
recipes.name: Cucumber Salad with Tomatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Don’t Play With Your Food: Spring and Summer Cookbook — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this cool and tangy low-fat yogurt dip with your favorite vegetables.

ingredients.name: salt and lemon pepper
ingredients.raw: salt and lemon pepper, to taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir yogurt and cream cheese until smooth.
Rinse the cucumber under running water.
Slice the cucumber in half the long way and run a spoon down the middle to remove the seeds.
Chop the cucumber into small pieces.
Stir the cucumber, chopped garlic, and seasonings (optional) into the yogurt mixture.
recipes.name: Cucumber Yogurt and Cream Cheese Dip
recipes.notes: To quickly soften cream cheese, microwave for approximately 20 seconds.
recipes.recipe_by: Iowa Department of Public Health — Iowa Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon and dill combined with low-fat yogurt make this a flavorful and healthy dip. Serve it with your favorite vegetables.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel, seed, and grate one cucumber.
Slice other cucumber and set aside.
Mix yogurt, grated cucumber, sour cream, lemon juice, dill, and garlic in a serving bowl.
Chill for 1 hour.
Arrange sliced cucumbers, tomatoes, broccoli, and carrots on a colorful platter.
Serve with cucumber dip.
recipes.name: Cucumber, Yogurt and Herb Dip
recipes.notes: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube .
recipes.recipe_by: More Matters Recipes — US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Short on time? This better-for-you creamy cauliflower risotto makes for a quick and tasty dinner. Heart healthy avocado gives the dish its smooth, indulgent texture instead of traditional dairy-based ingredients.

ingredients.name: medium shrimp
ingredients.raw: 8 medium shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed

ingredients.name: ripe
ingredients.note: fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled and diced
ingredients.raw: 1 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled and diced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Microwave frozen “riced” cauliflower according to package directions, usually about 5-6 minutes; set aside.
Heat 1 Tbsp. olive oil in a medium nonstick pan over medium heat.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side until light pink and opaque.
Place shrimp in a small bowl and season with cumin, lime zest, and salt.
Add remaining oil into the pan.
Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is soft, about 2 minutes.
Add garlic and avocado and cook for one minute, until heated through.
Transfer avocado onion mixture into a blender or food processor and add lime juice.
Cover and blend until smooth, stirring mixture with a spatula if needed.
Transfer heated “riced” cauliflower into the pan and top with pureed avocado onion mixture.
Cook over medium heat, stirring gently until cauliflower has a beautiful green color.
Divide into two bowls and top with cooked shrimp.
recipes.name: Cumin Lime Shrimp over Creamy Cauliflower Risotto
recipes.notes: Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and additional avocado slices. For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com/
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Fresh Avocados Love One Today, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Brown rice gets a flavor burst when curry powder, onions, and dried apricots are added. Toasted pumpkin seeds add a nice crunch.

ingredients.name: brown rice
ingredients.raw: 1 cup brown rice, short grain, uncooked

ingredients.name: medium red onion
ingredients.raw: 1 medium red onion, peeled and finely chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the rice well.
Heat the oil over medium heat in a large heavy saucepan.
Add the onions and garlic and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, then stir in the curry powder.
Add the rice and broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in the apricots and spinach.
Replace cover and let sit for 10 minutes.
Add the pumpkin seeds, salt, pepper (and more curry if desired) and fluff with a fork.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Curried Brown Rice with Pumpkin Seeds, Apricots and Spinach

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Shredded chicken is coated with yogurt, curry powder, and cilantro and combined with crisp celery and apples give this salad delicious flavor with a refreshing "crunch." Chill and serve with crackers or use as a sandwich filling.
instructions: Put chicken in a bowl and add remaining ingredients.
Mix to combine.
Cover and refrigerate at least one hour and up three days.
recipes.name: Curried Chicken Salad
recipes.notes: If you do not have leftover chicken, you can poach chicken. Put 4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs in a pan and cover with cold water (about 4 cups) and bring to a boil over high heat. Lower the heat and cook for 10 minutes. Turn the heat off, turn the chicken pieces over and set aside for 20 minutes. Remove the thighs with a slotted spoon and set aside to cool completely. Shred and prepare recipe as directed. You can also substitute 2 cans of drained light tuna, instead of chicken thighs.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Savory chicken and mushrooms balanced with the sweetness of raisins and red bell peppers will make this curried one-pan recipe a family favorite.

ingredients.name: boneless
ingredients.note: about 12 oz, diced into 1 inch cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in large sauté pan.
With heat on medium-high, place chicken in pan and cover with lid.
Cook chicken about 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and peppers to pan and sauté 3 to 4 minutes.
Add chicken broth.
Gently mix in raisins, rice, and curry powder; bring to boil, reduce heat and cover.
Simmer until rice is done; fluff with fork and let sit 3 to 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Curried Chicken with Raisins and Mushrooms
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Add a side salad with light dressing and an 8 oz glass of fat-free milk. Time Saving Ideas: Purchase sliced mushrooms, fresh or frozen bell pepper strips, and pre-cooked, diced chicken.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish can be served on whole wheat bread, on a bed of lettuce, or as a dip with your favorite veggies!

ingredients.name: (15 ounces each) chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15 ounces each) chickpeas, low-sodium, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the chickpeas to a large bowl and mash with a potato masher.
You can mash them to be as smooth or coarse as you desire.
Add all of the remaining ingredients to the bowl and mix until everything is combined.
recipes.name: Curried Chickpea Salad
recipes.notes: Add the Curried Chickpea Salad to a sandwich and add spinach or lettuce if desired. Also, try topping tossed salad with it instead of salad dressing.
recipes.recipe_by: Penn State Extension — Nutrition Links Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve these flavorful potatoes with roasted chicken and a salad for a filling and tasty dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the onion, and chop it into small pieces.
Peel the potatoes, and chop them into 1 inch cubes.
Boil the potatoes in a medium saucepan until they are soft.
Drain off the hot water.
Add ice cold water to cover the potatoes.
Melt the butter on medium heat in a frying pan or skillet.
Cook the onion in the butter until it turns yellow.
Drain the water from the potatoes and add them to the frying pan.
Stir and cook until they absorb the butter.
Add the broth, curry powder, and lemon juice.
Cook until the potatoes have absorbed the broth.
recipes.name: Curried Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This flavorful dish has protein, vegetables, dairy, and lots of herbs and spices.

ingredients.name: head of cauliflower
ingredients.raw: 1 head of cauliflower, trimmed and cut into small florets

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook quinoa until just tender, according to package directions.
Heat oil in saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add curry powder and cumin, and cook, about 30 seconds, or until fragrant.
Stir in broth and chopped garlic.
Bring to a boil.
Add cauliflower, cover, and return to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer 3 minutes.
Add frozen peas and cook until cauliflower is just tender, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Stir in 2 tablespoons broth from cauliflower mixture into yogurt in small bowl.
Add yogurt mixture to cauliflower.
Fold in quinoa, cashews, and cilantro.
Sprinkle with green onion and top with a little fresh lime juice.
Optional: Season with a pinch of salt.
recipes.name: Curried Quinoa and Cauliflower
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Curry powder and cinnamon give unique flavor to this zucchini, butternut squash, tomato, and bean stew. Add raisins or dried cranberries for an added "sweet note."

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounce) low-sodium white beans or chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounce) low-sodium white beans or chickpeas

instructions: Heat a large pot on the stove over medium heat and add oil.
Add the onion, garlic and celery and cook about 10 minutes, until the onion is tender.
Add zucchini and curry powder and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the butternut squash, tomatoes and chickpeas and cover.
Continue cooking about 10 minutes.
Serve with cooked brown rice.
recipes.name: Curried Squash Stew
recipes.notes: For additional flavor, add 1/2 cup raisins.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Curry powder adds lots of flavor to this vegetable dip. Serve it with veggies or whole wheat pita for a satisfying snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the sour cream, yogurt, and curry powder.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the refrigerator until you serve it.
recipes.name: Curry Dip
recipes.notes: Serve with bite-sized raw vegetables, crackers, or pita bread.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Turn the heat up on this vegetable dip by using hot curry powder or use regular curry powder for a more mild taste.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix ingredients in a bowl.
Chill.
Serve with crisp raw vegetables pieces, such as celery, carrot, or summer squash sticks.
recipes.name: Curry Vegetable Dip
recipes.recipe_by: Pyramid Snacks — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Team Nutrition

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This salad will make a great side dish for your next cookout.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blanch the cabbage with boiling water for 1 minute.
Discard the water.
Place the cabbage in a large bowl and add grated carrots, sliced onion, red pepper, oregano, olive oil, salt, brown sugar, vinegar, and water.
Place in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Curtido Salvadoreño (Cabbage Salad)
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Stuffing mushrooms just makes something wonderful even better! But what you stuff in these tasty little vegetables can make or break the dish. Typically, mushrooms are stuffed with foods containing saturated fats and sodium. So, if you're trying to watch one or both of these, consider various herbs and spices -- they do a nice job of seasoning so many foods.

ingredients.name: canned
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup canned, drained, no-salt added chickpeas

instructions: Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Clean mushrooms with a paper towel or vegetable brush; remove stems to use for the filling.
While oven is warming, put mushroom caps (open side down) in oven for 10 minutes.
This will prepare the caps for stuffing.
Chop the garlic and onions and sauté with 1 teaspoon of olive oil.
One minute before they are finished, add the four herbs.
After 1 minute, remove from heat.
In a large bowl, mash mushroom stems and chickpeas.
Add all other ingredients.
Mix well.
Lightly spray a baking sheet and the mushroom caps.
Stuff the mushrooms with the mixture and place on baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes or until the stuffing is golden brown.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with an herb of your choice, and enjoy.
recipes.name: Dave’s Herb-Stuffed Mushrooms
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Dave, MyPlate Nutritionist and Webmaster

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cranberries and apples are the perfect combination for this delicious homemade dessert.

ingredients.name: large apples
ingredients.raw: 4 large apples, peeled, cored, and sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir all ingredients (except for the pie crust) together in a medium sized mixing bowl and place in a 10-inch deep dish pie pan.
Place one pie crust on top of the fruits.
Cut 3 or 4 slits to allow the steam to escape.
Bake at 375 °F for about an hour.
Serve warm.
Refrigerate any leftovers.
recipes.name: Deep Dish Apple Cranberry Pie
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe combines traditional leafy greens with cabbage, garlic, and onions for a savory side dish that's packed with flavor and nutrition.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse greens, remove stems, and tear in small pieces.
In a large saucepan, boil 3 quarts of water.
Add mustard greens, return to a boil and cook 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and cook 1 more minute.
Drain in colander.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium high heat.
Add oil and sauté garlic and onion until light brown, about 3 minutes.
Add greens and vinegar and cook briefly, about 3 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Delicious Greens
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lentils are a great variety of dried legume! They are full of protein, fiber, and nutrients like iron; have a great taste; and cook faster than dried beans because they do not require pre-soaking. Try them in this hearty stew for lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) whole tomatoes
ingredients.note: or 3-4 fresh tomatoes cut in wedges
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) whole tomatoes, low-sodium, cut into pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt butter in a large skillet.
Sauté onion until tender.
Add water, lentils, Worcestershire sauce, oregano, and garlic powder.
Cover, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add carrots, celery, and salt.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes more or until the vegetables are tender.
Add tomatoes.
Heat thoroughly and serve.
recipes.name: Delicious Lentil Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Go With Beans — University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — Eau Claire County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These oven fries are crisp and seasoned with pepper, allspice, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes and cut into 1/2 inch strips.
Place potato strips into ice water, cover, and chill for 1 hour or longer.
Preheat oven to 475 °F.
Remove potatoes and dry strips thoroughly.
Place garlic powder, onion powder, salt, white pepper, allspice, and pepper flakes in plastic bag.
Toss potatoes in spice mixture.
Brush potatoes with oil.
Place potatoes in nonstick shallow baking pan.
Cover with aluminum foil and place in preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Remove foil and continue baking uncovered for additional 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Turn fries occasionally to brown on all sides.
recipes.name: Delicious Oven French Fries
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A favorite dish at parties and potlucks, Deviled Eggs also make a great, protein-filled anytime snack!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Hard boil eggs by placing eggs in a saucepan and covering them with water.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to simmer; cook for 15 minutes.
Immediately rinse under cold water to stop cooking and to make it easy to peel off shells.
Refrigerate peeled eggs (without shells) until ready for use.
Slice eggs into halves lengthwise.
Remove yellow yolks and save whites.
Place yolks in a one-quart zip lock style bag along with the remaining ingredients (except the egg whites).
Press out air.

Close bag and knead (mush together) until ingredients are well-blended. (Note: you could also put yolks in a bowl with other ingredients [except the egg whites] and mix together well until they look like a paste).
Push contents toward one corner of the bag.
Cut about 1/2 inch off the corner of the bag.
Squeezing the bag gently, fill reserved egg white hollows with the yolk mixture. (Note if you used a bowl, spoon the yolk mixture into the egg whites).
Chill to blend flavors.
recipes.name: Deviled Eggs
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use fish fillets from the freezer in this recipe to make a quick, weeknight seafood dinner.

ingredients.name: frozen haddock or cod fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound frozen haddock or cod fillets

instructions: Microwave Method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw frozen fish in refrigerator overnight or thaw in microwave oven.
Then, separate into 4 fillets or pieces.
Place fish in a glass-baking dish.
Cover with wax paper.
Cook at "medium" power in the microwave for 3 minutes.
Remove cover, turn fish over, and sprinkle with lemon juice and seasonings.
Cover and continue cooking at "medium" power for 3 minutes or until fish flakes with a fork.
Skillet method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Separate into four fillets or pieces.
Place fish in heated fry pan.
Sprinkle with lemon juice and seasonings.
Cover and cook over moderate heat until fish flakes when tested with a fork, about 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Dilled Fish Fillets
recipes.recipe_by: Microwave Recipes — University of Illinois Extension Service
recipes.serving_size: 1 4 oz. piece of fish, 1/4 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Dirty rice is a flavorful way to spice up your main dishes. It is also a good way to serve leftovers; cooked chicken or ham can be used in place of ground beef.
instructions: In a small bowl, combine dried egg mix and water.
Mix well and set aside.
In a large skillet, cook ground beef, onion, and green pepper in oil over medium heat for about 10 minutes.
Add dried egg mix to skillet.
Scramble eggs over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Add peas and beans to skillet.
Cook for about 5 minutes.
Add rice and pepper to skillet.
Stir to break up any clumps of rice.
Cook for about 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Dirty Rice
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Looking for a healthy, crunchy snack? This recipe is super simple and can be made in bulk in advance.

ingredients.name: acidic fruit juice (lemon
ingredients.raw: acidic fruit juice (lemon, lime, orange, pineapple) to reduce browning

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice bananas into 1/8 to 1/4-inch slices. (Optional) Dip banana slices into fruit juice to reduce browning.
Sprinkle with cinnamon or other flavorings if desired.
Dry until pieces bend like thick leather and no longer feel sticky.
Oven Instructions: Set oven to lowest temperature possible (175 to 200 °F).
Use convection bake if available.
Arrange banana slices in a single layer on a wire rack or baking sheet.
A wire rack will help the banana dry faster.
A baking sheet takes longer and pieces need to be turned part way through drying.
Drying takes 1 to 3 hours.
Dehydrator Instructions: Arrange banana slices in a single layer on dehydrator racks.
Set dehydrator to 135 °F.
Drying takes 6 to 12 hours.
Cool.
Store in an airtight container or bag.
recipes.name: Dried Bananas
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using our Better Baking Mix and getting rid of the rolling and cutting steps means you can enjoy the goodness of homemade biscuits even when you're short on time. See the notes section for fun ways to vary this recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Lightly grease baking sheet.
Add oil and water to the dry mix.
Stir just until all ingredients are wet.
Drop spoonsful 4 inches apart on baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until lightly browned.
recipes.name: Drop Biscuits (from Better Baking Mix)
recipes.notes: Try these variations on this recipe: Herb Biscuits - Add to dry ingredients: 1 teaspoon Italian herb mix. Cheese Biscuits - Add to dry ingredients: 1/3 cup grated sharp cheese. Fruit Scones - Add to the dry ingredients: 1/4 cup sugar, 1/2 cup raisins or dried cranberries, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, or the grated rind of an orange or lemon.
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This treat blends cool, tangy yogurt with the sweetness of apple sauce and spices for a smooth and satisfying dessert or snack!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a small bowl.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled.
Eat and enjoy as a snack or as a dessert.
recipes.name: Dutch Apple Yogurt Dessert
recipes.recipe_by: Fun Food News — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using canned green beans and other pantry items, this side dish is great when you don't have much time. Adding the onion at the end kicks up the flavor a bit.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the beans, and save the liquid from the can in small bowl.
Pour 1/2 cup bean liquid into the saucepan.
Add the cornstarch in the bean liquid.
Stir well.
Add the vinegar and brown sugar.
Put on medium heat and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low.
Add the green beans and onions.
Heat and serve.
recipes.name: Dutch Green Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Kids can enjoy making this healthy, fun, and easy after-school snack using peaches, cottage cheese, and raisins.

ingredients.name: canned peach halves
ingredients.raw: 2 canned peach halves, packed in juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place one peach half, cut side up, in center of plate for nest.
Place 1 tablespoon of cottage cheese in center of nest.
Place raisins on cottage cheese to make eggs.
Enjoy your Eagle Nest.
recipes.name: Eagle Nest
recipes.notes: Adults: If preparing with children, use a can opener to open peaches. Drain juice and discard sharp edged lid.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations — Chickasaw Nation, Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: What should you do with over-ripe bananas? Don't toss them! Freeze them and then throw them in the blender to make this delicious and creamy frozen dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
When bananas have become very ripe, peel and slice them into medium size round pieces.
Place on a plastic wrap covered baking sheet and put in freezer overnight.
Place frozen bananas in a food processor or blender with a small splash of milk (not over 1/4 cup total).
Pulse food processor or blender until bananas begin to break up.
They will be tiny balls of bananas at this point.
Using a spoon or rubber spatula, scrape down the banana mixture.
Continue running the food processor until the mixture is smooth and creamy.
This may take a few minutes.
The ice cream will look and tasted like soft serve ice cream when finished.
Serve in an ice cream cone or in a small bowl with a small ribbon of chocolate syrup on top (optional).
recipes.name: Easiest Banana Ice Cream
recipes.recipe_by: Alabama Cooperative Extension System

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This sweet and nutty squash pairs well with meats and other main dishes.

ingredients.name: maple syrup or honey (can replace with 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper per squash half for a savory flavor)
ingredients.note: can replace with 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper per squash half for a savory flavor
ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoons maple syrup or honey (can replace with 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper per squash half for a savory flavor)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut acorn squash in half and scoop out seeds.
Fill a baking pan with about 1/2 inch of water.
Place the squash in the pan, flesh side up.
If they are lopsided, slice the underside horizontally so the bottom sits flat on the pan.
Add 1 tablespoon maple syrup or honey (or ground pepper if you prefer a savory flavor) to each half and spread evenly across the flesh.
Bake for about 1 hour, or until flesh is tender.
Serve as a side with meat or another main dish.
recipes.name: Easy Baked Acorn Squash
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from American Indian Health and Wellness Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a favorite southwestern dish. Serve with vegetables for lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: (about 30 ounces) no salt added diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (about 30 ounces) no salt added diced tomatoes, drained

ingredients.name: (about 15 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (about 15 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drained

instructions: In a large pan, cook ground beef over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain fat.
Add onion, green pepper, and tomatoes to ground beef and cook until onion turns light brown.
Turn down the heat to a simmer.
Add macaroni, tomato juice, spices, and beans to the pan.
Stir well.
Cover the pan and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Remove pan from heat, stir, and serve hot.
recipes.name: Easy Beef Supper
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations — Adapted from a recipe by Phyllis Blackbear, Cheyenne Arapaho Tribes FDP

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Classic comfort foods with a modern twist, these easy-to-prepare fish sticks and spiced apples will please any finicky youngster's palate.

ingredients.name: For the Spinach Basil Dipping Sauce:
ingredients.raw: For the Spinach Basil Dipping Sauce:

ingredients.name: frozen chopped spinach
ingredients.raw: 1 cup frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained

ingredients.name: frozen pollock
ingredients.raw: 1 pound frozen pollock, or other white fish, such as haddock or cod

instructions: Place rack in center and heat oven to 450 °F.
Spray cookie sheet with cooking spray.
To make dipping sauce, place all ingredients in a blender or food processor; blend or process until smooth.
Cut pollock into strips 1-inch wide (easiest when fish is partially, rather than full, thawed) and place on prepared baking sheet.
Mix breading ingredients (bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and pepper) in a shallow dish or pie pan; place flour and egg whites in separate dishes.
Dip fish sticks in flour, then in egg whites, then breading mix, coating evenly.
Return coated fish sticks to baking sheet, spacing evenly.
Cook fish until it is 145 °F, confirmed with a food thermometer, about 10 to 12 minutes, golden brown, turning as needed.
While fish sticks are baking, cut apples in quarters and core them; slice into smaller wedges (about 12 per apple).
Toss with raisins, pecans, and cinnamon.
Heat butter in medium sauce pan.
Add fruit mix.
Sauté lightly about 3 to 5 minutes.
Apples should still be slightly crisp.
recipes.name: Easy Oven Fish with Spinach Basil Dipping Sauce & Spiced Apples
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 100% fruit juice and green beans or asparagus.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy a taste of the Caribbean with seasoned vegetables, tilapia and pears, baked in no-fuss foil or parchment packets.

ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1" chunks

ingredients.name: green beans (fresh
ingredients.raw: 1 cup green beans (fresh, frozen, or canned)

ingredients.name: tilapia fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound tilapia fillets, fresh, or frozen

ingredients.name: salt-free Caribbean citrus seasoning blend
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon salt-free Caribbean citrus seasoning blend

instructions: Heat oven to 425 °F.
Scrub potatoes under running water, cut into 1-inch chunks.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes with other vegetables, seasonings, and olive oil.
Spread mix in a 2-quart baking dish and place in oven.
Roast until potatoes and other vegetables are tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
About 15 minutes after the potato dish was placed in the oven, put in a baking sheet with fish packets, prepared as follows: Brush fish with olive oil, coat with seasoning blend.
Place each filet in the center of a square of aluminum foil (or substitute foil with parchment paper).
Cut pears into quarters and core; slice into thin wedges (about 8 to 12 per pear).Top fish with pear wedges.
Bring the foil over the fish and fruit.
Fold and pinch the seams.
Place foil packets on a baking sheet.
Bake about 20 minutes, until tilapia is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, confirmed with a food thermometer, and fruit is tender.
To serve, carefully open the packet, slide contents onto individual serving plates, and add roasted vegetables.
recipes.name: Easy Oven Packet Caribbean Tilapia with Pears and Carnival Roasted Potatoes
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Making pizza at home has never been easier! Enjoy this recipe using our Better Baking Mix with adults or kids of all ages. Add veggie sticks and fruit for dessert for a great weeknight dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F.
Grease a 12x15 inch or larger baking sheet, or 12-inch pizza pan.
Measure mix into a bowl.
Add oil and water.
Stir to form soft dough.
Transfer dough onto baking sheet.
Sprinkle with flour.
Dip fingers in flour and pat dough into a circle about 11-12 inches across.
Spread pizza crust with tomato sauce.
Leave about 1/2 inch around edge with no sauce.
Sprinkle with onion, seasoning and cheese Bake 10-12 minutes until edges are brown and cheese is melted and starting to brown.
Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Easy-As-A-Mix Pizza (from Better Baking Mix)
recipes.notes: Use leftover tomato sauce from a can within 5 days, or freeze to use later.
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Keep this seasoning mix on hand and use it whenever you want to boost flavor without adding salt.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients.
Store in airtight container.
Use in recipes as indicated.
recipes.name: Eating Smart Seasoning Mix
recipes.notes: Recipe makes about 2.5 cups, one serving size = 1/4 cup. This recipe is used in the Chili Tomato Macaroni and Beef & Potatoes recipes.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart Being Active Recipes — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
