Add the lemon and lime zest and remaining 1 tablespoon of oil.
Mix in cilantro and jalapeno pepper, if desired.
With a spoon, mix massaged kale with yogurt dressing.
Toss pumpkin seeds over salad.
recipes.name: Kale Salad with Yogurt Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Nuts and raisins add protein and fiber to this bright green dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, toast nuts for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in frying pan on medium heat.
Add garlic and kale to frying pan and cook for 4 minutes.
Add raisins and nuts and cook for 1 minute more.
Add salt to taste (optional)
recipes.name: Kale with Nuts and Raisins
recipes.notes: Walnuts used for costing and nutrition analysis.
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart. Be Fit. — University of Maryland Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This traditionally Kurdish dish is delicious, fresh, and flavorful! The beef dumplings are enjoyed in a soup that is loaded with Swiss Chard. This will be your newest family favorite!

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound ground beef, 85% lean (coarsely ground, if available)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Fry ground beef in a small amount of oil.
Prepare the dough by mixing matzo meal, semolina, water, and salt.
Wet hands and shape into walnut-sized pieces.
Roll out dough into a small circle and fill with 1 Tablespoon of meat.
Seal the dough.
Continue until all the dough and meat is used.
In a large pot, heat a small amount of oil and fry garlic until golden.
Add the scallions and Swiss chard.
Mix well.
Cook about 10 minutes.
Cover with water and continue to cook until boiling.
Add lemon juice, to taste (optional).
Add stuffed dough to soup and cook 15 more minutes.
recipes.name: Kibbeh Khamoustah
recipes.notes: Kibbeh Khamoustah is a Kurdish dish. Kibbeh, or dumplings, are stuffed with meat, traditionally lamb or beef, and served with soup.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This recipe features crispy, baked taco cups filled with seasoned ground pork, cheese, and fresh toppings. These fun and easy-to-make mini tacos are perfect for a quick weeknight dinner or a kid-friendly meal that the whole family will enjoy.

ingredients.name: yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and diced

instructions: In a large skillet over medium heat, add oil and chopped onion.
Stir occasionally until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ground pork, peppers and spinach.
Stir to crumble meat, cook until no longer pink, about 6 minutes.
Return to heat and add seasonings, stirring to combine.
Brown meat 2–3 minutes more and until internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F.
Remove from heat and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine tomatoes with lime juice and fresh cilantro.
Season with salt if desired.
Arrange 12 serving cups on a platter and fill with cooked pork mixture.
Top with your choice of toppings and tomatoes.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Kid-Friendly Taco Cups
recipes.notes: Optional ingredients: Avocado, corn, jalapeños, black beans, salsa, nonfat Greek yogurt
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the National Pork Board, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Looking for a healthy snack for game day? This Layered Black Bean Dip is colorful, wholesome, and tasty. Kids in the kitchen can help with the mashing, mixing, and layering. Paired with veggie sticks or baked whole wheat tortilla chips, this is recipe is a winner!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash beans and mix with onion powder, dried oregano, garlic powder, and cayenne pepper.
Spread on a serving dish.
Top with salsa, sour cream, green onions, and grated cheese.
recipes.name: Layered Black Bean Dip
recipes.notes: Serve as a dip for raw vegetables such as celery, carrot sticks, and pepper slices.
recipes.recipe_by: Good Food Cookbook — Cornell Cooperative Extension of Onondaga County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Light and flavorful, this salad is easily doubled for entertaining or for introducing children to new vegetables! Bright and colorful beets, with crunchy carrots, cucumbers, and sunflower seeds are an easy make this salad an easy appetizer or side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lay lettuce leaves on a flat surface.
Top each leaf with all ingredients: cucumbers, carrots, beets, and sunflower seeds.
Drizzle each leaf with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Slowly roll the leaf with all ingredients.
recipes.name: Leaf Finger Salad
recipes.recipe_by: University of California at Davis — Children's Garden Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spinach, tofu, and sesame seeds are a fun and delicious combination, and can be made in minutes! A quick and delicious side dish!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tofu.
Dice tofu into 1-inch cubes.
Tear spinach into bite-sized pieces.
In a large pan, heat oil and saute tofu cubes for a few minutes.
Move tofu to the center of the pan.
Add spinach, and soy sauce.
Mix.
Cover pan and cook until spinach is wilted.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds.
recipes.name: Leafy Tofu
recipes.notes: You may use other dark green leafy vegetables.
recipes.recipe_by: Lifeskills in Food Education, Food Skills Cookbook — University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension — Food Stamps Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Leftover turkey, is jazzed up with cheese, cream of mushroom soup, and celery in this hearty casserole dish! Use leftover turkey that has been properly handled and stored.

ingredients.name: reduced-sodium cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can reduced-sodium cream of mushroom soup

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Lightly coat a 9x9x2 inch baking dish with vegetable spray.
Cut 6 slices of bread (fresh or day-old) into 1-inch cubes and place half into the bottom of a baking dish.
In a bowl, combine turkey, onion, celery, mayonnaise, and pepper.
Spoon mixture over bread crumbs.
Place remaining bread cubes over turkey mixture and press down slightly with spoon.
Combine eggs and milk and pour mixture over cubes.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
When ready to bake, preheat oven to 325 °F.
Spoon soup over top of casserole.
Spread one teaspoon margarine on side of each slice of bread.
Cut buttered bread into 1/2-inch cubes and sprinkle on top of casserole.
Bake for 60 minutes or until knife inserted in middle comes out clean.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheese over top.
Let stand 15 minutes before cutting and serving.
recipes.name: Leftover Turkey Casserole
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A light and flavorful cake, packed with sweet and tangy lemon flavor! The lemon glaze takes this cake to the next level!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Mix first five ingredients together in mixing bowl.
Combine yogurt, lemon peel, oil, egg yolk, and milk together and stir into dry ingredients just until blended.
Whip egg whites with mixer until stiff.
Fold into corn meal mixture.
Pour into round 9 inch cake pan coated with nonstick cooking spray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until corn cake tests done.
For optional lemon glaze: Over low heat blend lemon juice together with powdered sugar.
Pierce cake top repeatedly with fork.
Slowly pour glaze evenly over the top.
recipes.name: Lemon Corn Cake
recipes.recipe_by: Celebrate Health with a Lowfat Fiesta — California Department of Health Services — California Project LEAN

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this different way to eat Brussels sprouts. The Greek yogurt combined with the dill makes the perfect creamy, fresh vegetable dish.

ingredients.name: plain Greek yogurt
ingredients.raw: 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, fat free

ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts
ingredients.raw: 2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved lengthwise

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix yogurt, dill weed, lemon juice, and salt.
Set aside.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, sauté sprouts (cut side down) in margarine or butter until they begin to brown.
Stir sprouts and add water.
Cover the pan and steam until the water is gone and sprouts are tender crisp, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Mix sprouts with lemon dill sauce.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Lemon Dill Brussels Sprouts
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: With a mix of flaked salmon, breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, and egg, a simple fillet transforms into a tasty pan-seared patty!

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: can also use dried egg mix
ingredients.raw: 1 egg, slightly beaten (can also use dried egg mix)

ingredients.name: frozen salmon
ingredients.raw: 7 ounces frozen salmon, thawed, drained, and finely chopped (optional to remove the skin)

instructions: Mix breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, egg, and lemon pepper in a medium bowl.
Add salmon and mix.
Measure 1/3 cup of salmon mixture (packed) and form into a round patty.
Repeat until you have five salmon patties.
Spray a skillet with cooking spray and set stove to medium heat.
Place the salmon patties in the skillet and cook until light brown, 5–7 minutes.
Flip the patties and cook on the other side until brown.
Salmon should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145°F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
recipes.name: Lemon Pepper Salmon Patties
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Chickasaw Nation Nutrition Services, Get Fresh Initiative

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Potatoes are cut and coated with a blend of lemon juice, garlic, and oil and then baked until flaky and golden brown. Brush potatoes with remaining lemon mixture and serve warm.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375 °F.
Combine lemon juice, garlic clove, and oil.
Set aside 1 tablespoon.
Peel the potatoes and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Pour the lemon juice mixture in a casserole dish or small baking pan to coat the bottom of the dish.
Place the potatoes in the baking dish and coat with the lemon juice mixture.
Bake about 30 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
After removing from the oven, brush the remaining lemon juice mixture on the potatoes.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Lemon Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tangy spinach side dish can be prepared in a flash! Lemon juice adds extra flavor to this dish. Enjoy as a side to your favorite entree!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the spinach.
Trim off the stems.
Put the spinach, black pepper, and lemon juice in a pan.
Cook over medium heat.
Let the spinach boil for about 3 minutes, until just tender.
recipes.name: Lemon Spinach
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Light and refreshing, this tasty dessert, packed with fat-free vanilla yogurt, graham crackers, and mandarin oranges, can be made in minutes! This recipe doubles easily if serving a crowd.

ingredients.name: mandarin orange
ingredients.note: 4 ounce, slices, drained or your favorite fruit

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine vanilla yogurt and pudding mix; gently stir together.
Layer bottom of individual dishes with crushed graham crackers.
Reserve a few crumbs to sprinkle on top.
Pour pudding mixture over cracker crumbs.
Top with mandarin orange slices or your favorite fruit.
Sprinkle with remaining crumbs.
recipes.name: Lemon Velvet Supreme
recipes.recipe_by: Choices: Steps Toward Health — University of Massachusetts Extension — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fresh, single serving of lemonade that is perfect for a hot summer day. Only one lemon is needed for this recipe. Enjoy!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut lemon in half crosswise.
Place lemon half on juicer.
Push and twist to squeeze out the juice.
Pour juice into glass.
Add about 3/4 cup water.
Add sugar, stirring to mix ingredients.
Create-a-Flavor Changes Squeeze one-half each lemon and lime.
Squeeze one-half each lemon and orange.
Add 1/4 cup apple juice concentrate and leave out the sugar.
Use 1/4 cup seltzer water and 1/2 cup water.
recipes.name: Lemonade
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun -- A Pyramid of Snacks — Cornell Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A big pot of lentils, tomatoes, and pearl barley simmer into this hearty soup. A great "make ahead" for quick meals and easy clean up.

ingredients.name: 14.5 ounce low-sodium whole peeled tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can 14.5 ounce low-sodium whole peeled tomatoes

instructions: Place a large soup pot on the stove and add lentils, scallions, carrots, celery, oregano, barley, and water.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for one hour.
Add the tomatoes and continue cooking about 45 minutes.
Just before serving, add vinegar.
recipes.name: Lentil Barley Soup
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lentils, tomatoes, and ground beef are a winning combination in the lentil chili. This recipe packs 9 grams of fiber per serving. Flavorful and filling.

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cans tomatoes, low-sodium, diced or crushed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, brown beef over medium-high heat, breaking it into bite sized pieces.
Drain fat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add lentils, tomatoes, chili powder, and cumin.
Cook for about 1 hour until flavors are blended.
Serve hot, topped with your favorite chili toppings.
recipes.name: Lentil Chili
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This soup starts with plenty of vegetables - carrots, celery, sweet potato, zucchini, and tomatoes and hearty lentils simmered to make a rich and tasty meal for a hungry family.

ingredients.name: sweet potato
ingredients.raw: 1 sweet potato, peeled and diced into 1/4-inch pieces

ingredients.name: canned diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cups canned diced tomatoes, no salt added

instructions: Put a soup pot on the stove over medium-high heat.
When the pot is hot, add the oil.
Add onion and garlic and cook about 7 minutes until golden.
Add carrots, celery, sweet potato, and zucchini and cook about 10 minutes until slightly tender.
Add tomatoes, lentils, water, and chicken bouillon cube and bring to a boil over high heat.
Turn the heat down to low, cover and cook 40 minutes.
Add the kale and cook an additional 20 minutes.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
recipes.name: Lentil Minestrone
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This wholesome lentil soup is simple yet satisfying. Using vegetable broth makes it a delicious vegetarian option.

ingredients.name: large red
ingredients.raw: 1 large red, yellow, or white onion, chopped

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth
ingredients.raw: 8 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onions, carrots, red pepper flakes, and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, bay leaf, salt and pepper and stir well.
Add rinsed lentils and broth and simmer until lentils are soft, about 30 minutes.
Keep checking lentils until they are done.
Season with additional salt and pepper, if desired.
recipes.name: Lentil Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Bronson Wellness Center, Adapted from Easy Lentil Soup — Bronson Healthcare - Michigan

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this hearty spaghetti sauce over your favorite pasta for a quick, easy, and delicious dinner!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large sauce pan brown meat.
Drain.
Add onion and garlic to drained meat.
Cook until onions are soft but not brown.
Add cooked lentils and spaghetti sauce and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and cook gently for 15 minutes.
Serve sauce over hot cooked spaghetti noodles.
recipes.name: Lentil Spaghetti Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lentils, carrots, and tomatoes are a savory and satisfying combination in this delicious and easy to prepare stew. Enjoy with a side of your favorite citrus fruit.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion.
Cook for 3 minutes, or until tender.
Stir in garlic powder, carrots, lentils, tomatoes, water, and chili powder.
Simmer, uncovered, for about 20 minutes or until lentils are tender.
recipes.name: Lentil Stew
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lentils and raisins are an surprising and delicious duo in these sweet and savory tacos. Green peppers add extra flavor and texture. Enjoy with a tossed salad on the side.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook lentils in 3 cups water for 10 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add more water if necessary.
Serve with corn tortillas.
Can also be served over rice or noodles.
recipes.name: Lentil Tacos
recipes.notes: Alternate seasoning: 2 tablespoons taco seasoning instead of the other spices.
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lentils, potatoes, carrots, and peas are combined with seasonings and olive oil to make this savory side dish. This salad pairs well with your favorite baked or broiled meat, fish, or tofu entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil 1 cup water in a saucepan.
Add the lentils.
Cook for 20 minutes over low heat until tender, then drain.
Cook the peas for 3 minutes in another saucepan.
Then remove from heat.
Rinse and drain the peas.
Wash, peel, and shred the carrots.
Put the cooked lentils, sliced potatoes, peas, and shredded carrots in a bowl.
Put the parsley, vinegar, mustard, and olive oil in another bowl.
Stir well.
Pour the dressing over the lentil vegetable salad.
recipes.name: Lentil Vegetable Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this hearty vegetable and lentil soup -- packed with lentils, celery, onion, and tomato sauce -- on a cold winter's evening.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sort lentils.
Place lentils in deep pot with water.
Bring to a boil and add all ingredients except vinegar.
Reduce heat and cover.
Cook slowly for 1 hour, adding more water if necessary.
Add vinegar.
Remove garlic and bay leaf before serving.
recipes.name: Lentil Vegetable Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe Collection — University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This fun, kid-friendly breakfast is a healthy twist on an ice cream classic.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and cut the banana in half, lengthwise.
Place the banana on a plate.
Top banana with yogurt and sprinkle with cereal and fruit.
recipes.name: Lickety Split Banana Split
recipes.recipe_by: Nebraska SNAP-Ed

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Adding more whole grains to your diet is easy with this tasty pancake recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat griddle.
In medium bowl, stir or sift dry ingredients together.
In a separate bowl, beat egg, buttermilk, brown sugar, and oil together.
Stir into dry ingredients just until moistened; batter should be slightly lumpy.
Pour 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto sprayed or seasoned hot griddle.
Flip the pancake when bubbles appear on surface; turn only once.
recipes.name: Light as a Feather Whole Wheat Pancakes
recipes.recipe_by: Now Serving Whole Grains — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A simply marinated lean beef flank steak grilled alongside poblano peppers stuffed with whole-grain brown rice, black beans and tomatoes. A tasty, complete meal on the grill or in the skillet.

ingredients.name: diced tomatoes with green chiles
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cans diced tomatoes with green chiles

ingredients.name: fresh lime juice for marinade
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup fresh lime juice for marinade

ingredients.name: low sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can low sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: medium poblano chile peppers (about 4 inches long)
ingredients.raw: 6 medium poblano chile peppers (about 4 inches long)

ingredients.name: optional toppings: toasted
ingredients.raw: optional toppings: toasted, shelled pepitas (pumpkin seeds), lime wedges, crumbled queso fresco

instructions: Drain tomatoes, reserving juice for marinade.
Set aside diced tomatoes with green chiles.
Combine reserved tomato juice, 1/2 cup cilantro, lime juice and olive oil in medium bowl.
Cover and refrigerate 1/3 cup marinade for rice.
Place beef Flank Steak and remaining marinade in food-safe plastic bag; turn steak to coat.
Close bag securely and marinate in refrigerator 6 hours or as long as overnight, turning occasionally.
Combine rice, reserved 1/3 cup marinade, diced tomatoes, black beans and remaining 1/4 cup cilantro in medium bowl.
Season with salt and pepper, as desired.
Set aside.
Cook's Tip: Two cups leftover cooked rice or 1 package (8.8 ounces) ready-to-serve whole grain brown rice can be substituted.
Cut slit lengthwise down 1 side of each poblano pepper to create pocket, leaving stem and tip intact.
Make another small crosswise cut just below the stem to form T-shaped opening.
Remove and discard seeds and membranes, being careful to keep peppers intact.
Spoon rice mixture evenly into peppers.
Wrap each tightly in aluminum foil to seal.
Remove steak from marinade; discard marinade.
Place steak in center grid over medium, ash-covered coals; arrange peppers around steak.
Grill steak, covered, 11 to 16 minutes (over medium heat on preheated gas grill 16 to 21 minutes) for medium rare to medium doneness, turning occasionally.
Grill peppers, covered, 25 to 30 minutes (20 to 25 minutes on gas grill) or until peppers are tender and filling is heated through, turning occasionally.
Carve steak across grain into thin slices.
Remove peppers from foil.
Serve peppers with steaks and toppings as desired.
recipes.name: Lime-Marinated Flank Steak with Stuffed Poblano Peppers
recipes.notes: Cook's Tip: Two cups leftover cooked rice or 1 package (8.8 ounces) ready-to-serve whole grain brown rice can be substituted. For more information on degree of doneness, safe food handling, and beef safety, visit: https://www.beefitswhatsfordinner.com
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the National Cattlemen's Beef Association, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this healthier version of a soul food favorite.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl, mix sliced okra, oil, salt, and pepper.
Coat a large fry pan with cooking spray.
Heat over medium heat, and add okra mixture, turning often with a wooden spoon or spatula.
Cook until okra is browned, about 10 minutes.
Serve with hot sauce or favorite relish.
recipes.name: Lite Fried Okra
recipes.recipe_by: Champions for Change Recipes — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Making your own salad dressings is a simple way to add a fresh, homemade taste. Try this one today!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a pint sized jar with tight fitting lid.
Shake vigorously to blend ingredients.
Store refrigerated.
recipes.name: Lite Italian Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up canned green beans with peppers, onions, and tomatoes!

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium green beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium green beans, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the green pepper and celery.
Drain the liquid from the green beans.
Rinse with water.
Put the green beans in a saucepan.
Add enough water to cover them Cook the green beans on low heat until tender.
Then drain off the water.
Combine all the ingredients in a skillet.
Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, until the celery is tender and the food is hot.
recipes.name: Louisiana Green Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dressing is low in calories but not flavor. Dress up any salad with this tasty dressing.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients.
Whisk or stir together.
Store in refrigerator.
recipes.name: Low Calorie Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A cool and tangy dressing or dip that’s perfect for your next salad or veggie tray.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix and stir all ingredients in small container.
Store covered in refrigerator and use within 1 week.
recipes.name: Low Fat Creamy Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A blender transforms canned beans, herbs, and spices into this delectable ranch style dip!

ingredients.name: great northern beans
ingredients.note: 15 ounce, rinsed and drained, low sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend the beans and garlic in a blender, adding enough water for the desired consistency.
Blend for 2 minutes to make it silky smooth.
Use a spatula to scrape the mixture into a medium bowl.
Stir in the yogurt, cayenne, chives, parsley, and tarragon, salt, and lemon juice.
Serve in a bowl.
recipes.name: Low Fat Ranch Dip
recipes.recipe_by: National Cancer Institute (NCI) — 5 A Day for Better Health Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bell peppers, tomatoes, and beans add color and flavor to this meal, while the red pepper flakes add a little bit of heat.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: cooked macaroni
ingredients.raw: 2 cups cooked macaroni, without salt or fat added

instructions: Wash hands with warm water and soap.
Peel and finely chop the garlic.
Core, seed, and finely chop the bell pepper.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and bell pepper.
Cook for one minute.
Do not let garlic brown.
Add diced tomatoes (do not drain) and red pepper flakes.
Cover the skillet and lower heat.
Cook for 10 minutes or until sauce is slightly thickened.
Add beans and cooked macaroni to skillet and cook 5 minutes or until heated through.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Mac and Beans Medley
recipes.recipe_by: Champions for Change Recipes — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Broccoli gives flavor, texture, and nutrients to this creamy spin-off of the traditional mac and cheese dish. Try this with roasted squash or sweet potatoes in the fall or winter, roasted beets in the spring, or a tomato salad in the summer for a meal with tasty seasonal veggies!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook macaroni, following the instructions on the package.
Drain the cooked macaroni and return to the pan.
While the macaroni is still warm, sprinkle in the flour and stir thoroughly.
Over medium heat, slowly stir the milk into the macaroni.
Add the cheese and pepper.
Stir over medium heat until the milk and cheese thicken into a creamy sauce, approximately 7-10 minutes.
Stir in the broccoli; heat thoroughly.
Taste; add a small amount of salt, if needed.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Macaroni & Cheese with Broccoli
recipes.notes: Fresh or frozen broccoli can be used.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This savory soup is packed with tomatoes, green beans, and chickpeas. The recipe also doubles easily if leftovers are desired or if you are making it for a large group.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, bring broth and water to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Add macaroni, celery flakes, and oregano.
Simmer 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add stewed tomatoes, green beans, chickpeas, and garlic powder.
Simmer 5 minutes, or until macaroni and beans are tender.
recipes.name: Macaroni Chick-Pea Soup
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This main dish is magically delicious. Use whatever vegetables you have on hand for this fun recipe.

ingredients.name: vegetables
ingredients.raw: 2 cups vegetables, frozen, no salt added

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook onion in oil (or cook with vegetables).
Cook vegetables (or use leftovers).
Drain well.
Grease round pie pan or 8x8 inch baking dish.
Spread cooked vegetables in pan.
Spread cheese on top of vegetables.
Mix milk, eggs, and baking mix.
Pour over vegetables and cheese.
Bake at 350 °F for 35 minutes, until a safe internal temperature has been reached and a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean.
recipes.name: Magic Crust Quiche
recipes.notes: Suggest preparing with frozen broccoli (shown) or spinach.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Whip up this recipe ahead of time and use it in just about any recipe that calls for baking mix.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dry milk, flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in margarine with two knives until the mixture looks like cornmeal.
Store in a dry, closed container in the refrigerator for up to 6 weeks.
recipes.name: Magic Mix
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe Collection — University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The whole family will love making this as much as they love eating it! Pineapple, grapes, and bananas add flavor and texture to this creamy and delicious dessert.

ingredients.name: (20 ounces) pineapple chunks
ingredients.raw: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks, juice packed

ingredients.name: seedless grapes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup seedless grapes, red or green

ingredients.name: (3.5 ounces) instant pudding mix
ingredients.raw: 1 package (3.5 ounces) instant pudding mix, lemon or vanilla

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain off the juice from the canned pineapples.
Put chunks in a large bowl.
Rinse the grapes and drain.
Add the grapes to the bowl.
Peel the bananas and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Add to the bowl.
Pour the milk over the fruit.
While slowly stirring the fruit mixture, sprinkle in the pudding mix.
Let the mixture stand for 5 minutes and serve.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Magical Fruit Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mango, berries, spinach, and feta cheese make for a colorful twist on pasta salad, with the perfect balance of sweet and tangy.

ingredients.name: (4 oz) whole-wheat rotini pasta
ingredients.raw: 1 cup (4 oz) whole-wheat rotini pasta, uncooked

instructions: In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients; set aside.
Boil water and cook rotini according to package instructions.
Drain cooked rotini and rinse in cool water.
While rotini is cooking, cut mango into chunks, removing peel and pit.
Place salad ingredients in a large bowl; drizzle with vinaigrette.
Toss gently.
recipes.name: Mango Berry Rotini Salad
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestion: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet, ripe mangoes are the basis for this refreshing and quick chilled summer soup. It's a no-stove recipe that's perfect when outdoor temperatures rise.
instructions: Cut all but one half of mango into chunks, removing peel and pit; chill remaining mango half for use with garnish.
Slice off 1/4 of the cucumber and chill for use with garnish.
Coarsely chop remaining 3/4 of the cucumber.
Place chopped mango, cucumber, onion, and pepper (optional) in blender or food processor with lime juice and water.
Purée until smooth.
Blend in yogurt.
Chill until ready to serve.
About 15 to 30 minutes before serving, prepare garnish.
Dice chilled mango half, removing peel and pit; dice remaining cucumber.
Mix mango and cucumber dices with cilantro.
To serve, top bowls of soup with garnish.
recipes.name: Mango Cucumber Soup
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% apple juice.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This sweet and tangy salsa pairs perfectly with grilled or baked fish or chicken. The recipe doubles easily if making for a crowd.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Serve with baked tortilla chips.
recipes.name: Mango Salsa
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The sweetness of fresh mango combined with savory pepper and onion and the zest of lime give this salsa a balance of flavors that are refreshing and crisp. Serve this appetizer with baked tortilla chips or whole grain crackers for a tasty snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the mango, be sure to remove the seed.
Cut the pepper and onion into small pieces.
Mix all the ingredients together.
recipes.name: Mango Salsa
recipes.recipe_by: Iowa Department of Public Health, Adapted from Easy Mango Salsa — Iowa Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Have a fruity and frosty treat! Banana, mango, and milk are blended together to make this delicious drink.

ingredients.name: fresh pitted mango
ingredients.note: or 4 Tablespoons of frozen mango juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients into a blender.
Blend until foamy.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Mango Shake
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this hearty chowder full of carrots, tomatoes, potatoes, and clams that can be easily made in a slow cooker.

ingredients.name: (6.5 ounces each) clams
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (6.5 ounces each) clams, chopped and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes well to remove any eyes or blemishes.
In a slow cooker, combine all ingredients; stir.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or until the vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf and peppercorns before serving.
recipes.name: Manhattan Clam Chowder
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet potatoes, maple syrup, orange juice, and yogurt are a winning combination in this easy dish that can be made in the microwave.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prick potato skins with a fork.
Microwave on high for 3 to 4 minute until soft and easily pierced with a knife.
Scoop out the pulp into a medium bowl.
Mash the pulp and stir in the yogurt, maple syrup, and orange juice.
Transfer to a microwave safe serving bowl and microwave for 1 to 2 minutes to heat through.
recipes.name: Maple Sweet Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Canned tomatoes and fresh spinach come together beautifully in this quick and tasty marinara recipe.

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounce) crushed tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 4 cans (14.5 ounce) crushed tomatoes, low sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the vegetables.
Collect, dice, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic powder.
Cook for about 10 minutes or until the onion is clear.
Add the carrots and celery and cook for 5 minutes until slightly soft.
Add the tomatoes and Italian seasoning.
Stir until all ingredients are mixed together.
Taste, and add a little bit of salt and pepper if desired.
Turn the heat to medium-high and bring sauce to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for at least 30 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until spinach wilts.*.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Eat within 3 to 5 days. * For a smoother sauce, blend in a blender or food processor.
recipes.name: Marinara Sauce
recipes.notes: This recipe freezes well. Defrost in the refrigerator overnight, then reheat and eat!
recipes.recipe_by: Colorado State University Extension, Adapted from Easy Marinara Sauce

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tangy, marinated beef is full of flavor and pairs well with roasted potatoes, steamed broccoli, and fresh, sliced tomatoes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a cutting board and sharp knife, cut round steak across the grain into thin strips about 1/2 inch wide and 2 to 3 inches long.
In a medium glass mixing bowl, combine garlic, lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, salt, and pepper.
Add beef strips and stir to coat with the oil mixture (marinade sauce).
Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 2 hours.
In a medium skillet over medium-high heat, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil for 1-2 minutes until hot.
Drain marinade from beef.
Put beef in skillet, stir and cook for 5 to 7 minutes or until meat is thoroughly browned.
recipes.name: Marinated Beef
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Beans, celery, and onion make for a delicious marinated salad that the whole family will enjoy. Try it with our Lite Italian Dressing .
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the canned beans.
To reduce the sodium rinse the beans under running water Peel and chop the onion.
In a large bowl, combine the cannellini beans, green beans, kidney beans, onion, and celery.
Pour the Italian dressing over the vegetables and toss lightly.
Cover the bowl and marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour.
The salad can be left in the refrigerator over night.
Drain before serving.
recipes.name: Marinated Three-Bean Salad
recipes.notes: Double the recipe to use the entire can of beans. Garnish with parsley if desired.
recipes.recipe_by: The Texas A&M University System — Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A twist on a classic comfort food, this combination of parsnips and potatoes is sure to hit the spot. This dish can be made with substitutions: like using yogurt instead of milk. Enjoy it your way!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub parsnips and potatoes under running water and peel.
Cut into similar size pieces.
In a medium saucepan, cover the vegetables pieces with cold water.
Bring the water to a boil and simmer until vegetables are soft, 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain the vegetables and mash.
Stir in milk, salt, pepper, garlic powder and margarine.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Mashed Parsnips and Potatoes
recipes.notes: Try other seasonings such as parsley, thyme or nutmeg.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mashed sweet potatoes are an easy and nutritious side dish that can accompany any entrée. A great idea to try in place of traditional mashed potatoes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and peel the potatoes.
Cut them into slices that are 3/4 inch thick.
Put them in a saucepan with enough water to cover the potatoes.
Bring the water to a boil on medium heat.
Cook the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes until they’re soft.
Drain the water.
Put the potatoes in a medium bowl.
Use a fork or potato masher to mash the potatoes.
Mix in the thyme, salt, and pepper.
recipes.name: Mashed Sweet Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This baking mix is an ingredient in several recipes such as this recipe for Crustless Pumpkin Pie.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, dry milk, baking powder, and salt.
Mix thoroughly.
Cut in shortening with pastry blender or two knives until mixture looks like course cornmeal.
Store in covered containers in the refrigerator.
recipes.name: Master Mix Oregon
recipes.notes: The final product of this recipe is intended to be used as an ingredient in other recipes. It is not intended as a ready-to-eat product.
recipes.recipe_by: Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Kugel is a baked pudding or casserole. Matzo meal kugel is traditionally served on the Jewish holiday of Passover. This dish is easy to make and can be served as a side dish or a dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine eggs and sugar; beat well.
Add milk and melted butter; mix well.
Stir in matzo meal and salt.
Pour into buttered 11x13 inch pan.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour (don't over bake).
Cut into slices.
Can be served hot or cold.
recipes.name: Matzo Meal Kugel (Pudding)
recipes.recipe_by: Osteoporosis Facts and Recipes — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mixed vegetables, meatballs, and brown rice make a delicious and hearty soup that will warm you up on a cold winter night.

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef or chicken bouillon cubes
ingredients.raw: 3 low-sodium beef or chicken bouillon cubes

ingredients.name: medium onion
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium onion, peeled and finely chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, combine water, rice, bouillon cubes, and oregano.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Stir to dissolve bouillon.
Reduce heat to low and simmer.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, mix ground meat, tomato, onion, egg, and salt.
Form into 12 meatballs.
Add meatballs to broth mixture and simmer 30 minutes.
Add vegetables.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes or until meatballs are cooked and rice and vegetables are tender.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Meatball Soup
recipes.recipe_by: California Champions for Change Lunch Recipes — California Department of Public Health — Network for a Healthy California
recipes.serving_size: 1/2 cup broth mixture and 3 large meatballs

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this flavorful meatloaf without ever turning on your oven. This delicious single serving meal can be prepared in the microwave.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients and stir to mix.
Spray microwave-safe mug with cooking spray.
Pat beef mixture into mug.
Make a small hold in center, all the way to the bottom.
Microwave on HIGH (100%) for 3 minutes or until done.
recipes.name: Meatloaf in a Mug
recipes.notes: Food Safety Note: Cook until the internal temperature is 160 °F when measured with a meat thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: Spend Smart. Eat Smart. — Iowa State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Here is a delicious recipe for potatoes stuffed with meat, vegetables, and cheese that will become a favorite at your home. Enjoy this dish with a side or dessert of your favorite fruit.

ingredients.name: turkey
ingredients.note: or use cooked chicken, beef, or pork

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes.
Remove any bad spots.
Do not peel.
Cut each in half, lengthwise.
In a covered saucepan, boil potatoes in just enough water to cover the pieces.
When they are fork-tender (about 15 to 20 minutes), remove from heat and drain.
Set aside. (Note: you can also pierce whole potatoes with a knife or fork in several places and cook in microwave without water until fork tender, then cut each in half, lengthwise).
Meanwhile, in a large skillet sprayed with non-stick cooking spray, combine cooked meat, broccoli, onion, carrots and water.
Boil until vegetables are fork tender - about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to low.
In a jar with a tight fitting lid, combine milk, flour and pepper.
Shake well.
Stir flour mixture into meat mixture until well blended.
Stir in cheese.
Cook over low heat about 5 minutes longer or until sauce thickens, stirring frequently.
To serve, place 2 potato halves on each plate and mash the middle somewhat.
Spoon about one third cup of the meat mixture over each potato half Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Meaty Stuffed Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series — Kansas State University Research and Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This refreshing salad starts with cooked chicken, white beans, cucumber, and onion with a splash of fresh lemon juice, oil and seasonings for a delicious combination. Try it with tuna and chopped tomatoes for variety.

ingredients.name: skinless chicken
ingredients.note: cooked and diced into 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.raw: 1 cup skinless chicken, cooked and diced into 1/2 inch pieces

ingredients.name: 15.5 ounce can low-sodium white beans
ingredients.raw: 1 15.5 ounce can low-sodium white beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.note: peeled and diced into 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.raw: 1 cucumber, peeled and diced into 1/2 inch pieces

ingredients.name: red or white onion
ingredients.raw: 1/4 red or white onion, chopped into 1/2 inch pieces

ingredients.name: dried basil or parsley leaves
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon dried basil or parsley leaves

instructions: Put everything in the bowl and gently toss.
Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days.
recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken and White Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A wonderful recipe to enjoy in the summer when eggplant is in season. Top this side dish with freshly ground black pepper if desired.

ingredients.name: low-sodium pizza or spaghetti sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 cup low-sodium pizza or spaghetti sauce

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and remove the stem end, and slice the eggplants into 1/2-inch slices.
Spray a baking pan with vegetable oil spray and lay the eggplant in the pan in a single layer.
Spoon low-sodium pizza or spaghetti sauce on each slice.
Bake 30 minutes in the preheated oven.
Stir the yogurt and garlic together.
Drizzle the sauce in thin lines on each of the eggplant slices before serving.
You can do this easily by putting the sauce in a plastic squirt bottle or using a spoon.
Serve immediately as an entrée or side dish.
recipes.name: Mediterranean Roasted Eggplant with Tomato Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Do Yourself a Flavor by Graham Kerr — Arizona Health Zone

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this fresh take on tuna salad. It's delicious with walnuts, garbanzo beans, veggies, and a lemony vinaigrette dressing.

ingredients.name: 15.5-ounce can garbanzo beans
ingredients.raw: 1 15.5-ounce can garbanzo beans, low sodium, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place walnuts, onion, bell pepper, parsley, tuna, and garbanzo beans in a large bowl and mix lightly.
Whisk together lemon juice and olive oil and drizzle over salad; stir lightly to coat ingredients with dressing.
Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Place lettuce on a platter or divide between 8 salad bowls.
Top with equal amounts of salad.
recipes.name: Mediterranean Tuna Antipasti Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the California Walnut Commission, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: My family’s recipes are a sacred tradition, especially our slow cooker stuffing. Rather than take away “unhealthy” ingredients, I wanted to make my version colorful by adding red cranberries and green apples. I also replaced the white bread with 100% whole wheat bread. The end result? My family loved it and I hope yours will too!
instructions: Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Add onion, celery, mushrooms, and parsley to pan.
Stir often until veggies are tender.
Combine bread cubes, cranberries, and apple in a large bowl.
Pour veggies over bread cubes and mix gently.
Season with poultry seasoning, sage, thyme, garlic powder, and pepper.
Pour in broth (just enough to moisten) and gently mix in eggs.
Transfer mixture to slow cooker and cover.
Set slow cooker to High for 45 minutes; then reduce heat to Low and cook for 4 to 8 hours.
recipes.name: Melissa’s Slow Cooker Stuffing
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Melissa, USDA Nutritionist

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: In the mood for a refreshing snack? The combination of mint and lime on this fruit makes it a refreshing treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend lime juice, mint leaves, and brown sugar together in a small food processor.
Place melon cubes in a bowl.
Drizzle dressing over melon and toss gently.
recipes.name: Melon and Mint
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Exploding with delicious summer flavors, this salsa recipe is amazing with whatever melon you have on hand.

ingredients.name: fresh melon
ingredients.note: use one kind or a combination of honeydew, cantaloupe, or watermelon
ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh melon, seeded and chopped

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cucumber, peeled, seeded, and chopped

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup onion, red or white, chopped

ingredients.name: lime juice or lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup lime juice or lemon juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium size bowl, stir together all ingredients.
Taste and season with more lemon or lime juice, sugar if needed.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Serve with grilled or broiled fish or chicken.
recipes.name: Melon Salsa
recipes.notes: Caution: When handling hot peppers, the oils can cause burning and skin irritation. You can wear clean kitchen gloves or wash hands thoroughly after preparing. KEEP HANDS AWAY FROM EYES.
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Here is a sweet apple treat that you can prepare in minutes in the microwave.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apples and remove core.
Cut a thin slice off bottom of each apple to form a flat surface.
Place apples in a microwave-safe baking dish.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon in a small dish.
Spoon mixture into center of apples.
Cover wax paper and microwave on high power 6 to 10 minutes or until apples are soft.
recipes.name: Microwave Baked Apple
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish is a great way to enjoy a piping hot baked potato, without even turning on your oven.
instructions: Number of Potatoes Time 1 7 to minutes or until soft 2 or 3 10 to 12 minutes or until soft 4 or 5 14 to 18 minutes or until soft
recipes.name: Microwave Baked Potato
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare cauliflower, peas, and onion in a flavorful cream sauce without even turning on your stove.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine cauliflower, peas, and water in a 1-quart casserole.
Cover.
Microwave at High 6 to 8 minutes, or until fork-tender, stirring after half the time.
Let stand, covered.
Place onion and butter or margarine in 2-cup measure.
Microwave at High 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, or until onion is tender.
Stir in flour.
Microwave a few seconds until flour mixture starts to bubble.
Add remaining ingredients.
Microwave at High 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, or until thickened, stirring every minute.
Drain vegetables. (Freeze drained liquid for use in soups later.) Pour sauce over vegetables and stir to coat.
recipes.name: Microwave Cauliflower and Peas in Cream Sauce
recipes.notes: Options : Vegetables may be boiled or steamed and sauce prepared on top of a range if a microwave is not available. Variations : Use other combinations of vegetables, such as green beans and cauliflower; broccoli and carrots; or peas and carrots. Add lime as a garnish if desired.
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Vegetable Cookery — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick egg scramble sandwich is made fast in the microwave for a great on-the-go breakfast, lunch, or snack.

ingredients.name: red or green bell peppers
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons red or green bell peppers, chopped

ingredients.name: slider-sized bun or whole wheat English muffin
ingredients.raw: 1 slider-sized bun or whole wheat English muffin, split and toasted

instructions: Place peppers and onions in 8 ounce ramekin or custard cup, or in a small bowl.
Microwave on high 30 seconds; stir.
Add egg, ham, and water, beat until egg is blended.
Microwave on high 30 seconds; stir.
Microwave until egg is almost set, 30 to 45 seconds longer.
Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Serve in bun.
recipes.name: Microwave Denver Scramble Slider
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this tasty soup in your microwave in minutes. Enjoy it with a fresh salad and a side of fruit for a light meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt margarine in glass bowl on HIGH for 30 to 50 seconds.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper until smooth.
Blend milk into flour-margarine mixture.
Cook on HIGH for 6 to 8 minutes, until thickened, stirring well each minute.
Set aside.
In a separate microwave safe bowl, cook 2 potatoes in 1 cup water.
When potatoes are done add potatoes and cooking water to white sauce.
Stir in one 16 ounce can of corn.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes or until steaming hot.
recipes.name: Microwave Potato Corn Chowder
recipes.notes: Shredded cheese, crumbled bacon, chopped ham, or onion may be added. Add clams for clam chowder.
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Eggs, tortillas, pepper, onion, and cheese are a tasty combination in this quick and easy recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Tear tortillas into small pieces.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan.
Add tortillas and stir until pieces begin to brown.
Add peppers and onion; sauté until soft.
Add eggs; stir until the eggs are cooked.
Remove from heat and sprinkle on the grated cheese.
Cover the pan and let cheese melt.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Migas "Crumbs"
recipes.recipe_by: The Texas A&M University System — Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare delicious soup in a snap! Canned beans and frozen veggies make this dish perfect for busy weeknights.

ingredients.name: (10 ounces) frozen vegetables
ingredients.raw: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen vegetables, any type

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium stewed tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium stewed tomatoes

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium broth
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium broth, any flavor

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans, any type

instructions: This recipe is developed for a child to help an adult in the kitchen.
Directions are written to different audiences.
recipes.name: Minestrone Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Food Wise Learn at Home Print Materials — Rutgers Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These fun, bite-sized snacks are a great way to use basil and tomatoes from a SNAP-Ed garden. They can also help kids learn to like veggies.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon olive oil, or cooking oil of choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice string cheese into 4 equal parts.
On a toothpick, skewer one cherry tomato, 2 basil leaves, and 1 piece string cheese.
Drizzle finished kebabs evenly with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
recipes.name: Mini Caprese Bites

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh and canned fruit make this juicy salad a wonderful snack or dessert.

ingredients.name: mandarin oranges in light syrup
ingredients.raw: 1 can mandarin oranges in light syrup

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Mixed Fruit Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Using cornmeal, rye, and whole wheat flour gives this chewy and delicious bread a wonderful texture and flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cornmeal, brown sugar, salt and oil with boiling water, cool to lukewarm (105 to 115 degrees F).
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water; stir into cornmeal mixture.
Add whole wheat and rye flours and mix well.
Stir in enough all purpose flour to make dough stiff enough to knead.
Turn dough onto lightly floured surface.
Knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, turning oil top.
Cover with clean towel; let rise in warm place until double, about 1 hour.
Punch dough down; turn onto clean surface.
Cover with clean towel; let rest 10 minutes.
Shape dough and place in greased 9x5-inch pan.
Cover with clean towel; let rise until almost double, about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Bake 35 to 45 minutes or until bread sounds hollow when tapped.
Cover with aluminum foil during baking if bread is browning too quickly.
Remove bread from pan and cool on wire rack.
recipes.name: Mixed Grain Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun - Yeast Breads — Cornell University Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Did you know cottage cheese, skim milk, and lemon juice can be thrown in a blender and taste just like sour cream? Enjoy this quick and easy recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all in the blender and blend until smooth.
recipes.name: Mock Sour Cream
recipes.recipe_by: Creative Vegetable Cookery — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of sweet potato flavor, this delicious pie will be a hit at your next holiday meal.

ingredients.name: cooked sweet potatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 cups cooked sweet potatoes, skin removed and mashed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Crust: Combine the flour and sugar in a bowl.
Add milk and oil to the flour mixture.
Stir with fork until well mixed and then form pastry into a smooth ball with your hands.
Roll the ball between two 12-inch squares of waxed paper using short, brisk strokes until pastry reaches edge of paper.
Peel off top paper and invert crust into pie plate.
Filling: Combine sugars, salt, spices, and eggs.
Add milk and vanilla.
Stir.
Add sweet potatoes and mix well.
Pour mixture into pie shell.
Bake in preheated oven for 60 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Cool and cut into 16 slices.
recipes.name: Mock Southern Sweet Potato Pie
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This sweet, creamy, and fruity treat is low in fat and rich in flavor.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place milk, sugar, vanilla, and banana in blender.
Process 15 seconds at high speed until smooth.
Pour mixture into a small bowl; fold in yogurt.
Chill.
Spoon into four dessert dishes; garnish each with two banana slices just before serving.
recipes.name: Mousse a la Banana
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This spicy and savory oven-fried fish will be a hit in your home. Enjoy it with seasonal vegetables and a side of your favorite fruit.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 475 degrees F.
Clean and rinse fish.
Wipe fillets with lemon juice and pat dry.
Combine buttermilk, garlic, and hot sauce in a medium bowl.
Combine pepper, salt, and onion powder with crumbs and place on plate.
Let fillets sit briefly in milk.
Remove and coat fillets on both sides with seasoned crumbs.
Let stand briefly until coating sticks to each side of fish.
Arrange on lightly oiled shallow baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes on middle rack without turning.
Cut into 6 pieces.
Serve with fresh lemon wedges.
recipes.name: Mouth-Watering Oven-Fried Fish
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A healthy twist on a deep-fried appetizer, these breaded and baked Mozz Totz are a favorite of kids and adults alike. Served with warm marinara sauce for dipping, they are great for a potluck meal or as an after-school snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Line a baking sheet with foil and spray lightly with cooking spray.
Remove cheese from package and cut into bite size pieces.
In a small non-stick skillet mix oregano and basil with breadcrumbs.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally until crumbs are lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Dip each piece of cheese in milk and then into toasted bread crumbs, coating completely.
Place on baking sheet about 1 1/2-inches apart.
Spray string cheese lightly with non-stick cooking spray.
Bake 5 to 6 minutes or until heated through. (Cheese may melt slightly and lose shape.
Simply press it back into place).
Dip in warmed marinara sauce and enjoy.
recipes.name: Mozz Totz
recipes.recipe_by: Champions for Change Recipes — Arizona Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chicken, mozzarella, and spinach seasoned with garlic make this an easy and delicious dinner.

ingredients.name: small chicken breast halves
ingredients.raw: 8 small chicken breast halves, skin and bone removed

ingredients.name: part skim mozzarella cheese
ingredients.raw: 8 ounces part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Place chicken between 2 sheets of plastic wrap; pound chicken to 1/4 inch thick.
Coat chicken with breadcrumbs and place on foil-covered baking sheet.
Discard remaining breadcrumbs.
Bake 10 minutes.
Top chicken with cheese; bake 4 to 5 minutes until cheese is melted and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet on medium heat.
Add garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add half the spinach and cook 1 minute.
Add remaining spinach.
Cook until wilted, turning occasionally.
Serve with chicken.
recipes.name: Mozzarella Chicken with Garlic Spinach
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try the original recipe using our Better Baking Mix , or try one of the variations with fruit and spice for a wonderful fresh baked treat.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Grease 12-cup muffin pan.
Mix the Better Baking Mix and sugar in a bowl.
Beat the egg with a fork.
Add egg, oil, and water to dry ingredients.
Stir just until all ingredients are wet.
Spoon into the prepared muffin pan.
recipes.name: Muffins (from Better Baking Mix)
recipes.recipe_by: Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare this hearty soup with vegetable broth if you desire it to be vegetarian or vegan.

ingredients.name: medium carrots
ingredients.raw: 2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced thin

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in large soup pot over high heat.
Sauté onion, celery, carrots, and mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients except for the parsley and bring to a boil.
Lower heat to a simmer and cook until the barley is tender, about 20 minutes.
Sprinkle parsley on top of soup and serve hot.
recipes.name: Mushroom Barley Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chopped mushrooms, when sautéed, blend seamlessly with ground meats. Swapping or adding mushrooms to a recipe can add an extra serving of vegetables to the plate.
instructions: Chop mushrooms to approximate size and texture of cooked ground beef.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef and mushrooms, and cook.
Sauté until ground beef is done.
Remove mushroom-beef mixture from pan.
Add onions and garlic to pan; cook until golden.
Return mushroom-beef mixture to pan, along with remaining ingredients.
Simmer about 10 minutes; remove from heat.
recipes.name: Mushroom Beef Sloppy Joes
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and a slice of watermelon.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bring another serving of vegetables and important nutrients to your plate with this veggie-filled twist on classic fajitas. We've upped the vegetables ante by sautéing savory mushrooms and mixing them with steak for an umami-rich, flavorful punch. And we've sped up the preparation time for this Tex-Mex favorite, foregoing marinating the steak by using a tender cut.

ingredients.name: sirloin or other boneless steak
ingredients.raw: 12 ounces sirloin or other boneless steak

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 cup green bell pepper, sliced into strips

ingredients.name: medium red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium red bell pepper, sliced into strips

ingredients.name: medium yellow bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips

instructions: Slice beef across the grain into 1/4-inch strips.
Place in a medium bowl with 1/2 tablespoon fiesta lime seasoning; toss to coat.
Place mushrooms, peppers, and onion and remaining fiesta lime seasoning in a large bowl; toss to coat.
Heat oil in large, non-stick skillet.
Add beef strips; cook about 3 to 4 minutes.
Remove from skillet.
Place coated vegetables in skillet and sauté until vegetables are slightly tender, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Add beef back to skillet and sauté mixture 1 to 2 more minutes.
Assemble fajitas by dividing beef-vegetable mixture evenly on each tortilla, top with remaining ingredients and roll up.
recipes.name: Mushroom Steak Fajitas
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and side of mango chunks.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy the amazing smell coming from your grill as you make this delicious naan. Be sure to savor the delicious flavor and texture while it is still warm!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water and let stand about 10 minutes, or until frothy.
Stir in sugar, milk, egg, salt, and enough flour to make a soft dough.
Knead for 6 - 8 minutes on a lightly floured surface or until smooth.
Let it rise 1 hour until the dough has doubled in volume.
Punch down dough and knead in garlic.
Pinch off small handfuls of dough about the size of a golf ball.
Roll into balls and place on a tray.
Cover with a towel and allow to rise until doubled in size, about 30 minutes.
During the second rising, preheat grill to high heat.
At grill side, roll one ball of dough out into a thin circle.
Lightly oil grill.
Place dough on grill and cook for 2 - 3 minutes or until puffy and lightly browned.
Brush uncooked side with butter and turn over.
Brush cooked side with butter and cook until browned, another 2 to 4 minutes.
Remove from grill and continue the process until all the naan has been prepared.
recipes.name: Naan
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Did you know that canned tomatoes have more lycopene and B vitamins than fresh tomatoes? That’s because the canning process seals in food’s natural goodness! So when you add canned tomatoes to this delicious dish, you’re adding nutrition, freshness and flavor.

ingredients.name: no salt added diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can no salt added diced tomatoes

ingredients.name: canned tuna packed in water
ingredients.raw: 5 ounces canned tuna packed in water, drained

ingredients.name: Salt and ground pepper to taste
ingredients.raw: Salt and ground pepper to taste

instructions: Cook fettuccine as label directs.
Reserve 1 cup cooking liquid; drain.
Meanwhile, in 10-inch skillet over medium heat, in hot oil, cook onion and garlic, about 5 minutes until just softened.
Add diced tomatoes and capers; simmer 5 minutes.
Add tuna, olives, salt, and pepper to taste.
Toss fettuccine with tuna mixture to mix well.
Serve immediately.
If necessary, add reserved cooking liquid.
recipes.name: Neopolitan Tuna Fettuccine
recipes.recipe_by: Cans Get You Cooking

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spice up your week with these delicious New Orleans Red Beans. Season with hot sauce if desired.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pick through beans to remove bad beans; rinse thoroughly.
In a large pot combine beans, water, onion, celery, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil; reduce heat.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 1-1/2 hours until beans are tender.
Stir.
Mash beans against side of pan.
Add green pepper, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Cook, uncovered, over low heat until creamy (about 30 minutes).
Remove bay leaves.
Serve with hot cooked brown rice, if desired.
recipes.name: New Orleans Red Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Sweet breakfast cookies that can be prepared in advance for breakfast on the go.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat honey and peanut butter in a medium saucepan over low heat.
Stir until blended.
Remove from heat.
Stir in dry milk.
Fold in cereal and raisins.
Drop by heaping tablespoons onto waxed paper to form mounds.
Cool to room temperature.
Store in refrigerator.
recipes.name: No Bake Breakfast Cookies
recipes.notes: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Buy Better. Eat Better. — Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Boiled instead of baked, these chewy cookies are full of peanut butter, cocoa, oats, and raisins. Yum!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large sauce pan, bring the first six ingredients to a full, rolling boil for 1 minute, stirring as needed.
Remove from heat.
Add oats, dry milk, raisins, and vanilla to boiled mixture.
Mix well.
Drop by tablespoons onto waxed paper and let stand until cool, about 15 to 20 minutes.
recipes.name: No-Bake Cookies
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Full of fruit and oat bran, these tasty muffins can be enjoyed as a snack or a dessert.

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons raisins, dates, or other dried fruit

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
In a large bowl, mix the first four dry ingredients.
Set aside.
In another bowl, mix the egg with orange juice, milk, and oil.
In small bowl, mix fruit and blend with dry ingredients.
Add the liquid ingredients to the dry until it is moist.
Spray muffin tin with a non-stick coating.
Pour batter into muffin tins.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes.
Remove muffins from pan after 10 minutes.
Cool on a rack.
Freeze muffins for later use.
recipes.name: Oat Bran Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These oat snack cakes are full of whole grains and flavor, making them perfect for sharing with friends and family.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Mix together oatmeal, flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Combine oil, vanilla, egg whites, and water.
Stir into dry ingredients and add raisins, mixing only until it holds together.
Wash hands thoroughly, then dip in cornmeal or flour.
Pinch off pieces of dough and form into balls about 1 inch in diameter.
Place balls on baking pan (sprayed with non-stick cooking spray) and press out slightly to about 1/4-inch in thickness.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool, then store in an airtight container.
recipes.name: Oat Snack Cakes
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Futures — Virginia Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Packed with whole grains, this tasty bread is perfect as a snack topped with jam or peanut butter.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine rolled oats and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in boiling water; cool to lukewarm (105 to 115 degrees F).
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water in small bowl.
Add yeast water, molasses, and oil to cooled oatmeal mixture.
Stir in whole wheat flour and 1 cup all-purpose flour.
Add additional all-purpose flour to make a dough stiff enough to knead.
Knead dough on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes.
Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, turning to oil top.
Cover with clean towel; let rise in warm place until double, about 1 hour.
Punch dough down; turn onto clean surface.
Shape dough and place in greased 9x5 inch pan.
Cover with clean towel; let rise in a warm place until almost double, about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Bake 50 minutes or until bread sounds hollow when tapped.
Cover with aluminum foil during baking if bread is browning too quickly.
Remove bread from pan and cool on wire rack.
recipes.name: Oatmeal Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun - Yeast Breads — Cornell University Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: What's better than a toasty muffin right out of the oven? Enjoy these oatmeal raisin muffins with your breakfast or as a snack or dessert.

ingredients.name: margarine or butter
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon margarine or butter, to grease the muffin cups

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
