instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop all the vegetables.
Combine with the meat and seasonings in a large pot.
Add enough water to completely cover the mixture and add the oil and vinegar.
Cook, covered, for two to three hours on low heat until everything is well done.
recipes.name: The Bosnian Pot
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This sweet and savory salad is fresh and light and sure to please! This salad "pears" perfectly as a side dish at your holiday gathering. This dish is kid-tested and mom-approved!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large mixing bowl, add the pear, Brussels sprouts, and all other ingredients and mix until well incorporated.
Serve and enjoy!
recipes.name: The Perfect "Pear" and Brussels Sprout Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this sweet and tangy dressing on your favorite salad or as a dip for veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and warm water.
Mix ingredients together.
Chill and serve over vegetables or on a salad.
recipes.name: Thousand Island Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Food Wise Learn at Home Print Materials — Rutgers University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty salad pairs excellently with a tuna salad sandwich on whole grain bread and a piece of fruit. Make ahead of time and chill overnight in the refrigerator to let the flavor blend together.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, vegetables and garlic cloves in a large bowl.
Mix vinegar, oil, and sugar in a saucepan.
Heat until sugar dissolves.
Cool slightly.
Stir seasonings into vinegar mixture.
Pour over vegetables.
Toss lightly.
Chill overnight.
Remove garlic before serving.
recipes.name: Three Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: The Bold and Beautiful Book of Bean Recipes — Washington State WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A true comfort recipe to warm you up year-round. Make it your own by using any vegetables or beans that you have on hand.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: corn
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen or a 15-oz can (drained and rinsed)

ingredients.name: cooked beans
ingredients.note: any type or a 15-oz can (low-sodium, drained and rinsed)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large pan on medium heat.
Add carrot and onion and sauté until onions have begun to turn slightly brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add garlic, squash, and corn and continue to stir for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, broth, cumin, and pepper.
Allow soup to come to a boil and then turn heat down to a simmer until all vegetables are tender to taste (15 to 30 minutes, depending on the vegetables used).
recipes.name: Three Sisters Soup
recipes.notes: Try This: Change the vegetables and beans based on what you have on hand. Instead of cumin, try 2 to 3 teaspoons of Italian seasoning or 1 tablespoon of curry powder.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This hearty stew is great for dinner and even better the next day. It uses different ingredients like sweet potatoes and quick-cooking oats.

ingredients.name: red potatoes
ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cans, about 24 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 3 cups red potatoes, cubed (or 1 1/2 cans, about 24 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained)

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained
ingredients.raw: 2 tomatoes, diced (or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained)

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) tomato sauce
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce, no salt added

ingredients.name: frozen corn kernels (or 1/4 can
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup frozen corn kernels (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained)

ingredients.name: yellow squash
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and diced
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup yellow squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and diced)

ingredients.name: green squash
ingredients.note: or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium carrots, drained
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup green squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium carrots, drained)

ingredients.name: low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1/2 can low-sodium kidney beans, drained (about 8 ounces)

instructions: In a small skillet, brown ground beef and onions over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain fat.
In a large pot, combine cooked ground beef, water, and red potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Add all the other ingredients to the pot and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.
recipes.name: Three Sisters Stew
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer. See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations — Adapted from a recipe submitted by Alicson Scott, Chickasaw Nation, Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this scrumptious snack with your family. Use another nut butter if a member of your family suffers from a peanut allergy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Using two knives, cut peanut butter into dry ingredients until it appears coarse and crumbly.
In a small bowl, beat together egg white and milk.
Add to dry ingredients and mix well.
Spread mixture into a greased loaf pan.
Bake at 325 °F for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and remove from pan.
recipes.name: Three-Grain Peanut Bread
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Futures: Choosing Healthy Foods — Virginia Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Let kids build mini pizzas. Top a whole-grain pita with sauce and criss-cross of low-fat mozzarella cheese and vegetables for a quick, fun dinner.

ingredients.name: pasta sauce
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup pasta sauce, no salt added

ingredients.name: sticks part skim mozzarella string cheese
ingredients.raw: 4 sticks part skim mozzarella string cheese

instructions: Place rack in middle of oven and pre-heat to 400 °F.
For Xs, cut carrot and bell pepper into small sticks about 2 inches long.
For Os, cut summer squash into 12 slices.
For grid, pull apart each cheese stick to make 4 strips.
Place pita rounds on baking sheet and spread pasta sauce on each.
Let kids build tic tac toe pizzas with cheese and vegetables.
Bake about 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbling.
recipes.name: Tic Tac Toe Veggie Pizza
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Searching for a good vegetarian lunch option? Enjoy this tofu and vegetable salad on whole grain bread, with a piece of fruit for a satisfying and tasty meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare tofu by draining the water from the package and placing tofu between two plates.
Put a heavy object on top and let stand for 10 to 15 minutes.
Drain the water that collects on the bottom plate every few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, and soy sauce.
In a medium bowl, combine the diced tofu, celery, onion, pepper, and parley; stir in the mayonnaise mixture and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate covered until the flavors are blended -- at least one hour.
Use as a sandwich filling or on top of whole grain crackers.
recipes.name: Tofu Salad
recipes.notes: You may substitute yellow mustard for brown mustard.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tofu cooked until golden brown, and broccoli sautéed in a soy and scallion sauce make up this one-skillet meal. Serve with a side of brown rice for a quick dish.
instructions: Put the tofu on a cutting board and cut it in half and then cut each half into 4 equal pieces.
Put 2 layers of paper towel on a cutting board and put the tofu on top.
Let drain at least 20 minutes (and up to 2 hours).
Place a skillet over medium heat and when hot, add 2 teaspoons oil.
Add the tofu, one piece at a time, and cook until golden, about 3 minutes per side.
Remove the tofu to a plate and set aside.
Reheat the skillet and when hot, add remaining 2 teaspoons oil.
Add garlic and scallions and cook until just golden, about 2 minutes.
Add the broccoli and water and raise the heat to high.
Cook until the broccoli is tender, about 4 minutes.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the remaining ingredients.
Stir well.
Serve with a side of brown rice.
recipes.name: Tofu with Broccoli
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This vegetable and tofu soup is a delicious way to end your day. You can use fresh or frozen spinach and top with cilantro for a satisfying soup.

ingredients.name: tofu
ingredients.note: 14 ounce - patted dry and cut into ½ inch cubes
ingredients.raw: 1 package tofu, silken, firm or extra firm

ingredients.name: spinach leaves
ingredients.note: washed and dried, or 1- 10 ounce box frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a 3 quart saucepan over medium heat; add oil and chopped onion.
Cook onion until softened, but not brown.
Stir in garlic and cook just until fragrant.
Add chicken broth.
Bring to a boil.
Add tomatoes and tofu.
Lower heat and simmer until tomatoes are soft but not mushy (this takes just a couple of minutes).
Stir in green onions (optional), spinach, ground pepper and cilantro.
Cook just until spinach is wilted.
Remove from heat.
Taste for seasoning.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Tofu, Tomato, and Spinach Soup
recipes.notes: Add extra vegetables that you have on hand, such as peppers, spinach, avocado, kale, etc. for more flavor and nutrients!
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This refreshing salad is an excellent source of vitamin C and a great way to take advantage of the vegetables’ summer growing season.

ingredients.name: olive oil (or oil of your choice)
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or oil of your choice)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine the salad ingredients.
In a small bowl, mix the dressing ingredients together.
Pour the dressing over the salad.
Mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
recipes.name: Tomato and Cucumber Salad
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toasted garlic bread and mozzarella cheese combine with tomatoes and basil to give this easy omelet delicious, fresh flavor. Add a piece of fruit on the side to for a meal with food from each food group.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 °F.
Cut the bread into cubes; toss with oil and garlic in a small bowl.
Spread the cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for 15 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown, tossing once or twice.
Transfer to a plate to cool.
Spray a medium pan with nonstick cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat.
Pour in egg substitute.
When the egg begins to set, spread evenly across the bottom of the pan and reduce the heat to low.
Once the top layer of egg is almost cooked, sprinkle the cheese and basil on top and scatter the tomatoes and bread over half of the omelet; fold the unfilled omelet half over the filling.
Slide the omelet on a plate and serve.
recipes.name: Tomato and Garlic Omelet
recipes.recipe_by: California Champions for Change: Breakfast Recipes — California Department of Public Health — Network for a Healthy California

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Beans, tomatoes, and basil are mixed with pasta and a tasty vinaigrette to give you a easy and tasty meal. Bring this pasta salad to your next cookout or gathering. Add whatever vegetables you have on hand.

ingredients.name: pasta
ingredients.note: ziti, bow tie or other shaped pasta

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: kidney beans
ingredients.note: cooked or low-sodium canned drained, or try garbanzo beans or black beans

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together vegetable oil, vinegar, Dijon-style mustard, and pepper to make vinaigrette.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pasta, beans, basil, and tomatoes.
Pour vinaigrette over top and toss together.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
If desired, add nuts and cheese just before serving, tossing again to combine.
recipes.name: Tomato Basil and Bean Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious appetizer is a great way to use ripe tomatoes and basil from your garden. Serve with toasted bread on the side for a quick and delicious appetizer for your family or at your next get-together.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: French bread baguette
ingredients.note: or Italian, cut into 1/2 inch diagonal slices

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Combine tomatoes, garlic, onion, basil, and olive oil in a bowl.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste (optional).
Set aside.
Arrange bread on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake about 5 to 7 minutes until it begins to brown slightly.
Remove bread from oven and transfer to a serving platter.
Serve the tomato mixture in a bowl with a serving spoon and let everyone help themselves.
Or place some on each slice of bread before serving.
If adding the tomato mixture yourself, add it at the last minute or the bread may become soggy.
recipes.name: Tomato Basil Bruschetta
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Eating Recipes — University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This creamy soup can be prepared using pantry staples such as canned tomatoes and non-fat dry milk. Garlic and onion give this delicious soup an extra kick of flavor.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: non-fat dry milk
ingredients.note: + 2 cups water or substitute 2 cups non-fat milk

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium saucepan, cook onion in oil over medium heat, stirring frequently until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer.
Add chopped tomatoes.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spoon 3/4 of mixture into food processor or blender container; puree until smooth.
Return to saucepan.
Add red pepper, basil, and reconstituted milk to the soup.
Heat until hot, but do not boil.
Season to taste with salt and pepper (optional).
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Tomato Basil Soup
recipes.recipe_by: USDA’s Collection of Nonfat Dry Milk Recipes — USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Food Distribution Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Pasta and tomato sauce are topped with cheese and cooked in the oven. Double this recipe for a family of 4. Add a tossed salad for a hearty meal.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
In a small saucepan, cook onion and garlic in oil until tender.
Stir in tomatoes, basil, oregano, sugar, and pepper.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Add pasta to sauce.
Transfer to a greased 1-quart baking dish.
Top with cheeses.
Bake, uncovered at 375 °F for 10 to 15 minutes or until cheese is melted.
recipes.name: Tomato N' Cheese Pasta
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking For You or Two — University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Peas, lentils, and beans combined with spices and veggies provide this pasta soup with flavor and fiber. Enjoy this hearty soup on a chilly night.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse beans.
Put into a 4 or 5 quart heavy pot with 8 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender (1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours).
Add 4 cups water and remaining ingredients to beans.
Return to boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 1/2 hour, until tortellini and vegetables are tender.
recipes.name: Tortellini Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare this layered dip with beans, salsa, sour cream, and cheese for your next party. Make your own tortilla chips to serve on the side. Fill up on fiber while having fun.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Place tortillas in a stack on cutting board.
With a sharp knife, cut stack into eight pieces, forming triangles or wedges.
Lay tortillas pieces out in single layer on baking sheet.
Set aside while making dip.
Open canned beans.
Pour beans in colander; rinse and drain.
Place beans in a small mixing bowl and mash with a potato masher.
Spread beans over bottom of baking dish.
Measure salsa and spread over beans.
Measure sour cream and spread over beans.
Grate and measure cheese; sprinkle over bean mixture.
Place lettuce wedge on cutting board.
Slice into thin strips; set aside.
Place both the baking sheet with tortilla pieces and the dip in preheated oven.
Bake about 8 minutes or until tortilla pieces are crisp and dip is bubbly.
Sprinkle lettuce over dip and serve with tortilla chips.
recipes.name: Tortilla Chips and Bean Dip
recipes.notes: Flavor Change Options:
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun - A Pyramid of Snacks — Cornell Cooperative Extension — Cornell University Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These mini pizzas combine the flavors of tacos with the fun and variety of pizza. A favorite for kids and adults alike.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of choice or margarine

ingredients.name: (16 ounces) low-sodium
ingredients.raw: 1 can (16 ounces) low-sodium, fat-free refried beans

ingredients.name: fresh or canned green chili peppers
ingredients.raw: 2 ounces fresh or canned green chili peppers, diced

ingredients.name: vegetables
ingredients.note: try broccoli, mushrooms, spinach, and red bell pepper, or use your favorite veggies

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brush one side of two tortillas with water.
Press the wet sides of the tortillas together to form a thick crust for the pizza.
Brush the outside of the tortillas with a small amount of oil or margarine.
Evenly brown both sides in a heated frying pan.
Repeat with the rest of the tortillas.
Set aside.
Heat refried beans, onion, and half of the chili peppers together in a medium saucepan, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat.
Spread about 1/3 cup of the bean mixture on each tortilla pizza.
Sprinkle with 1/2 tablespoon taco sauce, then top with 1/2 cup of the chopped vegetables, 1 teaspoon chili peppers, and 1 tablespoon cheese for each pizza.
Return to frying pan and heat until cheese melts.
Top with cilantro, if desired.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Tortilla Pizzas
recipes.notes: Corn tortillas used for nutrient analysis. Using flour tortillas will change nutrition information.
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A toasty tortilla with beans and melted cheese, topped with cool fresh veggies!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, arrange tortillas in a single layer.
Spray both sides with non-stick cooking spray and bake for 4 minutes or until crisp.
If desired mix chili powder into refried beans.
Spoon 1/3 cup of refried beans on each tostada.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Top each one with lettuce and tomato.
Serve with salsa and sour cream (optional).
recipes.name: Tostadas
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Crisp tortillas, refried beans, and layers of fresh veggies make this a tasty and healthy vegetarian option.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Turn on oven to 350 °F.
Place tortillas on a cookie sheet and put in oven for 10 minutes or until crispy.
Wash lettuce and tomatoes.
Shred lettuce and dice tomatoes Spread two large tablespoons of refried beans on each tortilla.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes, and cheese.
Add green onions if desired.
Serve immediately and refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Tostadas Delgadas
recipes.recipe_by: The Texas A&M University System — Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service — Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: You can adjust this recipe to accommodate food allergies. Try with sunflower seed butter or almond butter if you are working with a peanut allergy.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl.
Combine honey and sugar in pan and bring to a boil.
Add peanut butter and vanilla, stir until peanut butter melts.
Pour mixture over cereal and mix well.
Press into a 13x9 inch pan and cool.
recipes.name: Trail Mix Bars
recipes.notes: * Children under one year of age should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Throw together this quick treat full of dried fruit, nuts, and delicious grains. Enjoy it as a snack on your next walk through the park or hike.

ingredients.name: square corn
ingredients.raw: square corn, rice, or wheat cereal

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Choose the ingredients you want to use.
Measure the suggested amounts of chosen ingredients and add to mixing bowl.
Mix ingredients using stirring spoon and divide evenly into 4 storage bags.
Enjoy your Trail Treat!
recipes.name: Trail Treat
recipes.notes: Ingredients used for costing and nutritional analysis:
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this tasty fruit dish in the morning or as a snack anytime of the day.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place orange juice in bowl.
Wash apple and dry.
Remove the seeds and dice.
Coat apple surfaces with orange juice to prevent browning.
Peel orange and break into sections.
Cut sections into small pieces.
Peel and slice banana into 1/4 inch circles.
Combine all fruit and orange juice lightly in a bowl and mix together.
Chill or serve immediately.
recipes.name: Tropical Morning Treat
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Breakfast is a snap with a quick step the night before. Mix oats, milk, and yogurt and refrigerate overnight. Add bananas and pineapple chunks in the morning.
instructions: Mix oats, milk, yogurt, and allspice in two bowls or glass jars.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Just before serving, add pineapple, banana, and almonds.
recipes.name: Tropical Overnight Oatmeal
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy a tropical treat with these frozen yogurt pops! They are fun to make and have 1/4 cup of fruit per serving.

ingredients.name: mango pieces
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup mango pieces, fresh or frozen

ingredients.name: pineapple pieces
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup pineapple pieces, fresh, canned, or frozen

ingredients.name: ice cube tray or small paper cups
ingredients.raw: ice cube tray or small paper cups

instructions: Place all ingredients into blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups) and place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!
recipes.name: Tropical Yogurt Pops
recipes.notes: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Pita bread stuffed with salad greens, tuna, veggies, and fruit makes an easy and flavorful lunch or dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, stir together tuna, onion, apple, celery, raisins, and 2 tablespoons of dressing.
In another bowl, toss together salad greens with remaining dressing.
Carefully open pita breads and fill with equal amounts of greens and tuna salad.
recipes.name: Tuna Apple Salad
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: Discover the Secret to Healthy Living — California Department of Health Services — California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Liven up your lunch-time sandwich with a refreshing mix of tuna, apples, raisins, and walnuts.

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.note: such as Fuji or Pink Lady Washington

ingredients.name: leaves lettuce
ingredients.note: Bibb, Romaine, green, or red leaf

instructions: Cut apple in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium-sized bowl, mix all salad ingredients, except tuna.
Gently fold in tuna.
Make sandwiches using lettuce and whole-grain bread (toasted, if desired), and fill with tuna apple salad.
recipes.name: Tuna Apple Salad Sandwich
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of 100% orange juice.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Delicious and easy, this tuna melt makes a yummy lunch or dinner. Each sandwich bakes in it's own foil package, so there's an added bonus of easy cleanup.
instructions: Divide tuna mixture into six portions, place one portion on six slices of whole wheat bread.
Then place a single slice of bread on top of each. (you will make a total of 6 sandwiches).
Remove from oven.
Pierce foil to release steam before serving.
recipes.name: Tuna Melt Burger
recipes.recipe_by: Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program — The Texas A&M University System

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Loaded with protein-packed tuna, nutritious veggies and fresh cooked pasta, this dish makes a delicious meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook spaghetti according to package; drain.
Heat oil in a large skillet or pan over medium heat.
Add onion and broccoli (or zucchini).
Cook until softened.
Stir in tomato-based pasta sauce.
Bring to a boil.
Turn heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add drained tuna into the sauce mixture.
Stir just enough to heat the tuna.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Add cooked spaghetti to the sauce.
Stir the pasta and sauce mixture until mixed together uniformly.
Optional: Add 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese to cooked mixture of pasta and sauce.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Tuna Pasta
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This hearty pasta dish uses pantry staples such as canned tuna and cream soup along with a few fresh veggies to make a dish full of protein and flavor.

ingredients.name: pasta shells
ingredients.raw: 12 ounces pasta shells, or other pasta

ingredients.name: cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.note: 10.75 ounces, or cream of celery, or chicken
ingredients.raw: 1 can cream of mushroom soup, reduced sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions and drain.
In a large skillet or pot, cook onion and pepper in oil.
Add cream soup, diced tomatoes and tuna to onion and pepper.
Mix with pasta.
Put in baking dish.
Cook at 350 °F for 25 minutes until bubbly.
Top with cheese and parsley if desired and return to oven for 5 minutes to melt.
recipes.name: Tuna Pasta Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quesadilla can be cooked quickly in the microwave or on the stove. Serve with a fresh salad and an apple for a complete meal.

ingredients.name: tuna fish
ingredients.raw: 1 can tuna fish, packed in water

instructions: Microwave Spoon filing onto half of each tortilla.
Top filling with cheese and fold tortilla in half.
Microwave on high for 60 seconds.
Turn the plate halfway through cooking time.
OR Stovetop Divide mixture onto two tortillas.
Top with cheese and the remaining two tortillas.
Spray a skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Brown quesadillas on both sides.
Cut before serving.
recipes.name: Tuna Quesadillas
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tuna salad served on a bed of lettuce and veggies with a whole grain crackers on the side makes this an easy and delicious lunch. Have a piece of fruit as a tasty side dish or dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss lettuce, vegetables, oil, vinegar and herbs in a large salad bowl.
Mix ingredients for tuna salad in another medium sized mixing bowl.
Assemble salad by placing greens on a large plate.
Top with a scoop of tuna salad.
Serve crackers on the side.
recipes.name: Tuna Salad on Greens
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Demo II — Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grapes make this tuna salad both savory and sweet. Serve this salad over lettuce leaves for a quick and easy lunch.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine drained tuna, celery, mayonnaise and yogurt and stir.
Add grapes to mixture and stir gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serve over lettuce leaves.
recipes.name: Tuna Salad with Grapes
recipes.notes: Optional:
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Tuna Salad, Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: For a touch of spice and everything nice, add some canned green chilies to tuna sliders. You won't believe how much flavor this canned staple packs in! With a well-stocked pantry full of canned ingredients, like tuna and green chilies, it’s easy to create delicious, homemade meals you can feel good about serving your family and friends.

ingredients.name: canned tuna
ingredients.raw: 5 ounces canned tuna, packed in water

ingredients.name: chopped fresh cilantro or parsley
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

instructions: In large bowl, combine tuna, green chilies, celery, red onion, mayonnaise, and chopped cilantro; toss to mix well.
Add lettuce leaves to the bottom half of each roll.
Top with some tuna mixture.
Add top half of roll and enjoy!
recipes.name: Tuna Slider with Green Chiles
recipes.recipe_by: Cans Get You Cooking

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Herbs really give this salad a real zest. Marinate overnight in the refrigerator to allow flavors to blend. If you don't have the vegetables listed, substitute whatever veggies you have on hand.

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: raw, chopped or any of your favorite raw veggies

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.note: raw, chopped or any of your favorite raw veggies

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and trim vegetables.
Chop into bite-sized pieces.
Place in large bowl.
Combine vinegar, dill (or other herbs), garlic, and oil.
Pour over vegetables.
Drain and rinse beans.
Break up tuna into smaller chunks.
Combine vegetables, beans, and tuna; toss gently.
Marinate salad overnight to combine flavors.
Chill and serve as a light summer lunch or as a picnic side dish.
recipes.name: Tuna Veggie Antipasto
recipes.recipe_by: Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes — Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: It's time to raise the bar on the good ol’ tuna sandwich. Boost flavor with lemon juice and Dijon. Seasonal veggies in the mix do double-duty – taste and color!

ingredients.name: red bell peppers
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup red bell peppers, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: romaine lettuce leaves
ingredients.raw: 6 romaine lettuce leaves, torn in half

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix together tuna, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice.
Stir in carrots, red bell peppers, and celery.
Place 6 torn leaves of romaine lettuce on half of the slices of whole wheat bread.
Spoon tuna mixture on top of the lettuce slices.
Place another torn lettuce slice on each tuna sandwich and cover with another slice of bread.
Wrap sandwiches in colorful plastic wrap or wax paper and keep chilled.
Your sandwiches are now picnic ready!
recipes.name: Tuna Veggie Picnic Sandwich
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the Grain Foods Foundation, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These sandwiches, flavored with herbs and spices, are sure to hit the spot. With whole grains, lean protein, and dairy, this well-rounded MyPlate meal will keep you satisfied all afternoon.

ingredients.name: turkey breast
ingredients.note: or fat free, low-sodium deli turkey

instructions: Mix the yogurt, dill, onion, pepper, and chopped cucumbers.
Divide the yogurt/ cucumber mixture on all 8 slices of bread.
Top the whole wheat bread with turkey and cucumber slices.
Cover with the white bread slices.
recipes.name: Turkey and Cucumber Sandwich
recipes.recipe_by: MyPlate National Strategic Partners — The Grain Chain

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon juice give these zesty burgers a real treat for your next cookout. Serve with tomatoes, lettuce, onion, and a whole wheat bun to boost your veggie and whole grains for the day.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine onions, turkey, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and parsley.
Mix well.
Shape mixture into four patties.
Fry in a pan on medium heat or grill until internal temperature reaches 165 °F.
recipes.name: Turkey Burgers
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This gravy uses chicken or turkey broth to create an easy and fast gravy. Perfect for a big holiday meal.

ingredients.name: chicken or turkey broth
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups chicken or turkey broth, low-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt margarine in skillet over low heat.
Mix in flour and salt.
Stir and heat until bubbly.
Add broth slowly, stirring constantly.
Cook over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the cooked giblets.
Heat a few minutes to blend flavors.
Store leftovers in refrigerator within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Turkey Gravy
recipes.recipe_by: Pictorial Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service — Oregon Family Nutrition Program — Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toss some sweet potatoes in the oven when you're baking this meatloaf, and pair this dinner with a tossed salad for a tasty and delicious meal!

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: dehydrated, or one small onion, minced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Bake in 9x5 loaf pan for 25 minutes or until it reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F.
Check the temperature with a meat thermometer.
Cut into five slices and serve.
recipes.name: Turkey Meatloaf
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy these tasty patties with fresh tomato slices and your favorite condiments on a whole grain bun.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix ground turkey, bread crumbs, egg, onions, and mustard in a large bowl.
Shape into 4 patties, about 1/2 inch thick.
Spray a large skillet with cooking spray.
Add patties and cook, turning once to brown other side.
Cook until golden brown outside and white inside, about 10 minutes.
Remove.
recipes.name: Turkey Patties
recipes.recipe_by: Quick and Healthy Meals: Tips and Tools for Planning Meals for Your Family — Ohio State University Cooperative Extension — Cuyahoga County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Colorful tomatoes and spinach make these appetizers festive enough for your next party or potluck.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place tortillas on microwaveable plate or paper towel; microwave uncovered on HIGH 10 to 15 seconds to soften.
Spread about 2 tablespoons cream cheese over each tortilla.
Top with a slice of turkey, chopped tomatoes, and spinach.
Roll up lightly; then wrap in plastic wrap.
Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours to blend flavors.
Cut each roll into eight 1-inch slices.
Arrange with cut side down on serving plate.
recipes.name: Turkey Pinwheel Appetizers
recipes.recipe_by: Ohio State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Green pepper, onions, and celery give this salad a delicious crunch. Serve chilled on a bed of lettuce or whole grain bread.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix turkey, celery, potato, onion, and green pepper.
Mix mayonnaise, mustard and salt.
Stir lightly into turkey mixture.
Chill.
recipes.name: Turkey Potato Salad
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maine Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh orange juice and Dijon mustard give this vinaigrette a bright and zesty flavor to top this turkey and orange salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a jar with tight-fitting lid, combine all vinaigrette ingredients; shake well.
If you don't have a container with a tight-fitting lid, place ingredients in a small mixing bowl and mix together with a whisk.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients; toss gently.
Serve with vinaigrette.
recipes.name: Turkey Salad with Orange Vinaigrette
recipes.recipe_by: Cook it QUICK! — University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This hearty stew of turkey, potatoes, and vegetables will warm up a cold winter night. You can replace the cooked turkey with cooked chicken.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: finely chopped, or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium saucepan.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, and celery and stir for 2 minutes.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, and water to pan.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add turkey and cook another five minutes or until heated.
Season to taste before serving.
recipes.name: Turkey Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Turkey and ground beef stuffed cabbage leaves are cooked and topped with a sweet and savory sauce of veggies, lemon juice, and brown sugar.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse and core cabbage.
Carefully remove 10 outer leaves, place in saucepan, and cover with boiling water.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Remove and drain cooked cabbage leaves on paper towels.
Shred 1/2 cup of raw cabbage and set aside.
Brown ground beef and turkey and minced onion in skillet.
Drain fat.
Place cooked and drained meat mixture, bread crumbs, water, and pepper into mixing bowl.
Drain tomatoes, reserving liquid, and add 1/2 cup of tomato juice from can to meat mixture.
Mix well; then place 1/4 cup of filling on each parboiled, drained cabbage leaf.
Place folded side down in large skillet.
In skillet top cabbages with tomatoes, sliced onion, water, shredded cabbage, and carrot.
Cover and simmer about 1 hour (or until cabbage is tender), basting occasionally.
Remove cabbage rolls to serving platter; keep warm.
Mix lemon juice, brown sugar, and cornstarch together in small bowl.
Add to vegetables and liquid in skillet, and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened and clear.
Serve over cabbage rolls.
recipes.name: Turkey Stuffed Cabbage
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These tostadas are layered with refried beans, turkey, and cheese to create a delicious and easy dinner. Top with tomatoes, lettuce, and onions to increase your veggies.

ingredients.name: cooked turkey
ingredients.note: cut into bite-sized pieces, or 2 cups ground turkey, browned in a skillet and drained

ingredients.name: cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375° F.
Wash and prepare vegetables.
In a large skillet over medium heat, combine turkey, taco seasoning, and water.
Bring mixture to boil, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place tortillas on a baking sheet.
Bake at 375° for 4 to 7 minutes or until tortillas are crispy.
Spread tortillas with a tablespoon of beans.
Top with 1/4 meat mixture and cheese.
Return tortillas to oven to cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Top with tomatoes, lettuce, onions, and taco sauce.
Garnish with yogurt and guacamole, if desired.
recipes.name: Turkey Tostadas
recipes.notes: Recipe analysis includes light meat turkey without skin.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Massachusetts Extension — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A great way to try turnips. Full of vegetables and packed with flavor, turnip pancakes will satisfy audiences of all ages.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix flour, pepper, egg, garlic, soy sauce, and water in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the turnip, carrot, and green onion Heat half of oil in a large skillet over medium heat (350 °F in an electric skillet).
Pour about 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake into skillet.
Flatten with a fork into a 3-inch circle.
Cook until edges look dry and bottom is golden, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn once.
Cook until bottom is golden and crispy.
Repeat with remaining batter, adding remaining oil as needed.
Pancakes will be moist in the center.
Combine dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Serve with warm pancakes.
recipes.name: Turnip Pancakes
recipes.notes: No rice vinegar? Try apple cider vinegar instead.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple and fun snack is created using only fresh apples and canned oranges.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apple.
Cut in half (see notes).
Place apple half in center of small plate.
Put mandarin oranges next to apple for arms, legs, and head.
Enjoy your Turtle Apple.
recipes.name: Turtle Apple
recipes.notes: Adults: Make sure you use sharp knife to cut apple in half, remove core, and discard. Then, using a can opener, open mandarin oranges, and discard sharp-edged lid.
recipes.recipe_by: Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon zest, garlic, and rosemary add a delightful Tuscan twist to this green bean, potato, and chicken skillet. The best part? Only having to use one pan to whip up this weeknight favorite, which also makes clean-up a breeze!
instructions: Cut each potato into 4 wedges.
Place in a large microwave-safe bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Microwave on HIGH for 4 minutes.
Stir and microwave for 4 minutes more.
While potatoes are cooking, cut each chicken tenderloin into 4 equal pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken and cook for 5 minutes or until nicely browned, stirring frequently.
Add remaining oil and potatoes; cook and stir for 5 minutes more to brown potatoes and fully cook chicken.
Stir in rosemary, garlic, green beans, lemon zest and juice.
Cook for a few minutes more to heat through.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
recipes.name: Tuscan Potato Skillet
recipes.notes: Use whatever type of potatoes you have on hand, are on sale, or offer the best price.
recipes.recipe_by: Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget — MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This no-fuss chili is a great way to use ground beef and beans to make a tasty main dish. Chili can be served by itself, with crackers, cooked rice, or baked potato.

ingredients.name: (about 8 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1/2 can (about 8 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drained

instructions: In a medium-sized pot, brown ground beef over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain fat.
Add kidney beans, vegetarian beans, onions, chili powder, tomato juice, and pepper.
Cook over low heat for about 40 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Two Bean Chili
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking with ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer. Tip: USDA Foods macaroni products such as spaghetti, rotini, and macaroni are great additions to chili.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: An easy and delicious one-pot dish that makes plenty of leftovers to savor!

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables
ingredients.note: chopped cauliflower, peppers, carrots, or peas

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, ginger, turmeric, and cumin, stir while cooking for 1 minute.
Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce heat.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers with in 2 to 3 hours.
recipes.name: Vegetable and Rice Skillet Meal
recipes.recipe_by: Original Recipe Name - Indian Vegetables and Rice Skillet Meal Healthy Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cooked turkey combined with your favorite frozen veggies means you can throw this stir fry together quickly for a healthy weekday dinner.

ingredients.name: thin slices of ginger root
ingredients.raw: 2 thin slices of ginger root, minced

ingredients.name: cooked turkey
ingredients.raw: 16 ounces cooked turkey, cut into 1/2 inch cubes

ingredients.name: (10 ounces each) frozen vegetables
ingredients.raw: 2 packages (10 ounces each) frozen vegetables, chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large frying pan on high heat.
Add ginger, garlic, turkey, vegetables, and salt.
Stir fry about 1 minute to coat with oil.
Adjust heat to prevent scorching.
Add sugar.
If vegetables are tender, stop cooking at this time.
If the vegetables are firm, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover and cook for 2 minutes or until tender.
Serve at once, or if you wish to add a gravy, mix the gravy ingredients well, pour over vegetables and turkey, cook for 30 seconds.
recipes.name: Vegetable and Turkey Stir Fry
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Swiss cheese, vegetables, and curry powder make this thick and creamy soup a filling meal on a cold night this winter. Serve with whole wheat toast on the side.

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables
ingredients.raw: 3 cups mixed vegetables, frozen or fresh, chopped

ingredients.name: Swiss cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup Swiss cheese, cut into small pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring 2 cups water to a boil.
Add vegetables, onions, salt, and curry powder, if using.
Reduce heat, cover and cook until almost tender.
Mix remaining 1 cup water, dry milk, and cornstarch together in a small bowl.
Add to partially cooked vegetables.
Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until thickened.
Add cheese and stir until melted.
Add more water if too thick.
Top with green onions if desired.
recipes.name: Vegetable Cheese Soup
recipes.notes: Store leftovers covered in the refrigerator.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chunks of zucchini, sweet potatoes, and frozen corn add a creative twist to this chili dish. Combined with canned beans and diced tomatoes this tasty one-pot meal will hit the spot.

ingredients.name: yellow onions
ingredients.raw: 2 yellow onions, peeled and coarsely chopped

ingredients.name: 16-ounce cans low-sodium dark red kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 3 16-ounce cans low-sodium dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: 14.5-ounce cans no salt added diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 14.5-ounce cans no salt added diced tomatoes

instructions: Put the pot over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onions, zucchini, sweet potatoes, garlic, and spices and cook, stirring from time to time, for 20 minutes.
Add the kidney beans and tomatoes.
Stir and cook, covered, until the squash is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add the corn and cook until warmed throughout.
Serve right away or transfer to a container once cooled.
Refrigerate up to 5 days.
recipes.name: Vegetable Chili
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Honey and brown mustard are the secret ingredients in this dip, the perfect compliment for raw veggies. Whip this up today, and start snacking.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together all ingredients in a bowl.
Serve with your favorite vegetables.
recipes.name: Vegetable Dipping Sauce
recipes.notes: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. Serving suggestion: Good with carrot sticks, broccoli, cauliflower, tomatoes, or any of your favorite vegetables.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This rice dish blends the flavors of soy sauce, pepper, and vegetables for a quick meal. It's cooked in one pan so clean up is quick too.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Make 2 cups of cooked white rice.
Use the package directions to make the rice.
Chop 1/2 cup of celery and 1/4 cup of onion.
Heat the oil in a skillet or large frying pan.
Add the celery and onion.
Stir fry for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the pan.
Keep stirring the vegetables until they are tender-crisp.
Add the cooked rice.
Sprinkle with soy sauce and pepper.
Stir fry for 2 minutes until the rice is heated and the flavors are blended.
recipes.name: Vegetable Fried Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use this colorful veggie plate at your next party or gathering.

ingredients.name: medium celery stalks
ingredients.raw: 2 medium celery stalks, cut into 3-inch sticks

ingredients.name: jalapeno chiles
ingredients.raw: 3 jalapeno chiles, finely chopped, seeded if desired

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Arrange vegetables on a platter.
In a small bowl, mix sour cream and salsa.
Serve.
Fresh Salsa Preparation: In a medium bowl, mix lime juice, tomatoes, onions, jalapeño chiles, cilantro, and salt.
Store salsa in refrigerator for up to three days in a covered plastic or glass container.
recipes.name: Vegetable Medley with Salsa Dip
recipes.notes: Feel free to serve with whatever vegetables you have on hand. Could also be served with crackers.
recipes.recipe_by: California 5 A Day, It’s So Easy — Contra Costa Health Services
recipes.serving_size: 1 cup vegetables and 1/2 cup salsa dip, 1/4 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Have kids help mix the ingredients and spread the cream cheese mixture on the tortillas for this fun and flavorful snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the corn and green chilis.
Collect, chop, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Mix cream cheese, corn, green chilies, onions, and salsa together in a bowl.
Spread mixture on tortillas, roll up tightly, and wrap in plastic wrap.
Cut in 1-inch slices, and serve immediately, or store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Vegetable Pinwheels
recipes.notes: Be creative! Add washed, chopped fresh cilantro or spices like cumin and chili powder in step #2.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy fresh, delicious pizza made at home. You can spice this up with red pepper flakes or garlic powder. Try with whatever vegetables you have on hand.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Spoon pizza sauce on pizza shell.
Put pizza shell on a cookie sheet.
Arrange vegetables over sauce.
Sprinkle on the cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes.
When baked, cool pizza for 3 minutes before slicing.
Cut into 8 wedges.
recipes.name: Vegetable Pizza
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Spunky Vegetable Pizza, California 5 A Day, It’s So Easy — Contra Costa Health Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Rice, vegetables, and seasoning are a winning flavor combination in this tasty side dish.

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium Mexican or Italian style tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium Mexican or Italian style tomatoes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium-sized saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the rice until just golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup of chicken broth if moisture is needed.
Add onions and garlic and cook for a minute or two.
Stir in the tomatoes and their juice, the rest of the chicken broth, salt, and bell pepper (if using).
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for about 20 to 25 minutes, or until the broth is absorbed.
recipes.name: Vegetable Rice with Tomatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Celebrate Health with a Lowfat Fiesta — California Department of Health Services — California Project LEAN

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty, marinaded veggie salad uses canned veggies and can be enjoyed at any time of the year. Use fresh vegetables if you have them on hand.

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) whole kernel corn
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) whole kernel corn, drained

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes (reserve 1/3 cup liquid)
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes (reserve 1/3 cup liquid)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain corn, carrots, and chickpeas.
Throw away liquid.
Rinse vegetables and drain again.
Drain tomatoes but save 1/3 cup of the liquid.
Mix corn, carrots, chickpeas, tomatoes, onion, and red pepper in a large bowl.
Mix together all other ingredients in a separate bowl.
Pour over vegetables.
Cover and set aside for at least 3 hours in the refrigerator.
recipes.name: Vegetable Salad
recipes.notes: Feel free to add other vegetables like green beans to the recipe. Instead of canned vegetables you could also use a 16 ounce bag of frozen vegetables. However, analysis was done with ingredients as specified in the recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Get creative with your fresh veggie snacks. This recipe calls for cucumber and tomatoes, but you can use your favorite veggies for this snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash ingredients.
Put cucumber slices (see notes) on a small plate to form a snake.
Add 2 slices of tomatoes for eyes.
Enjoy your Vegetable Snake.
recipes.name: Vegetable Snake
recipes.notes: Adults: Use a sharp knife to slice the cucumber and tomato into thin slices crosswise.
recipes.recipe_by: Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This soup can be prepared quickly in one pot for lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: ears corn
ingredients.note: or 1 can low-sodium whole kernel corn

ingredients.name: fresh carrots
ingredients.note: or 1 can low-sodium carrots, about 15 ounces
ingredients.raw: 1 pound fresh carrots, peeled and diced

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: or 2 cans low-sodium sliced potatoes, about 15 ounces each

instructions: In a large pot, heat the chicken and water over medium to high heat until hot.
Cut the kernels off the ears of corn.
Add the corn kernels and all other ingredients to the pot and boil for 10 seconds.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Vegetable Soup with Chicken
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 degrees F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — Adapted from a recipe by Natalie Gibson, San Pasqual Reservation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The green chili pepper adds delicious spice and flavor to this potato, corn, and summer squash stew.

ingredients.name: white potatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cups white potatoes, cut into 2-inch strips

ingredients.name: summer squash
ingredients.raw: 4 cups summer squash, cut into 1-inch chunks

ingredients.name: summer squash
ingredients.raw: 1 cup summer squash, cut into 4 chunks

ingredients.name: canned low-sodium sweet corn
ingredients.note: or 2 ears of fresh corn, cut off the cob
ingredients.raw: 1 3/4 cups canned low-sodium sweet corn, rinsed and drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put water and bouillon in large pot and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and carrots and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients, except for tomatoes, and continue cooking for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Remove 4 chunks of squash and purée in blender.
Return puréed mixture to pot and let cook for 10 minutes more.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let sit for 10 minutes to allow stew to thicken.
recipes.name: Vegetable Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This stroganoff has onion, garlic, carrots, zucchini, red bell pepper, and basil combined with a creamy tomato paste and yogurt sauce. Mixed with shaped pasta, this twist on stroganoff is a simple meal and real crowd pleaser.

ingredients.name: medium shaped whole wheat pasta
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound medium shaped whole wheat pasta

ingredients.name: 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes, no salt added

ingredients.name: tomato paste
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons tomato paste, no salt added

instructions: To cook the pasta, fill a pot halfway with water.
Bring it to a boil over high heat.
When it has boiled, add the pasta and cook until just tender, about 12 minutes.
Drain the pasta and set aside.
While the pasta is cooking, cook the stroganoff: Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion, garlic, carrots, zucchini, peppers, and dried basil and cook until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the sauce comes together, about 20 minutes.
Put the yogurt and tomato paste in the bowl, stirring until smooth.
Turn the heat off and move the vegetables in the skillet to one side.
Gradually add the tomato paste mixture to the other side of the skillet, stirring all the while.
Turn the heat to low and cook about 5 minutes, until heated through.
Add the cooked pasta and stir until mixed.
recipes.name: Vegetable Stroganoff
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These vegetable filled corn tortilla tacos get a kick from diced jalapeno peppers and garlic. Serve these as a side dish or enjoy as a snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onion, garlic and jalapeno, add cumin, salt, and black pepper.
When everything is soft, add red pepper and mushrooms.
Sauté for 2 more minutes.
Serve over tortilla and garnish with cut tomatoes and cilantro or cilantro sauce.
recipes.name: Vegetable Tacos
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from "Delicious Tacos" — Make Every Day A Healthy Snack Day — Alameda County Public Health Department

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicious chili packed full of veggies, beans, and spices is fast enough for a weeknight dinner. Top with cilantro for a boost of flavor.

ingredients.name: medium green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium green bell pepper, cut into 1/4-inch pieces

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium whole tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium whole tomatoes, cut into 1/4-inch pieces

ingredients.name: medium summer squash
ingredients.raw: 2 medium summer squash, cut in to 1/4-inch pieces

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add oil to a large pot and sauté onions, bell pepper, garlic, and jalapeno over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add chili powder, cumin, half of the chopped cilantro, salt, and pepper, and continue cooking for another 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the tomatoes, zucchini, and squash.
Bring mixture to a simmer.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add beans, and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes.
Serve the mixture hot.
Put remaining cilantro on top.
recipes.name: Vegetarian Chili
recipes.recipe_by: Veggin’ Out Recipe Book — Johnson and Wales University and Rhode Island Department of Health WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Want to add more leafy greens to your diet but aren’t sure how to start? Check out this recipe for collard greens. A healthy and tasty side dish to accompany your next meal.

ingredients.name: red pepper flakes
ingredients.note: increase to 1 teaspoon if you like food spicy

ingredients.name: collard greens
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cups collard greens, stems removed and chopped*

ingredients.name: medium tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 medium tomatoes, seeds removed and chopped**

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash all vegetables,* and remove seeds from the tomatoes.** Collect, chop, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, and cook for about 2 minutes until slightly soft.
Add the red pepper flakes and garlic, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped collard greens, and cook for another minute.
Add the broth, cover, and bring to a simmer.
Cook for about 40 minutes until the greens are tender.
Add tomatoes.
Taste, and add a small amount of salt and black pepper if desired.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Eat within 3 to 5 days.
recipes.name: Vegetarian Collard Greens
recipes.notes: * Preparing collard greens: First, remove any damaged outer leaves. Fill a large bowl with cold water, and dunk the greens. Swish them around for a few minutes to help loosen any dirt on the leaves. Pour out the dirty water and fill the bowl with clean water. Swish the leaves under the clean water again to remove any additional dirt. Continue this process until the water in the bowl remains clear. To cut collard greens, fold each leaf in half with the stem at the fold crease. Either cut or tear the stem off. Stack several leaves on top of each other and roll the leaves up. Cut the roll of leaves into 1-inch thick pieces. ** Removing tomato seeds: Turn the tomato on its side so the stem faces to the right. Cut the tomato down the center and use a 1/4 teaspoon to spoon out the seeds.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This savory, vegetable matzo ball soup is a delicious and quick meal on a cold evening.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
To Make Matzo Balls : Stir together eggs, oil, and vegetable stock in a small bowl.
Add matzo meal, dill, and salt.
Stir until evenly combined.
Cover and refrigerate 15 minutes to 8 hours.
Bring large pot of water to a boil; add a dash of salt.
Using oiled hands, form dough into 12 1-inch balls.
Drop the balls one at a time into the boiling water.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
To Make Broth : While matzo balls are simmering, make soup by adding all broth ingredients and bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
To serve, spoon 2 cooked matzo balls into a bowl and ladle 1 cup of soup over them.
recipes.name: Vegetarian Matzo Ball Soup
recipes.notes: Recipe cost can be reduced by substituting dried dill for fresh dill.
recipes.recipe_by: Boston University Sargent Choice Nutrition Center
recipes.serving_size: 2 cooked matzo balls with 1 cup soup, 1/6 of recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Combine oregano and basil with fresh and canned veggies to make your own spaghetti sauce, perfect for any pasta dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium skillet, heat oil.
Cook onions, garlic, and zucchini in oil for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Serve over pasta.
recipes.name: Vegetarian Spaghetti Sauce
recipes.recipe_by: DASH Eating Plan: Lower Your Blood Pressure — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Exploding with tomatoes and basil, these delicious stuffed peppers are a great side dish to any entrée.

ingredients.name: medium red
ingredients.raw: 4 medium red, yellow, or green bell peppers

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Lightly oil a large shallow baking pan.
Cut peppers in half lengthwise and remove seeds.
Arrange peppers cut sides up in baking pan and lightly oil cut edges of stems.
Halve cherry tomatoes and chop onion and basil.
Finely chop garlic.
In a bowl, toss tomatoes, onion, basil, garlic, and olive oil.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon equal portions of mixture into peppers and roast in upper third of oven until peppers are tender, about 20 minutes.
recipes.name: Vegetarian Stuffed Peppers
recipes.notes: Add any type of beans to add protein to this recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These delicious wraps are packed full of flavor and fiber. Mango, cilantro, and avocado add a fresh and flavorful topping to these wraps.

ingredients.name: medium green or red bell peppers
ingredients.raw: 2 medium green or red bell peppers, seeded and chopped

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a nonstick pan, sauté bell peppers and onion for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Add beans, stir well.
Reduce heat to low and simmer about 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine mangoes, lime juice, cilantro, and avocado.
Set aside 1/2 of this mango mixture for topping.
Fill warmed tortillas with 1/4 bean mixture and 1/4 mango mixture.
Fold ends of the tortillas over.
Roll up to make wraps.
Top veggie bean wraps with remaining mango mixture.
recipes.name: Veggie Bean Wrap
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vegetarian burgers can be made ahead of time and stored in the freezer. They can be served any time. To add some spice, top with salsa.

ingredients.name: (about 15 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn
ingredients.raw: 1 can (about 15 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn, finely chopped

ingredients.name: cayenne or jalapeño chilies
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon cayenne or jalapeño chilies, seeds removed and finely chopped,

instructions: In a large bowl, combine corn and cornmeal.
Add onions, green pepper, rice, chili powder, and pepper.
If using cayenne and jalapeño chilies, add them too.
Mix well.
Form the burger mixture into 6 equal patties about 1/2 inch thick, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Spray both sides of the patties with nonstick cooking spray.
In a large pan, brown both sides of the patties over medium to high heat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Bake the patties in the oven for 10 minutes.
Toast the flour tortillas in the oven for 8 minutes.
Place patty on half of tortilla and fold tortilla over to serve like a taco.
recipes.name: Veggie Burgers
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This noodle dish combines the crunch of fresh veggies with the flavors of onion, garlic, and soy sauce to create a delicious and easy stir fry. Make it a family favorite using your favorite veggies.

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.raw: 1 cup broccoli, cut into small pieces

ingredients.name: green or red bell peppers
ingredients.raw: 1 cup green or red bell peppers, finely chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare noodles according to package directions.
Drain and set aside.
Cook onion and garlic with oil in a large frying pan for 1 minute over medium/high heat.
Add carrot, chicken bouillon, and pepper sauce.
Stir.
Add broccoli, celery, and bell pepper and continue to stir.
Reduce heat to low and add noodles and soy sauce.
Mix well over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.name: Veggie Chow Mein
recipes.notes: Add other vegetables as desired. Top with chives.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cottage cheese is the key to this easy veggie dip. Try with different spices to suit your taste.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Measure cottage cheese and put in bowl or blender.
Beat with a fork or mixer, or in a blender, until cottage cheese is smooth.
Add the other ingredients.
Stir together.
Store the dip in the fridge for 1 to 2 hours to let the flavors blend.
recipes.name: Veggie Dip
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: With every forkful, you will experience the comforting creaminess of mashed potatoes mingling with the vibrant, zesty notes of a cucumber and tomato salad, the heartiness of spiced chickpeas, and the smoky allure of fire-roasted broccoli.

ingredients.name: 7.5-ounce can chickpeas
ingredients.raw: 1/2 7.5-ounce can chickpeas, low sodium, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and scrub the potato with a vegetable brush.
Cut into 2-inch pieces and place in a small pot.
Cover the diced potatoes with cold water.
Place the pot on the stove and turn the heat to high.
Once the water comes to a boil, reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook the potato pieces until they are fork-tender but not falling apart, about 15 to 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and drain the potatoes.
Return the potatoes to the stove for about 30 seconds to ensure all the water is removed from the pan and the potatoes are dry.
While the potatoes are boiling, roast the chickpeas and broccoli in the air fryer.
Toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil and the curry powder, lay them out on a baking tray in an even layer, and place in a 400 °F air fryer for 10 minutes, until crispy.
Toss the broccoli with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and the paprika, and roast in an air fryer at 400 °F for 10 minutes.
This can be done simultaneously if your air fryer has the space for both.
Remove the potatoes from the heat and add the Greek yogurt, olive oil, and granulated garlic.
Mash the potatoes using a potato masher or a sturdy wire whisk.
Do not over mix the potatoes, or they can become gluey.
Adjust the seasoning with the salt and pepper.
While everything is roasting, prepare the cucumber-tomato salad.
Dice 1/2 of a large cucumber and 1 large tomato.
Combine in a bowl and toss.
To serve, add the mashed potatoes on the bottom, followed by the roasted chickpeas, broccoli, and cucumber-tomato salad.
Top with optional garnishes and enjoy!
recipes.name: Veggie Loaded Mashed Potato Bowl
recipes.recipe_by: Created by Potatoes USA, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Clean out your cupboards with this quick and easy veggie recipe. Use whatever fresh or canned vegetables you have on hand and mix with noodles, sauce, and cheese for dinner tonight.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil water in a cooking pot.
Add the pasta.
Turn down the heat to medium-low; cook according to box directions.
Pour pasta and water into colander to drain.
Add vegetables and spaghetti sauce to cooking pot.
Cook over medium-low heat just until the vegetables are hot.
Return cooked, drained pasta back to cooking pot and mix together.
Sprinkle with cheese just before serving.
recipes.name: Veggie Noodles
recipes.notes: * Fresh or frozen vegetables can be used. Just cook them before tossing with pasta.
recipes.recipe_by: The Power of Choice — USDA Food and Nutrition Service and US Department of Health and Human Services Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Making a veggie omelet has never been so easy! Combine all of your ingredients in a mug, pop it in the microwave, and breakfast is ready!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly grease the inside of a 12-ounce microwave-safe mug.
Use a fork to combine the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in the mug and stir well.
Mix in the vegetables and cheese.
Microwave on HIGH for 45 seconds.
Stir.
Return to the microwave and cook on HIGH until the mixture has puffed and set, 60 to 90 seconds.
The omelet may look wet on the top but it will dry as it cools.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Veggie Omelet in a Mug
recipes.notes: To make a meal, serve with a slice of whole grain toast and fruit.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Don't want to turn on your oven or stove today? This veggie pizza pita is a delicious option that is made in the microwave. Top pizza with your favorite veggies.

ingredients.name: pita
ingredients.note: cut around the sides, into flats

ingredients.name: Pick two from the following vegetables:
ingredients.raw: Pick two from the following vegetables:

ingredients.name: green and red bell peppers
ingredients.raw: green and red bell peppers, sliced

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place one pita round on a plate.
Spread 2 tablespoons of tomato sauce on pizza.
Sprinkle various chopped vegetable over sauce.
Layer one slice of cheese on top of sauce.
Cover with the other half of pita round.
Microwave 35 to 45 seconds, or until cheese melts.
Slice in half, let cool, and enjoy!
recipes.name: Veggie Pizza Pita Pockets
recipes.notes: 1 tablespoon each of broccoli and red onion used for costing and nutrition analysis. Tips:
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from CSAAC (Community Services for Autistic Adults and Children)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish, full of veggies and cheese, is made with whole wheat tortillas. Top with salsa and use whatever veggies you have on hand.

ingredients.name: medium green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium green bell pepper, seeded and chopped

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash vegetables.
Spray pan with cooking oil spray.
